XsOXBiKamY.one_liner: Lower bounds show similarity assumptions cannot close the heterogeneous-homogeneous asynchronous gap; strong interpolation plus local PL can.
XsOXBiKamY.problem: Optimal time complexities for asynchronous parallel optimization are far more pessimistic in the heterogeneous setting than the homogeneous one, and it is unknown whether extra assumptions can close the gap.
XsOXBiKamY.method: Proves impossibility under first- and second-order similarity assumptions for any randomized algorithm, shows weak interpolation alone is insufficient, and introduces strong interpolation plus the local Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition to derive a time-complexity bound matching the homogeneous dependence on worker computation times.
XsOXBiKamY.key_idea: Show via lower bounds that similarity and weak-interpolation assumptions cannot help, then combine strong interpolation with local PL to recover the homogeneous dependence on worker computation times.
XsOXBiKamY.evidence: Theoretical lower and upper bounds only; no experiments are mentioned in the abstract.

86vBQaO1Gs.one_liner: Represents scenes as differentiable primitives in the two-plane 4D ray space, rendering rays by compositing the primitives' responses.
86vBQaO1Gs.problem: Novel view synthesis relies on dense ray databases, and effects such as anti-aliasing, defocus, fisheye, and refraction need specialized machinery in separate frameworks.
86vBQaO1Gs.method: Light Field Primitives (LFP) replace the dense ray database with compact differentiable primitives in the classical two-plane parameterization; each condenses a group of rays into one learned record whose response depends on how closely a query belongs to the group, and a camera ray is rendered by compositing all responses it elicits.
86vBQaO1Gs.key_idea: Place primitives directly in 4D ray space so optical and appearance effects become operations of one shared renderer.
86vBQaO1Gs.evidence: Standard novel view synthesis benchmarks (not listed in the abstract) and extensions to multi-scale anti-aliasing, defocus deblurring with refocusing, fisheye cameras, and refractive novel view synthesis compared with specialized frameworks.
86vBQaO1Gs.claimed_gains: Claims competitive performance on standard benchmarks and parity with specialized frameworks on anti-aliasing, defocus, fisheye, and refraction; no numbers are stated.

PPII4JrkqX.one_liner: Projects LoRA fine-tuning updates onto the orthogonal complement of the text-only activation subspace to suppress VideoLLM text shortcuts.
PPII4JrkqX.problem: Supervised fine-tuning teaches VideoLLMs to answer from textual regularities in the training data, a shortcut that bypasses the video, hides behind in-distribution accuracy gains, and costs SFT the video's gain under distribution shift.
PPII4JrkqX.method: VETO calibrates the subspace that text alone occupies in the base model's activations and projects the fine-tuning update onto its orthogonal complement, so the shortcut is suppressed as it forms without being defined at the data level.
PPII4JrkqX.key_idea: Estimate the text-only activation subspace of the base model and constrain the LoRA update to its orthogonal complement.
PPII4JrkqX.evidence: Seven VideoLLMs on the training distribution and six benchmarks under distribution shift.
PPII4JrkqX.claimed_gains: No numeric gains stated; the abstract says VETO preserves SFT's in-distribution gain across seven VideoLLMs and gains more than SFT on six benchmarks under shift.

iDTOFa9PjK.one_liner: MoETok routes content and detail query tokens of a 1D visual tokenizer through sparsely activated experts.
iDTOFa9PjK.problem: How learnable queries in 1D visual tokenizers gather information is poorly understood, and dense processing does not adapt to the heterogeneous roles they develop (few Content queries for semantics, many Detail queries for fine detail).
iDTOFa9PjK.method: MoETok routes tokens through sparsely activated experts; the router is jointly optimized with reconstruction and semantic objectives and learns role-specialized processing paths adapted to each token's representation.
iDTOFa9PjK.key_idea: A learned sparse router sends Content and Detail query tokens to different experts, specializing computation by token role under matched active computation.
iDTOFa9PjK.evidence: Comparisons with dense tokenizers across model scales and token budgets under matched supervision and active computation, on ImageNet, plus validation at scale in a unified autoregressive model for understanding and generation.
iDTOFa9PjK.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims improved reconstruction, semantic representation and autoregressive generation over dense tokenizers without numbers.

oxLFTvR0i2.one_liner: TACC organizes source views into carrier hierarchies and retrieves tokens within an exact budget by source-target geometric relevance.
oxLFTvR0i2.problem: Feed-forward novel view synthesis relies on global scene-token context that costs substantial memory and latency with dense source views, and target-agnostic compression does not adapt evidence to each target view.
oxLFTvR0i2.method: TACC organizes each source view into a progressive carrier hierarchy and, driven by source-target geometric relevance, adaptively retrieves tokens to allocate exact quotas, yielding a compact target-conditioned representation for feed-forward latent NVS.
oxLFTvR0i2.key_idea: Retrieve tokens from a per-view carrier hierarchy under an exact quota set by source-target geometric relevance, making the compressed context target-conditioned.
oxLFTvR0i2.evidence: Experiments on RE10K under dense input settings with LagerNVS and LVSM, measured by Effective FPS that excludes one-time source encoding and carrier construction.
oxLFTvR0i2.claimed_gains: TACC achieves 9.23x and 64x higher Effective FPS than Full Context on LagerNVS and LVSM, respectively, under dense input settings.

C6FKzgeUB4.one_liner: Applies slow- and fast-decay momentum only along flat curvature directions, with sphere constraints, to accelerate Muon in LLM pretraining.
C6FKzgeUB4.problem: AdamW and Muon rely on gradient normalization, which only weakly mitigates ill-conditioned curvature, so progress along flat (small-eigenvalue) directions that dominates final loss reduction stays slow.
C6FKzgeUB4.method: Adds a multiscale momentum applied only along flat directions, pairing a slow-decay component for noise reduction with a fast-decay component for rapid curvature adaptation. A sphere-constraint technique prevents the parameter inflation and effective learning-rate collapse that a naive combination would cause.
C6FKzgeUB4.key_idea: Multiscale (slow plus fast decay) momentum restricted to flat eigen-directions, stabilized by sphere constraints on the parameters.
C6FKzgeUB4.evidence: Experiments on dense and MoE architectures from 0.12B to 5.1B parameters, plus a theoretical analysis of the acceleration effect and design principles.
C6FKzgeUB4.claimed_gains: Significantly accelerates Muon across dense and MoE architectures and models from 0.12B to 5.1B parameters; no speedup figure is given in the visible abstract.

zYACyuZGP5.one_liner: Traverses weight-space regions of preserved network function using Hessian null space directions to find diverse internal solutions.
zYACyuZGP5.problem: It is unclear how the diverse internal solutions of neural networks are related in weight space, and whether mode-connected regions contain different internal mechanisms.
zYACyuZGP5.method: Hessian Null Space Continuation (HNC) uses local curvature information to traverse regions of weight space that preserve network function, and can be steered toward solutions with specified properties.
zYACyuZGP5.key_idea: Follow the Hessian null space step by step to move through weight space without changing network function, optionally steering toward chosen properties.
zYACyuZGP5.evidence: Applied to RNNs trained on a memory task, ImageNet-trained Vision Transformers, and RL policies, where HNC finds solutions with different representations and dynamics at maintained behavior.

zoEPmDfzVa.one_liner: Zero-shot cross-modal homography estimation that adapts at test time using synthesized prediction-centered training pairs from each test pair.
zoEPmDfzVa.problem: Zero-shot cross-modal homography methods treat each test pair as passive input, and direct reconstruction-based adaptation conflates appearance differences with geometric misalignment.
zoEPmDfzVa.method: TMO synthesizes prediction-centered training pairs with varying source geometries around the current alignment and requires adaptation to stay effective across them. This refines appearance transfer while keeping compatibility with a frozen geometric prior.
zoEPmDfzVa.key_idea: Self-supervise test-time adaptation with synthetic pairs of varied source geometry around the current alignment, so appearance transfer is refined without distorting scene structure.
zoEPmDfzVa.evidence: Six benchmarks, three of which are shared with prior zero-shot work.
zoEPmDfzVa.claimed_gains: Best results before adaptation on the three benchmarks shared with prior zero-shot work, and per-pair adaptation further reduces MACE by 16.9%-50.8% across six benchmarks.

iYQV7xkCPx.one_liner: IntentLoc reframes GUI grounding as intent-level object detection using semantic queries and Crosshair Attention for small targets.
iYQV7xkCPx.problem: VLM-based GUI agents predict coordinates as discrete tokens without explicit spatial supervision, and existing detectors propose GUI-element-like regions but rarely rank the intended one first.
iYQV7xkCPx.method: IntentLoc uses high-level semantic queries to give a detector intent understanding and adds Crosshair Attention to progressively locate small GUI targets; the authors also build Atypical-GUI-Bench for robustness under atypical in-the-wild observations.
iYQV7xkCPx.key_idea: Treat grounding as detection with intent-conditioned semantic queries that rank the intended element first, and refine small targets progressively with Crosshair Attention.
iYQV7xkCPx.evidence: Comparisons with coordinate-prediction baselines under the same backbone and training data on four GUI grounding benchmarks and two model sizes, plus Atypical-GUI-Bench and end-to-end tasks with a VLM planner.
iYQV7xkCPx.claimed_gains: IntentLoc-GUI outperforms pure coordinate prediction baselines by 10.6 points, averaged with equal weight over four GUI grounding benchmarks and two model sizes.

woSV2K2ZBG.one_liner: Long-WAM scales visual context of causal world-action models using autoregressive video pretraining and hardware-specific acceleration for real-time control.
woSV2K2ZBG.problem: Real-time robot control needs long visual history to infer motion and task progress, but processing that history delays action.
woSV2K2ZBG.method: Causal prediction is first learned from robot and egocentric videos without action labels (autoregressive pretraining) and the history-to-future structure is preserved during world-action adaptation; streaming observation encoding, asynchronous execution and hardware-specific acceleration enable deployment on RTX5090, DGX Spark and Jetson AGX Thor.
woSV2K2ZBG.key_idea: Pretrain the video foundation autoregressively so longer history is actually used, then stream observation encoding and run asynchronously to keep action latency low.
woSV2K2ZBG.evidence: RoboCasa GR-1, LIBERO-Long, RoboTwin2.0 and DOMINO experiments with a bidirectionally pretrained initialization as comparison, latency measurements on three platforms, and real-robot deployment on Unitree G1 and YAM.
woSV2K2ZBG.claimed_gains: On RoboCasa GR-1, increasing context from 0.0 to 19.2 seconds raises success from 63.3% to 78.7%; each action chunk takes 107.4 ms on RTX5090, and dynamic cup stacking reaches 95% success.

NyptcfFtqY.one_liner: JCVI regulates cross-view information exchange by utility and removes self-information paths so each view is predicted from the other views.
NyptcfFtqY.problem: Deep multi-view clustering treats cross-view interaction as inherently beneficial, though exchanged information can be unreliable, structurally incompatible, or redundant.
NyptcfFtqY.method: A utility-aware interaction mechanism jointly scores semantic reliability, structural compatibility, and feature complementarity to regulate exchange. For non-triviality, each view gets a target-exclusive supervisory context built only from the remaining views, plus pairwise and neighborhood-level structural constraints.
NyptcfFtqY.key_idea: Build each view's supervisory context only from the other views, removing the direct self-information path, and gate cross-view exchange by reliability, compatibility, and complementarity.
NyptcfFtqY.evidence: Experiments on five benchmark datasets, which are not named in the abstract.

ARmBOrICgf.one_liner: Two-stage aesthetic photo reconstruction: learned atomic-operation planning, then GRPO optimization of plans from realized visual outcomes within a semantic boundary.
ARmBOrICgf.problem: Larger structural edits can raise aesthetic gain but also risk altering subject identity and scene semantics, and existing methods optimize plans only in text space without feedback from realized visual outcomes or support for personalized intents.
ARmBOrICgf.method: Structured Photographic Planning Learning decomposes plans into atomic photographic operations and jointly learns reference-free, reference-guided, and intent-conditioned planning. Feasible-Space Visual Optimization then uses Visual Aesthetic GRPO (VA-GRPO) to execute candidate plans and optimize the planner from realized visual outcomes within the semantic elasticity boundary; the authors also build Harmonia-Bench.
ARmBOrICgf.key_idea: Execute candidate edit plans and train the planner with GRPO on realized visual outcomes, maximizing aesthetic gain within a photo-dependent semantic elasticity boundary.
ARmBOrICgf.evidence: Experiments on the new Harmonia-Bench for default and personalized aesthetic photo reconstruction, compared with AesFormer.
ARmBOrICgf.claimed_gains: Harmonia outperforms AesFormer using only 30% of its (the abstract is cut off after this).

IfWqfjO4eJ.one_liner: Shows exact planning with multi-step transition look-ahead is NP-hard for every fixed discount and gives a randomized polynomial-time approximation scheme.
IfWqfjO4eJ.problem: Prior NP-hardness for multi-step transition look-ahead was shown only with a discount factor near one, leaving open hardness at every discount and efficient near-optimal planning.
IfWqfjO4eJ.method: They prove NP-hardness for every fixed discount factor, give a randomized polynomial-time approximation scheme for every fixed look-ahead depth, and extend the approach to unknown transitions with a learning algorithm.
IfWqfjO4eJ.key_idea: A randomized approximation scheme for each fixed look-ahead depth; the abstract does not describe its underlying mechanism.
IfWqfjO4eJ.evidence: Hardness and approximation proofs, a near-optimal-regret learning result for unknown transitions, and empirical validation on a wind-farm storage-control benchmark from Lu et al.

rIRkUxOleG.one_liner: Training with uniformly sampled stochastic tokenizations makes LLMs robust to non-canonical and adversarial tokenizations without extra inference cost.
rIRkUxOleG.problem: Models trained with a deterministic canonical tokenization can be brittle to adversarially chosen or randomly sampled non-canonical tokenizations of the input.
rIRkUxOleG.method: Analyses how stochastic tokenization during pre-training and supervised fine-tuning, and in-context learning, affects robustness to adversarial and random non-canonical tokenizations.
rIRkUxOleG.key_idea: Sample tokenizations uniformly at random during pre-training or fine-tuning so the model sees non-canonical segmentations of the same text.
rIRkUxOleG.evidence: A systematic study across pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, and in-context learning regimes, over several datasets and model architectures.
rIRkUxOleG.claimed_gains: Uniformly sampled non-canonical tokenizations reduce the accuracy of a canonically trained Llama-1b model by 29.8%, while training with stochastic tokenization preserves accuracy without increasing inference cost.

bReEztZNyv.one_liner: Set transformer that predicts divergence-free kernel coefficients in one forward pass to reconstruct incompressible 3D flows from sparse samples.
bReEztZNyv.problem: Recovering divergence-free velocity fields from sparse, noisy, irregular observations needs physical consistency and robustness, while existing divergence-free kernel methods fit coefficients by a separate optimization per field.
bReEztZNyv.method: DFK-Former is a permutation-invariant set-to-field transformer that predicts the parameters of a divergence-free kernel representation, giving continuous mesh-free fields that are incompressible by construction. It also introduces adaptive and anisotropic divergence-free kernels.
bReEztZNyv.key_idea: Amortize divergence-free kernel fitting with a set transformer that outputs kernel coefficients directly, so incompressibility holds exactly and a learned prior fills in missing data.
bReEztZNyv.evidence: Experiments across varying sparsity, noise and occlusion, including zero-shot transfer (abstract is cut off).

H4nbHHmwDq.one_liner: GuardFlow adds imperceptible perturbations that accumulate along flow-model generation trajectories to disrupt text-guided image editing.
H4nbHHmwDq.problem: Image immunization methods target GAN or diffusion models and do not generalize to flow-based generative editing systems.
H4nbHHmwDq.method: GuardFlow exploits the trajectory-driven nature of flow models, where small perturbations accumulate and alter the generation path. The authors derive a perturbation bound that ensures effective disruption while preserving perceptual quality.
H4nbHHmwDq.key_idea: Craft perturbations that accumulate along the flow trajectory and divert the generation path, with a theoretical bound tying disruption to perceptual quality.
H4nbHHmwDq.evidence: Experiments on major flow-based editing frameworks, comparing effectiveness, visual fidelity and robustness against baselines.
H4nbHHmwDq.claimed_gains: Effectively impedes text-guided editing while keeping high visual fidelity and outperforms existing baselines in effectiveness and robustness; no numbers stated.

DBfaGUZSYV.one_liner: A generative model trained with GRPO co-evolves with an MLLM, synthesizing topic-relevant video features to improve weakly-supervised video highlight detection.
DBfaGUZSYV.problem: Adapting MLLMs to weakly-supervised highlight detection is limited by sparse video-level supervision, SFT struggles with signal scarcity, and semi-supervised methods depend on static, manually curated unlabeled data.
DBfaGUZSYV.method: A generative-adversarial post-training framework pairs the MLLM with a generative model that uses a video synthesis tool. The generator is updated with Group Relative Policy Optimization to produce realistic, topic-relevant training video features that raise the MLLM's discriminative ability.
DBfaGUZSYV.key_idea: Let a GRPO-trained generator keep synthesizing topic-relevant video features that adapt to the MLLM, replacing static unlabeled data with co-evolving synthetic data.
DBfaGUZSYV.evidence: Experiments on three public datasets (abstract cuts off), compared with standard supervised fine-tuning and classical semi-supervised learning.
DBfaGUZSYV.claimed_gains: Significantly outperforms standard SFT and classical semi-supervised learning, with new best results across three public benchmarks (abstract text cuts off); no numbers stated.

uNkwq9SGGA.one_liner: Corrects contrastive RL's missing-survival-mass bias with mass-weighted InfoNCE and a log-survival-mass policy score, using only one-bit failure signals.
uNkwq9SGGA.problem: Under failure termination, CRL builds positives only from pre-failure futures, discarding the occupancy mass absorbed by failure and overestimating goal-reaching values for short surviving futures.
uNkwq9SGGA.method: Mass-weighted InfoNCE corrects the overweighting of short surviving futures in critic learning, and a log-survival-mass score restores the missing mass in policy optimization; the one-bit failure termination signal is the only safety supervision.
uNkwq9SGGA.key_idea: Reweight the contrastive critic loss and add a log-survival-mass term to the policy score to restore the occupancy mass lost to failure.
uNkwq9SGGA.evidence: Twelve failure-prone robot navigation and locomotion tasks compared with Scaling-CRL, plus depth-scaling experiments.
uNkwq9SGGA.claimed_gains: Consistently improves mean survival time and achieves higher mean time at goal than Scaling-CRL, with substantial gains in nine of twelve tasks.

hppVhs94xI.one_liner: Post-trains pretrained single-physics modules on a coupled-system loss, using an implicit-adjoint equilibrium method with constant activation memory.
hppVhs94xI.problem: Modules pretrained on isolated single physics are never optimized for the coupled equilibrium, so interface coupling can amplify their errors.
hppVhs94xI.method: Multiphysics post-training adapts pretrained modules via a system-level loss on their joint predictions while keeping each module's inputs, outputs and exchange structure unchanged. It is implemented as Finite Unrolling (Unrolled-K) for low latency and Equilibrium Post-Training (EquiPT) with an implicit adjoint.
hppVhs94xI.key_idea: Train assembled physics modules at the coupled equilibrium through an implicit adjoint while keeping physical interfaces, instead of assembling frozen single-physics modules.
hppVhs94xI.evidence: Module-to-system error bounds plus neutron-thermal, reaction-diffusion and fluid-structure interaction benchmarks.
hppVhs94xI.claimed_gains: EquiPT reduces system error by 50.2% to 96.1% over frozen assembly.

bXlg7np7XS.one_liner: Distills individual adversarial attacks into universal perturbations by using individual adversarial examples as representation-level supervision.
bXlg7np7XS.problem: Individual adversarial perturbation methods have advanced rapidly while universal perturbation methods lag, since adapting methods to the universal setting is often nontrivial.
bXlg7np7XS.method: UPD is a domain-decoupled formulation that learns universal adversarial perturbations from off-the-shelf individual-attack methods by treating individual adversarial examples as representation-level supervision. It is instantiated for LLM jailbreak and image classification.
bXlg7np7XS.key_idea: Use individual adversarial examples as representation-level targets to train a single input-agnostic perturbation.
bXlg7np7XS.evidence: Two instantiations, LLM jailbreak and image classification, including robust image models.
bXlg7np7XS.claimed_gains: not stated (abstract reports matching or exceeding prior best results, with large gains on robust models, without numbers).

MsjbTKyHl5.one_liner: Visual-memory framework for unified multimodal models enabling long-horizon interleaved text-image generation with character and scene consistency.
MsjbTKyHl5.problem: Generated images accumulate in context over long trajectories, so imperfect or irrelevant visual states interfere with future synthesis while earlier characters and scenes must still be recovered.
MsjbTKyHl5.method: The authors build a large unified multimodal model natively trained on interleaved data and add a visual-memory framework that keeps persistent visual references, selectively retrieves scene-relevant historical states while preserving the full semantic history, and uses few-step self-rollout to adapt to imperfect generated histories. They also introduce LongMIG-Bench for long-horizon text-to-multi-image and image-to-multi-image generation.
MsjbTKyHl5.key_idea: Keep persistent visual references and retrieve only scene-relevant past images, while self-rollout training adapts the model to its own imperfect histories.
MsjbTKyHl5.evidence: Evaluation on LongMIG-Bench for long-horizon text-to-multi-image and image-to-multi-image generation; baselines and numbers are not stated in the abstract.

9IBmFgLm6f.one_liner: Coordinate-only first-layer weight and bias initialization that enriches initial features of ReLU MLP implicit neural representations.
9IBmFgLm6f.problem: Default-initialized ReLU MLPs recover fine detail poorly because of Inlet Rank Collapse: first-layer features gain no corresponding increase in effective representation dimensionality.
9IBmFgLm6f.method: Geometric Initialization constructs first-layer weights and biases from coordinates only, enriching the initial feature representation while keeping the ReLU architecture and training procedure; the paper also frames positional encoding, sinusoidal activations, and batch normalization as remedies for the same bottleneck.
9IBmFgLm6f.key_idea: Set first-layer weights and biases from coordinate geometry so initial features span more effective dimensions, targeting Inlet Rank Collapse.
9IBmFgLm6f.evidence: Image reconstruction experiments showing improved reconstruction and greater benefit from increasing network width (details cut off in the provided abstract).

GCPq7IYXcc.one_liner: Jointly trains a VLA on robot demonstrations and noisy egocentric human data with reliability-aware action learning and future-representation distillation.
GCPq7IYXcc.problem: Egocentric videos broaden task coverage, but motion reconstruction and retargeting produce noisy action labels, while clean robot demonstrations are costly to collect.
GCPq7IYXcc.method: EgoForesight couples future visual representation prediction with action generation in a joint vision-action flow. Reliability-conditioned corruption and reliability-weighted regression down-weight unreliable sources, and privileged-future distillation has an EMA teacher that sees the clean future supervise an earlier student layer receiving a corrupted future.
GCPq7IYXcc.key_idea: Allocate action supervision across noise levels by source reliability, and distill deeper representations of clean-future scene change from an EMA teacher into a student seeing a corrupted future.
GCPq7IYXcc.evidence: not stated (the abstract is cut off before experiments; keywords indicate vision-language-action models and dexterous manipulation).

0HdmOTvGef.one_liner: Aligns world action models for safer manipulation by probing imagined futures and applying monotonic DiffusionNFT-based safety updates.
0HdmOTvGef.problem: Safety approaches for world action models depend on predefined specifications and costly environment interaction, limiting safety coverage and making risk discovery expensive.
0HdmOTvGef.method: ForeAlign iteratively probes imagined futures and feeds safety feedback into policy updates, unifying safety requirements under a general safety distribution and extending DiffusionNFT into a monotonic improvement operator with bounded policy shift. It splits the WAM into an action policy and an independent action-conditioned world model to counter alignment faking.
0HdmOTvGef.key_idea: Self-align by scoring imagined futures from a separately parameterized world model, and update the action policy with a bounded-shift DiffusionNFT operator.
0HdmOTvGef.evidence: Simulated and real-world embodied manipulation benchmarks, with a theoretical bound on policy shift.
0HdmOTvGef.claimed_gains: Improves safe rate by 35.6% and task success rate by 24.6% on average.

VMbjRpsgGH.one_liner: A 16B autoregressive diffusion streaming video editor distilled to two steps with source-attention-adaptive teacher guidance.
VMbjRpsgGH.problem: Streaming video editors over-rely on historical frames even as errors accumulate in the generation history, which the authors call ruminative behavior.
VMbjRpsgGH.method: Resilient-DMD strengthens teacher-side source guidance during distillation when relative source attention falls below matched baselines, giving a two-step generator; Long-Horizon Autoregressive Distillation extends this to deeper rollout states with bounded activation memory. The engine uses bounded transformer state, single-frame VAE state handoff and asynchronous execution.
VMbjRpsgGH.key_idea: During distillation, boost teacher source guidance exactly where the student's relative attention to the source falls below matched baselines.
VMbjRpsgGH.evidence: Automatic and human evaluations on the authors' LongV2VBench of one-minute videos, against streaming baselines and offline editors.
VMbjRpsgGH.claimed_gains: End-to-end 720p editing at 34.87 FPS on a single B200 GPU; outperforms the evaluated streaming baselines and stays competitive with strong offline editors.

KocKRsXx7y.one_liner: Rank-K separable hypergraph convolution with geometry-dependent mixing reaches the expressive limit of sequence-geometry binding in proteins.
KocKRsXx7y.problem: Additive message passing is provably blind to content-geometry binding between a residue's sequence identity and its 3D position in protein structure models.
KocKRsXx7y.method: Characterizes the full class of single-layer bilinear content-geometry messages, then builds Hyper-Fold, where each radius neighborhood forms a sequence hyperedge and a contact hyperedge modulated by an edge-conditioned matrix-valued operator factored into K learned basis operators with geometry-generated coefficients. Variants are the hierarchical Hyper-Fold-Deep and Hyper-Fold-Pocket, an anchored set-prediction head for binding sites.
KocKRsXx7y.key_idea: Factor an edge-conditioned matrix-valued operator into K learned basis operators with geometry-generated coefficients over sequence and contact hyperedges to capture content-geometry binding.
KocKRsXx7y.evidence: Enzyme function prediction, fold classification, and ligand binding site detection (UniSite-DS and two zero-shot benchmarks), with controlled operator, backbone, and detection-head comparisons.
KocKRsXx7y.claimed_gains: Hyper-Fold and Hyper-Fold-Deep give the best results among protein-specific structure encoders; Hyper-Fold-Pocket surpasses UniSite-3D with no sequence language model features, 68x fewer parameters, and 4.8x lower latency.

UkH0vfqnDF.one_liner: Applies rotation then token-wise scaling to counter token norm imbalance in 2-bit KV cache quantization across X-LLMs.
UkH0vfqnDF.problem: Per-channel KV cache quantization loses fidelity at extreme compression because shared quantization parameters span token groups with large norm disparities (Token Norm Imbalance).
UkH0vfqnDF.method: OScaR (Omni-Scaled Canalized Rotation) applies Canalized Rotation followed by Omni-Token Scaling to reduce sequence-dimension variance caused by Token Norm Imbalance, with an optimized system design. It targets text-only, multimodal, and omni-modal LLMs without intricate quantization pipelines.
UkH0vfqnDF.key_idea: Identify token norm imbalance as the main error source and cancel it with a rotation plus per-token scaling on top of per-channel quantization.
UkH0vfqnDF.evidence: Empirical and theoretical analysis of per-channel quantization limits; per the TL;DR, accurate 2-bit KV cache quantization across text-only, multimodal, and omni-modal models. Experimental details are cut off in the abstract.

IX1ZrBT183.one_liner: Alchemy3D provides a 1.25M-asset 3D editing dataset, flow-based editing models, and the GEdit3D-Bench benchmark.
IX1ZrBT183.problem: Controllable 3D asset editing is held back by scarce training data, insufficient source-aware modeling, and missing practical evaluation protocols.
IX1ZrBT183.method: Curates Alchemy3D-1M (1.25M assets, 1.38M editing pairs, seven editing types), trains a family of generative flow models for image- and text-conditioned editing with few-step inference and transfer to multi-view 3D part segmentation, and introduces the open-world GEdit3D-Bench with a multi-dimensional protocol.
IX1ZrBT183.key_idea: Train flow-based 3D editors at scale on a million-pair dataset spanning seven editing types, evaluated on an open-world multi-dimensional benchmark.
IX1ZrBT183.evidence: Comparison with prior methods on existing and newly introduced benchmarks for editing fidelity, source preservation, and visual quality.
IX1ZrBT183.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative claim only: outperforms prior methods on most metrics of editing fidelity, source preservation, and visual quality)

1caM4AChuR.one_liner: Trains CLIP with graded-coverage captions so similarity rises with the amount of visible semantic content a caption covers.
1caM4AChuR.problem: CLIP objectives treat all semantically correct captions as equally valid, so models do not score captions with more semantic coverage higher.
1caM4AChuR.method: Introduces CoverageBench (1,300 Visual Genome images, each with four captions of increasing coverage that should satisfy s(I,C1) < s(I,C2) < s(I,C3) < s(I,C4)) and CoverCLIP, a coverage-aware training framework with three components. The first is the Coverage-1M dataset (710K graded-coverage, 228K long-short, and 76K highly descriptive caption samples); the other components are cut off in the abstract.
1caM4AChuR.key_idea: Supervise CLIP with captions of explicitly graded semantic coverage, mixed with general vision-language training to preserve general performance.
1caM4AChuR.evidence: Evaluation on the manually verified CoverageBench, where existing CLIP models are reported to struggle to rank captions consistently by coverage.

Auhy9UCA8h.one_liner: Gives each action part its own critic; slow parts commit for the full chunk, fast parts re-plan halfway.
Auhy9UCA8h.problem: Q-chunking commits every joint to the same chunk although robot parts act on different time scales, and letting some joints re-plan mid-chunk breaks value learning because a full-chunk critic scores actions never executed.
Auhy9UCA8h.method: FQC commits a slow part of the action for the full chunk and re-plans a fast part halfway through. Each part gets its own critic scoring exactly the actions that part executes, and actions are selected by ranking candidates with these critics.
Auhy9UCA8h.key_idea: Factor the chunk critic into per-part critics that score only executed actions, then select actions by ranking candidates with them.
Auhy9UCA8h.evidence: Online fine-tuning on DexJoCo (arm and hand) and BiGym (base and two arms) against a single critic ranking the same candidates, plus validation on a real humanoid robot.
Auhy9UCA8h.claimed_gains: Against a single critic ranking the same candidates, pooled success on DexJoCo rises from 0.231 to 0.327, and FQC is on par on BiGym (0.440 and 0.480).

WcveyOpJGj.one_liner: V-JEPA pretraining that injects ego motion into a few registers used as the only context for masked patch prediction.
WcveyOpJGj.problem: Driving world models inherit dense features from pretrained visual encoders that are not suited to motion-conditioned world modeling and planning, and dense grids make future prediction costlier as resolution increases.
WcveyOpJGj.method: MORE injects temporally aligned ego motion into a small set of registers used as the sole context for masked patch prediction, with a blockwise register-masking objective. Downstream, the register space defines the future states the world model predicts and provides shared scene memory for trajectory (abstract truncated).
WcveyOpJGj.key_idea: Channel dense patch-level supervision through a small bottleneck of ego-motion-conditioned registers learned during video pretraining as the world-state interface.
WcveyOpJGj.evidence: The visible abstract describes pretraining and downstream design but no datasets or results.

HwUWVjQkXp.one_liner: Estimates per-view gaze targets from uncalibrated multi-view images using a shared estimated 3D coordinate frame.
HwUWVjQkXp.problem: Gaze target estimation is limited by camera field of view, and prior multi-view attempts need fixed camera setups or explicit bounding boxes.
HwUWVjQkXp.method: GazeWorld builds a unified 3D-aware representation of scene geometry and semantics from pre-trained geometry priors, associates subjects through prompts, and predicts per-view gaze targets in a shared estimated 3D frame for a variable number of uncalibrated views. It is trained on a dataset of over 260K verified multi-view GTE groups curated from Ego-Exo4D.
HwUWVjQkXp.key_idea: Predict gaze targets from features expressed in a shared 3D frame estimated by pre-trained geometry priors, so uncalibrated views of any number resolve each other's ambiguities.
HwUWVjQkXp.evidence: Experiments on multiple benchmarks in single-view and multi-view settings, including a self-collected out-of-domain handheld benchmark with head-invisible cases.
HwUWVjQkXp.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative claim only: strong performance on multiple benchmarks and consistent gains as input views increase)

VA0yCrShah.one_liner: Agent builds a temporal memory tree while answering questions, refining detail at a higher frame rate on key intervals.
VA0yCrShah.problem: Build-then-reason video memory pipelines are costly for the whole video when few questions are asked and never update memory with what is learned from answered questions.
VA0yCrShah.method: Sprout watches the video segment by segment at a low frame rate until the current question can be answered, records each segment as a coarse tree node, and revisits key intervals at a higher frame rate to refine nodes. Recorded segments' video input is dropped from history while the video stays reachable through tools, and the tree and prior question-answer records persist across questions.
VA0yCrShah.key_idea: Grow a persistent temporal memory tree online from the first question, adding detail nodes only where questions require them, instead of building memory offline.
VA0yCrShah.evidence: The abstract is truncated before any experimental results; no datasets or baselines are visible.

PAKyCRDWkv.one_liner: Benchmark of 342 interactive tasks measuring whether multimodal agents learn in-context from action-annotated video demonstrations.
PAKyCRDWkv.problem: Multimodal in-context learning from video demonstrations in interactive environments is underexplored, and agents must turn demonstrations into executable policies grounded in new visual states.
PAKyCRDWkv.method: V-ICAL has 342 interactive tasks across 37 environments, using human-curated demonstration videos with action annotations as exemplars and evaluating agents through sustained interaction from a target initialization, covering state grounding, temporal memory, planning, and adaptation.
PAKyCRDWkv.key_idea: Test in-context learning by giving agents human-curated, action-annotated demonstration videos and scoring sustained interaction from a target initialization.
PAKyCRDWkv.evidence: Evaluation of 19 multimodal agents against a human baseline, with controlled comparisons (details cut off in the abstract).
PAKyCRDWkv.claimed_gains: The best model, Seed-2.1-Pro, scores only 54.4/100 and other leading models fail to surpass 50, against a human baseline of 83.6.

dORf1tVq6C.one_liner: Action head predicting a median and positive gaps that form ordered action quantiles in one forward pass.
dORf1tVq6C.problem: VLA action heads have limits: point regression gives only a point estimate of the action distribution, and flow-matching samplers need costly iterative sampling.
dORf1tVq6C.method: Unifies regression and flow matching under a shared objective, extends it to a quantile objective, and designs the Quantile Head to predict a median plus positive gaps that give ordered marginal action quantiles. The quantiles support multiple sampling strategies without retraining and are jointly supervised to train the default median policy.
dORf1tVq6C.key_idea: Predict a median and positive gaps for ordered marginal action quantiles, and supervise all quantiles jointly so the median policy is trained with lower-variance updates.
dORf1tVq6C.evidence: A local analysis of joint supervision under stated conditions, plus experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, LIBERO-Pro, and two real-robot tasks.
dORf1tVq6C.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative claim only: highest average success rates among compared methods and the shortest mean episode time among matched LIBERO baselines)

WtGCxYPpvD.one_liner: Multimodal benchmark of real and synthesized damage-evidence images for detecting AI-generated fraudulent refund claims.
WtGCxYPpvD.problem: AI-generated images can fabricate refund evidence, but existing detection benchmarks test standalone authenticity, cross-generator transfer, or localization rather than claim-conditioned fraudulent evidence.
WtGCxYPpvD.method: Built from real user-review evidence across e-commerce, food delivery, and travel services: genuine damaged and undamaged images are identified by MLLM-assisted filtering and human annotation, and fake-damaged images are synthesized from genuine undamaged references using 12 image editing and generation models.
WtGCxYPpvD.key_idea: Synthesize fake-damaged evidence from genuine undamaged review images with 12 editing and generation models to test claim-conditioned fraud detection.
WtGCxYPpvD.evidence: Evaluates MLLMs, specialized AI-generated image detectors, and human evaluators on the same evaluation images.

oAvDFiXQMu.one_liner: Benchmark for MLLMs writing parametric 3D programs from text, image, or assembly specifications, scored on geometry and structure.
oAvDFiXQMu.problem: Existing benchmarks rarely evaluate 3D modeling through code, which requires geometrically precise, semantically aligned, assembly-consistent programs.
oAvDFiXQMu.method: Three task families (Text-to-3D, Image-to-3D, Assembly-3D) are scored for executability, geometric fidelity, topology, text-grounded constraints, multiview semantic alignment, and part-level structure, using P3D-Dataset with 400 text cases, 400 image cases, and 203 annotated assemblies.
oAvDFiXQMu.key_idea: Score generated parametric 3D programs, which expose dimensions, operations, and part relations, on structure as well as appearance.
oAvDFiXQMu.evidence: Evaluation on 100 cases from each task family, finding multi-part generation substantially harder than single-part modeling.

r7zfsysr22.one_liner: Training augmentations (wrist-view perturbations, enriched captions, relabeled failed segments) that break modality shortcuts in VLA policies.
r7zfsysr22.problem: VLA policies can succeed while exploiting modality shortcuts, where visual, lexical, or motor cues predict expert actions without the task evidence that should determine them, and more demonstrations of the same kind leave shortcuts intact.
r7zfsysr22.method: PerturBot applies task-preserving wrist-view perturbations, enriches instructions with decision-relevant captions, and adds random and failed trajectory segments relabeled with the behavior they contain, leaving inference unchanged. It also proposes GroundingFscore, an offline score of how much a policy relies on modality shortcuts.
r7zfsysr22.key_idea: Make task evidence easier to use and shortcuts insufficient on their own, via perturbation, caption enrichment, and relabeled failure data during training.
r7zfsysr22.evidence: The visible abstract does not state benchmarks or results.

xBman3qpTm.one_liner: Two-stage training-free anomaly generation: region exploration, then detector feedback propagated along the full diffusion trajectory.
xBman3qpTm.problem: Training-free anomaly generation struggles with spatial control over fine-grained candidate regions and evaluates anomalies only after generation, so insufficiently formed anomalies cannot be corrected.
xBman3qpTm.method: Stage one, Anomaly Specific Region Exploration (ASRE), builds fine-grained candidate anomaly formation regions. Stage two uses terminal detection results as primary feedback and propagates it through the full diffusion trajectory (rest of the description is cut off).
xBman3qpTm.key_idea: Turn anomaly detection from post-generation evaluation into terminal feedback that optimizes the whole diffusion trajectory.
xBman3qpTm.evidence: The visible abstract describes the method but no datasets or results.

U6PHmThVsO.one_liner: Trains a policy that decides when, which, and whether to reuse test-time training procedures exposed as callable tools.
U6PHmThVsO.problem: TTT helps only in some settings, and applying an ill-suited TTT method wastes compute or hurts the model, so deciding when and how to use it requires agency.
U6PHmThVsO.method: Agentic-TTT turns TTT procedures into callable tools, treats accumulated skills as an evolving deployment environment, and trains a test-time policy on observed utility gains to decide whether to use TTT, which algorithm to invoke, and whether to reuse an existing skill.
U6PHmThVsO.key_idea: Learn a policy over TTT tools and accumulated skills, rewarded by the utility gain each decision produces.
U6PHmThVsO.evidence: Evaluated on the authors' own benchmark, including domains unseen during training.
U6PHmThVsO.claimed_gains: Nearly doubles utility over the backbone model on the authors' benchmark, learns to trade off utility against compute, and generalizes to unseen domains.

fzzOQGDNIJ.one_liner: Reconstructs both hands from shared full-frame scene-geometry features, without a hand detector, giving world-frame 4D trajectories without separate SLAM.
fzzOQGDNIJ.problem: Articulation-centric pipelines crop hands, use weak-perspective wrist translation, and rely on external SLAM, so they never represent hands relative to the scene, which could help resolve depth and occlusion.
fzzOQGDNIJ.method: G4D-Hand grounds hand prediction in a geometric representation: it reconstructs both hands from shared full-frame features, jointly recovering articulation and metric wrist translation in a common camera frame. Inter-hand and temporal supervision encourage consistent relative positioning and coherent motion, and the same backbone estimates camera motion to lift predictions into the world frame.
fzzOQGDNIJ.key_idea: Predict hands from full-frame scene-reconstruction features, with the same backbone also estimating camera motion for world-frame placement.
fzzOQGDNIJ.evidence: Egocentric benchmarks, including ARCTIC, a dataset with frequent hand occlusions (rest of abstract truncated).
fzzOQGDNIJ.claimed_gains: Runs at 30+ FPS for camera-frame prediction, matches the best prior articulation accuracy, and substantially improves localization on egocentric benchmarks.

mU0g4UJ3TC.one_liner: Reuses upstream agents' KV cache across LoRA adapters, recomputing only tokens flagged by attention concentration.
mU0g4UJ3TC.problem: In multi-LoRA agent pipelines, each downstream agent re-prefills the long upstream context from scratch, causing heavy compute and latency.
mU0g4UJ3TC.method: MuLA selectively recomputes a small subset of critical token positions when switching LoRA adapters, using attention-concentration signals from the upstream agent's forward pass to predict where KV deviations occur, instead of a full re-prefill.
mU0g4UJ3TC.key_idea: Attention concentration in the upstream forward pass predicts the sparse, deep-layer tokens whose KV cache deviates after a LoRA switch, so only those are recomputed.
mU0g4UJ3TC.evidence: Empirical analysis showing LoRA-switch-induced KV-cache deviations are sparse over tokens and delayed to deep layers; experimental results are cut off in the abstract.

ynF3LBCKj9.one_liner: Benchmark measuring coding agents' success when starting from a predecessor's failed-but-reported-complete work.
ynF3LBCKj9.problem: SWE benchmarks start agents from clean states, but in practice agents continue earlier work reported as complete, with no indication of what remains wrong.
ynF3LBCKj9.method: SWE-Residual contains 198 Residual States from 111 tasks in DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench, each being the state a predecessor agent left after submitting as complete while hidden tests still fail. The agent receives only the original request and the state, without the predecessor's trajectory or any failure signal.
ynF3LBCKj9.key_idea: Hold the request and hidden tests fixed and vary only the starting state to isolate Starting-State Robustness.
ynF3LBCKj9.evidence: Five frontier agents evaluated on DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench residual states against the source benchmarks' clean starts.
ynF3LBCKj9.claimed_gains: Success drops by 20.6-53.5 percentage points on DeepSWE and 20.6-34.9 points on Terminal-Bench across the five agents.

g2Uj82aU84.one_liner: Diagnoses late-stage robustness decline in masked-image pretraining and counters it with cross-perturbation self-distillation and low-rank projection.
g2Uj82aU84.problem: Prolonged generative SSL pretraining improves in-distribution accuracy while performance on style-sensitive shifts such as ImageNet-Sketch and an ImageNet-R subset peaks earlier and then declines.
g2Uj82aU84.method: HyGDL combines cross-perturbation self-distillation, low-rank geometric projection, and residual-conditioned reconstruction, following an invariance-aligned principle: pair input nuisance variation with supervision that makes nuisance-dependent features unreliable for the pretraining objective.
g2Uj82aU84.key_idea: Make nuisance-dependent features useless for minimizing the pretraining objective by combining perturbation-paired self-distillation, low-rank projection, and residual-conditioned reconstruction.
g2Uj82aU84.evidence: Tracks frozen representations through prolonged masked-image pretraining and evaluates on unsupervised domain generalization benchmarks.
g2Uj82aU84.claimed_gains: not stated (abstract is cut off at 'HyGDL improves robustness')

9ZT4TUPvto.one_liner: Inverts healthy repo environments into degraded Docker states with issues and verifiers, producing executable CLI repair tasks for training.
9ZT4TUPvto.problem: CLI agents must repair dependencies, permissions, system files, runtime configurations, and code, but executable training data for these interactions is scarce.
9ZT4TUPvto.method: An inversion agent starts from healthy unit-test-verified repository environments, builds counterfactual degraded states summarized as reproducible Dockerfiles, and pairs failures with natural-language issues and executable verifiers. A repair model's solved trajectories are filtered for shortcuts and length and used for supervised fine-tuning.
9ZT4TUPvto.key_idea: Generate repair tasks by having an agent break healthy environments under execution feedback, so each task ships with a reproducible Dockerfile and verifier.
9ZT4TUPvto.evidence: 4,066 inversion prompts yield 1,655 verified tasks; 291 filtered trajectories fine-tune Qwen3 agents evaluated on Terminal-Bench 1.0 and 2.0 under OpenHands, with a three-expert audit of the task collection.
9ZT4TUPvto.claimed_gains: Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct improves by 21.1 points to 46.1% pass@1 on Terminal-Bench 1.0 and by 12.9 points to 31.0% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, with consistent gains at the 32B scale.

tzIvYcn2CX.one_liner: Diffusion HOI generator conditioned on a reference image through interaction-state tokens and per-frame image-patch queries.
tzIvYcn2CX.problem: Text, object geometry, and waypoints leave grasps, approach directions, poses, contacts, and layouts of human-object interaction ambiguous, and a single global image representation conflates cues and conditions every frame identically.
tzIvYcn2CX.method: IMAGIN-4D uses supervised interaction-state tokens encoding body pose, object pose, contact, and spatial relations at the depicted frame, plus frame-aware tokens that query image patches per generated frame. Text, waypoints, and state tokens use separate AdaLN streams while motion tokens cross-attend to frame-aware visual tokens.
tzIvYcn2CX.key_idea: Split image conditioning into spatial interaction-state tokens and frame-aware tokens that retrieve per-frame visual cues, with role-aware separate conditioning streams.
tzIvYcn2CX.evidence: Experiments on FullBodyManipulation (FBM, with synthetic rendered reference images) and BEHAVE, using a new image-adherence metric.

SLtC8DSTo6.one_liner: Shows optimal data reuse in nonstationary RL balances statistical uncertainty against staleness, with minimax-optimal freshness-guided algorithms.
SLtC8DSTo6.problem: Existing nonstationary-RL models measure the cumulative magnitude of change, which does not capture dynamics that evolve through stochastic changes that may accumulate, cancel, or revert.
SLtC8DSTo6.method: Introduces diffusive distribution shift and an information freshness principle that gives an explicit restart scale and predicts the regret cost of tracking changing dynamics, then develops optimistic model-based RL algorithms for known and unknown diffusion rates.
SLtC8DSTo6.key_idea: Restart data reuse at a scale set by balancing statistical uncertainty against mismatch from diffusive drift in the dynamics.
SLtC8DSTo6.evidence: Matching upper and lower regret bounds up to logarithmic factors, with controlled experiments on the freshness mechanism and a wind-storage study.
SLtC8DSTo6.claimed_gains: not stated (theoretical claim: matching regret bounds up to log factors, and the adaptive algorithm matches the upper bound of the one tuned with the true diffusion rate)

7hDncLPVFk.one_liner: Proves a softmax gauge changes trace-NTK diagnostics without changing predictions, and uses the class-quotient NTK to remove the ambiguity.
7hDncLPVFk.problem: Training-free NAS proxies read spectral summaries off the empirical tangent kernel as architecture properties, but for softmax classifiers these are not identifiable.
7hDncLPVFk.method: Proves a function- and training-preserving softmax gauge z -> z + gamma h(x) 1_C injects arbitrary PSD contamination into the trace NTK while leaving softmax, loss, gradient, and training trajectory unchanged, then audits whole NAS search spaces. The class-quotient NTK is exactly invariant under the gauge.
7hDncLPVFk.key_idea: A softmax gauge shifts logits by a class-constant term, which alters the trace NTK but no prediction, so the class-quotient kernel is the invariant object.
7hDncLPVFk.evidence: Audits of all 15,625 NAS-Bench-201 cells and the 4,096-cell TransNAS-Bench-101 micro space.
7hDncLPVFk.claimed_gains: Editing one weight matrix leaves a spoofed top-10 shortlist holding 2 of its 10 architectures, and an adversary choosing the gauge strength per candidate forces selection of a network 34.6 accuracy points worse than the proxy's choice while predictions, loss, and gradients are preserved to 10^-3 in float32.

tizPMPrU1N.one_liner: Force-conditioned interactive video world model combining latent force encoding, force-response attribution, and physics-aware RL.
tizPMPrU1N.problem: Forces encoded as motion trajectories bring inappropriate motion priors, internal representations do not localize force-induced state changes, and limited force-annotated data hurts physical consistency in unseen scenes.
tizPMPrU1N.method: A two-stage framework: supervised fine-tuning with a Latent Force Intervention Encoder (maps force location, direction, and magnitude into the video latent space without exposing future motion) and a Physics Attribution Network (links forces to localized latent changes), then Physics-Aware Reinforcement Learning with self-supervised rewards on out-of-distribution videos.
tizPMPrU1N.key_idea: Encode force into the video latent space without future motion, attribute it to localized latent changes, and refine physical consistency with self-supervised RL rewards.
tizPMPrU1N.evidence: The visible abstract lists no benchmarks or results.
tizPMPrU1N.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative claim only: improved force controllability, physical consistency, and generalization to unseen scenes)

ASO6vhdAgh.one_liner: Product poster generation with pixel-space fidelity supervision in training and energy-guided velocity correction toward the reference at inference.
ASO6vhdAgh.problem: Generated posters distort a reference product's packaging text, textures, and colors, since VAE reconstruction degrades fine detail and sampling lacks explicit fidelity guidance.
ASO6vhdAgh.method: Pixel-Space Fidelity Activation (PFA) directly supervises decoded product regions during training. Energy-Guided Velocity Correction (EVC) measures inconsistent and missing details against the reference with a bidirectional correspondence energy and corrects the sampling velocity with its gradients, without product masks at inference.
ASO6vhdAgh.key_idea: Supervise decoded product pixels in training and correct the sampling velocity with gradients of a bidirectional correspondence energy against the reference.
ASO6vhdAgh.evidence: Builds FidPoster14K (14K product-poster pairs) and FidPoster-Bench (1,000 samples, including an 800-sample Fine-grained Fidelity setting); result details are cut off in the abstract.

OzqGoBnb4I.one_liner: Feed-forward reference-guided image completion that reprojects references with predicted poses and depths into merged and per-reference warps.
OzqGoBnb4I.problem: Reference-guided image completion methods require per-scene optimization, pairwise alignment, or a fixed number of reference images.
OzqGoBnb4I.method: WEAVE reprojects each reference into the target view using camera poses and depths from a frozen geometry model, forming a merged query warp (Q-Warp) and separate reference warps (R-Warps) that keep view-specific details and disagreements, then combines them with the original references to synthesize the missing content.
OzqGoBnb4I.key_idea: Provide both a merged target-aligned warp and separate per-reference warps so the model can resolve cross-view discrepancies that merging discards.
OzqGoBnb4I.evidence: Experiments on MegaDepth and RealBench with MM-DiT and U-Net backbones.
OzqGoBnb4I.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative claim only: consistent improvements on both benchmarks and outperforming scene-finetuned methods on RealBench without test-time optimization)

Qy0XBmxjyW.one_liner: Fast-Slow Training co-evolves optimized context as fast weights and model parameters as slow weights during RL.
Qy0XBmxjyW.problem: Updating LLM parameters via RL forces absorption of task-specific information, causing catastrophic forgetting and loss of plasticity, while prompt optimization alone cannot match RL gains.
Qy0XBmxjyW.method: FST treats model parameters as slow weights and optimized context as fast weights that learn from textual feedback, so slow weights stay closer to the base model while the context absorbs task-specific information.
Qy0XBmxjyW.key_idea: Co-evolve an optimized prompt (fast weights, learning from textual feedback) with policy parameters (slow weights) during RL.
Qy0XBmxjyW.evidence: Reasoning tasks compared against RL alone, with measurements of KL drift from the base model, catastrophic forgetting, and adaptation to a subsequent task.
Qy0XBmxjyW.claimed_gains: Up to 3x more sample-efficient than RL alone across reasoning tasks while reaching a higher performance asymptote, and up to 70% less KL divergence from the base LLM.

VtI8Fimfzu.one_liner: Diffusion mesh generator that encodes faces into latents and uses a Point Sink Flow model to supply face-center positions.
VtI8Fimfzu.problem: Discrete mesh topology is hard for continuous diffusion, and sorting cannot resolve the assignment ambiguity from variable cardinality and non-uniform spatial distribution of face latents.
VtI8Fimfzu.method: A Face VAE encodes mesh faces into compact latents and decodes complete mesh sequences in one step. A Point Sink Flow model transports a dense noisy point cloud into a sparse set of face centers, which are injected into the Face DiT as positional embeddings to fix correspondences between noisy and target latents.
VtI8Fimfzu.key_idea: Transport a noisy point cloud to face centers with a sink flow, and use those centers as positional embeddings so each noisy latent maps to a specific target face latent.
VtI8Fimfzu.evidence: The visible abstract is truncated before experiments; no datasets or results are shown.

liW6AQ3OqV.one_liner: Contrasts teacher-student gaps under correct and wrong hints to cancel privilege-induced style drift in on-policy self-distillation.
liW6AQ3OqV.problem: On-policy self-distillation with privileged context concentrates its distributional gap on style tokens, because the hinted model gives shorter, more direct outputs, which destabilizes training and shortens responses.
liW6AQ3OqV.method: RLCSD contrasts the teacher-student gap under a correct hint against that under a wrong hint, suppressing hint-induced style shifts regardless of correctness so the signal concentrates on task-bearing tokens. It also plugs into existing OPSD methods.
liW6AQ3OqV.key_idea: Contrast the correct-hint teacher-student gap against the wrong-hint gap so style-driven signal cancels and task-bearing tokens remain.
liW6AQ3OqV.evidence: Qwen3 (1.7B/4B/8B) and Olmo-3-7B-Think on mathematical and logical reasoning versus GRPO and prior OPSD methods, plus additional agentic-task results.
liW6AQ3OqV.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative claim only: consistently outperforms GRPO and prior OPSD methods)

XrI3GMlI64.one_liner: Represents Encoder and GNN updates through a shared low-dimensional latent state for federated multimodal graph foundation model adaptation.
XrI3GMlI64.problem: Federated GFM adaptation updates only graph-side modules and freezes the multimodal Encoder, although Encoder and GNN adaptations depend on each other and are sensitive to pairing.
XrI3GMlI64.method: FedCORE represents Encoder and GNN updates through a shared low-dimensional latent state (the core), optimizes it jointly from multimodal and structural signals, and performs federated evolution directly in that state space.
XrI3GMlI64.key_idea: Couple perception and reasoning adaptation by federating a shared low-dimensional core state instead of separate Encoder and GNN parameters.
XrI3GMlI64.evidence: Empirical studies of Encoder-GNN dependence and cross-client module swapping, plus extensive experiments (details cut off in the abstract).

5offY6ZcaQ.one_liner: Benchmark of 1,000 human-verified video-QA pairs testing MLLMs on brief, answer-critical visual events.
5offY6ZcaQ.problem: Broad video benchmarks do not show whether MLLMs can notice and use brief, temporally localized evidence such as momentary actions or state transitions.
5offY6ZcaQ.method: 1,000 human-verified QA pairs across seven domains and 25 subcategories cover Temporal Occurrence, Temporal Counting, Action Description, and Temporal Reasoning, built around observable events or event sequences. 34 proprietary and open-source MLLMs are evaluated, with diagnostic analyses of frame sampling.
5offY6ZcaQ.key_idea: Build questions whose answers hinge on transient visual events and diagnose frame-sampling sufficiency using a human-audited subset.
5offY6ZcaQ.evidence: Evaluation of 34 proprietary and open-source MLLMs, with diagnostics on denser frame sampling and an audited subset.
5offY6ZcaQ.claimed_gains: The best model, Seed-2.0-Pro, reaches 39.6% overall accuracy, and most open-source models remain below 25%.

xqwa1hjxba.one_liner: Open-world multimodal graph learning that detects unknown nodes, proposes classes with an MLLM, and expands classes only with consistent evidence.
xqwa1hjxba.problem: Fixed-label-space multimodal graph models cannot handle new classes after deployment, and existing methods do not check whether existing classes fail to cover unknown nodes or whether generated classes are reliable.
xqwa1hjxba.method: MOVE identifies nodes not assignable to existing classes using visual tokens, textual attributes, and graph context, has a multimodal LLM generate candidate classes, and expands the class space only when candidates are consistently supported by multimodal evidence and not redundant.
xqwa1hjxba.key_idea: Gate class-space expansion on multimodal evidence consistency, so only reliable, non-redundant LLM-proposed classes are added.
xqwa1hjxba.evidence: Experiments across unknown recognition, open-domain annotation, and downstream graph learning tasks; datasets are not named in the abstract.
xqwa1hjxba.claimed_gains: Average improvement of 2.73% across unknown recognition, open-domain annotation, and downstream graph learning tasks.

OMFyWCZRyw.one_liner: Dual-branch panoramic reconstruction: low-resolution equirectangular pose branch and high-resolution cubemap geometry branch linked by register tokens.
OMFyWCZRyw.problem: Feed-forward panoramic reconstruction becomes expensive at high resolution when pose estimation and dense geometry share global interactions, although pose accuracy peaks at moderate resolution while geometry benefits from higher resolution.
OMFyWCZRyw.method: PanoDPG does global camera reasoning on low-resolution equirectangular images and detailed geometry reconstruction on high-resolution cubemap views. Register tokens carry information between the branches and across cubemap groups without all-to-all interaction among high-resolution tokens.
OMFyWCZRyw.key_idea: Decouple pose from geometry by resolution and projection, exchanging context through register tokens rather than dense cross-token attention.
OMFyWCZRyw.evidence: Experiments on multiple datasets, which are not named in the abstract.
OMFyWCZRyw.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative claim only: competitive or best reconstruction accuracy with substantially reduced computational cost)

t1Y0AwnB4O.one_liner: Predicts each client's relative optimization trend from past participations and dispatches coordinated, client-specific local starting points in federated learning.
t1Y0AwnB4O.problem: Federated learning gives all clients the current global model as the local starting point, and prior work using historical model differences or random perturbations does not exploit repeat participants' historical responses relative to the concurrent collaborative process.
t1Y0AwnB4O.method: FedEcho recasts training starting-point dispatch as a jointly coordinated, low-dimensional optimization control among clients in the same round. The server predicts each client's relative optimization trend from its historical relative responses, measured against the same-round weighted-average displacement along the global trajectory, and dispatches starting points accordingly.
t1Y0AwnB4O.key_idea: Predict a client's next-participation relative optimization trend from its historical response relative to the same-round average displacement, then jointly coordinate low-dimensional starting-point dispatch across the round's clients.
t1Y0AwnB4O.evidence: The abstract reports an observation that client relative responses show short-term cross-participation persistence that weakens at longer participation gaps; experiments are in the truncated part and not visible.

TmNJjJVzRc.one_liner: Integrates 3D foundation-model features and depth, motion, pose, and intrinsics priors into an end-to-end differential bundle adjustment SLAM system.
TmNJjJVzRc.problem: Conventional visual SLAM relies on reliable correspondences and breaks under weak visual evidence and scene dynamics, while foundation-model feed-forward predictions may not satisfy multi-view geometric constraints.
TmNJjJVzRc.method: Foundation-model features and complementary depth, motion, pose, and intrinsics priors enter an end-to-end differential bundle adjustment (DBA) framework, with a warping-based updater for efficient correspondence estimation that reduces memory overhead. Uncertainty-gated relative-pose constraints are added to online BA to support camera estimation (sentence truncated in the abstract).
TmNJjJVzRc.key_idea: Embed foundation-model features and uncertainty-gated priors inside differential bundle adjustment, with a warping-based updater for correspondences, so multi-view geometry constrains the learned priors.
TmNJjJVzRc.evidence: The visible abstract describes the system design for streaming videos under unconstrained capture; benchmarks, datasets, and results are not visible in the truncated text.
TmNJjJVzRc.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says memory overhead is substantially reduced but gives no numbers.

eyy7VlEVIk.one_liner: Selects and combines multiple reader models' hidden-state probe scores and token-likelihood features to detect hallucinations in already-generated LLM answers.
eyy7VlEVIk.problem: Existing hallucination detectors need internal access to the target model or repeated interaction with it, and reader size, answering ability, and family match do not reliably guide which accessible reader to use.
eyy7VlEVIk.method: READ is a supervised framework that selects readers by cross-validated log-loss reduction and combines their hidden-state probe scores and token-likelihood features in a fixed additive logistic model. Each reader scores the question and observed answer tokens through teacher forcing.
eyy7VlEVIk.key_idea: Rank accessible reader models by cross-validated log-loss reduction and fuse their probe and token-likelihood evidence with a fixed additive logistic model, backed by an information-theoretic contribution measure.
eyy7VlEVIk.evidence: Experiments on 6 target LLMs and 7 benchmarks, plus an analysis showing reader rankings vary across targets and benchmarks and that readers provide complementary evidence.
eyy7VlEVIk.claimed_gains: 0.911 cell-macro AUROC, improving over the strongest published baseline under the same access constraints by 0.116.

XXmVu6trMs.one_liner: Training-free 3DGS reasoning segmentation: lifts 2D masks to language-anchored 3D supports, then selects targets via bounded vision-language decisions.
XXmVu6trMs.problem: Language-guided segmentation in 3D Gaussian Splatting must resolve spatial and relational constraints, but existing benchmarks emphasize single targets and shallow relations.
XXmVu6trMs.method: Introduces the Nest-LERF and Nest-ScanNet benchmarks (zero-target, single-target, and grouped-multiple-target settings with nesting, stacking, part-whole, spatial-directional, and mixed relations). NestSplat derives a scene vocabulary from training views, lifts 2D masks into language-anchored 3D supports, and selects query targets through bounded vision-language decisions with geometric context.
XXmVu6trMs.key_idea: Derive a scene vocabulary from training views, lift 2D masks into language-anchored 3D supports, and choose targets with bounded vision-language decisions given geometric context, with no per-scene training.
XXmVu6trMs.evidence: Evaluated on the new Nest-LERF and Nest-ScanNet benchmarks and transferred to Ref-LERF and Causal-LERF.
XXmVu6trMs.claimed_gains: 34.16% and 27.42% mIoU on Nest-LERF and Nest-ScanNet, respectively, without per-scene training; also says it transfers strongly to Ref-LERF and Causal-LERF (no numbers given).

oJWlezUBd8.one_liner: Encoder-only attack on LVLMs that manipulates visual-token priorities so inputs fail after token compression but stay correct with full tokens.
oJWlezUBd8.problem: Aggregate robustness measures do not show whether an adversarial failure is caused by visual-token compression or inherited from the underlying LVLM.
oJWlezUBd8.method: Frames compression-induced risk as paired failure attribution, where a compression-specific failure (CSF) is an adversarial input that is correct under full-token inference but fails after compression. CIRA optimizes image perturbations through vision-encoder-side objectives that manipulate token priorities across candidate compression budgets while preserving displaced evidence, using no questions, labels, language-model access, compressor access, or exact budget.
oJWlezUBd8.key_idea: Optimize image perturbations with encoder-side objectives that shift which tokens a compressor retains across candidate budgets, while preserving the evidence displaced by compression.
oJWlezUBd8.evidence: 12 dataset-compressor settings evaluated at four budgets, similar behavior on additional LVLM families, and counterfactuals in a controlled diagnostic cohort showing retained-set allocation causally changes compressed correctness.
oJWlezUBd8.claimed_gains: Mean CSFR of 20.35% while limiting full-token attack success to 6.92% across 12 dataset-compressor settings at four budgets.

HM2yW3MmCx.one_liner: Spiking mixture-of-experts with a k-WTA router that selects Top-K experts from discrete spike counts using lateral inhibition and refractory periods.
HM2yW3MmCx.problem: Combining spiking neural networks with mixture-of-experts requires an expert-selection mechanism based on spiking activity, and multimodal tasks also face incomplete multisensory inputs.
HM2yW3MmCx.method: A spike-based k-WTA Router, inspired by competition-inhibition in hippocampal CA1, uses lateral inhibition and a refractory period to pick Top-K experts by discrete spike counts. A two-stage missing-modality module combines empirical prototypes from an observed-modality pool with modality-specific learnable embeddings to build missing-modality representations.
HM2yW3MmCx.key_idea: Select Top-K experts by discrete spike counts under lateral inhibition and a refractory period, and fill missing modalities from observed-modality prototypes plus learnable modality embeddings.
HM2yW3MmCx.evidence: Experiments on vision, language, and multimodal benchmarks, including varied missing-modality conditions; specific datasets are not visible in the text.
HM2yW3MmCx.claimed_gains: Claims best results among SNN baselines, parity or better versus ANN counterparts, and robustness across missing-modality conditions; no numbers stated.

BmRHudh6iB.one_liner: Maps MM-DiT contextual tokens into a frozen LLM with a bottleneck so it can answer questions about the emerging image.
BmRHudh6iB.problem: MM-DiTs repeatedly update text tokens through multimodal attention into contextual tokens whose function is not well understood.
BmRHudh6iB.method: A lightweight bottleneck network maps intermediate contextual tokens into the input space of a frozen LLM, which answers questions about the emerging image from these hidden states. Building on the findings, Contextual Alignment is introduced as a training technique (description truncated in the abstract).
BmRHudh6iB.key_idea: Read contextual tokens by projecting them through a trained bottleneck into a frozen LLM's input space; Contextual Alignment training builds on the readability findings.
BmRHudh6iB.evidence: Probing experiments showing contextual tokens encode scene semantics early in denoising, stay decodable with an empty prompt, and correlate with human-preference scores; specific models and datasets are not visible.

7EkDxCbiuO.one_liner: Visual chemistry framework that retrieves literature mechanism figures and generates executable electron edits to predict reaction mechanisms zero-shot.
7EkDxCbiuO.problem: Learned reaction-mechanism models transfer poorly to unseen chemistry, because familiar mechanisms must be applied to unfamiliar structures and some target mechanisms are poorly covered in training data.
7EkDxCbiuO.method: MechaVLM learns reusable visual features through multiscale chemical grounding and cross-rendering contrastive learning. For open-book prediction it retrieves a fixed set of precedents from 70,384 literature mechanism figures and re-reads relevant visual evidence as the molecular state evolves, while an atom-indexed language decoder recursively generates executable electron edits.
7EkDxCbiuO.key_idea: Ground molecules in transferable visual features, retrieve precedent mechanism figures, re-read them as the molecular state changes, and decode atom-indexed electron edits recursively without symbolic figure parsing.
7EkDxCbiuO.evidence: Cross-dataset and literature-derived benchmarks, including the new MechBench with 2,184 mechanisms and 9,146 elementary steps; retrieval draws on 70,384 literature mechanism figures.
7EkDxCbiuO.claimed_gains: Claims strong zero-shot mechanism prediction across cross-dataset and literature-derived benchmarks; no performance numbers are visible (abstract truncated).

CE2m5ATPk0.one_liner: RL for query-level multi-agent system search: trains on queries at the policy's competence boundary and rewards substructures by output-quality gain.
CE2m5ATPk0.problem: Existing RL methods that learn query-specific MAS construction repeat a fixed query set and assign workflow-level rewards, ignoring queries' changing learning potential and hiding which substructures improve quality.
CE2m5ATPk0.method: ASPO adds an Adaptive Query-Selection Mechanism that focuses on queries the policy can solve but not yet reliably, plus a discovery mechanism that widens architectural exploration for hard queries. Substructure-level rewards measure output-quality gains within each action's descendant subgraph and guide proximal policy optimization.
CE2m5ATPk0.key_idea: Reward each action by the output-quality gain in its descendant subgraph, and sample training queries at the policy's competence boundary, within PPO.
CE2m5ATPk0.evidence: The visible abstract describes the training framework only; benchmarks, models, and results are in the truncated part and not visible.

aXeMWg7nFO.one_liner: Mechanistic analysis of carry errors in multi-operand LLM addition, yielding a training-free correction from arithmetic-incompatibility signals.
aXeMWg7nFO.problem: LLMs are brittle on elementary arithmetic, and it is unclear how a local carry error becomes a persistent autoregressive trajectory or whether evidence of the error survives after commitment.
aXeMWg7nFO.method: Uses matched digit-preserved carry counterfactuals and causal interventions to decompose errors into generation, read-back routing, and downstream compatibility. The delayed compatibility signal, visible in next-token behavior, entropy, and representation geometry, drives a training-free, mechanism-guided correction method.
aXeMWg7nFO.key_idea: The emitted digit selects a lower- or higher-carry route through a localized query-key interaction, and downstream states still signal whether that digit is arithmetically compatible, enabling correction.
aXeMWg7nFO.evidence: Matched digit-preserved carry counterfactuals and causal interventions on multi-operand addition; the models and exact-answer accuracy figures are not detailed in the abstract.
aXeMWg7nFO.claimed_gains: Substantially improves exact-answer accuracy and outperforms most training-required baselines; no numbers stated.

4ho38AY6PT.one_liner: Open benchmark of 150 AI-operated accounts over 30 workdays for testing monitors that catch insider threats by agents.
4ho38AY6PT.problem: Existing benchmarks do not test whether defenders can detect agent activity such as weight exfiltration, training-data poisoning, or weakened release gates among routine work under a limited review budget.
4ho38AY6PT.method: Mole contains 150 AI-operated accounts sharing 9 stateful services over 30 workdays, with 12 threats and 8 corpora from four models totaling roughly 20 billion tokens. It supports comparing 40 monitors across corpus generators, observability levels, and threats, and developing new monitors.
4ho38AY6PT.key_idea: Embed harmful agent objectives in realistic multi-account, multi-service activity corpora and score monitors on detection under a limited review budget.
4ho38AY6PT.evidence: Evaluates 39 agent models on harmful objectives and 40 monitors across corpus generators, observability levels, and threats, including a single-day audit-event comparison and benchmark-guided monitor search.
4ho38AY6PT.claimed_gains: 72% of 39 agent models complete most assigned harmful objectives; the best monitor misses nearly half of completed harm; benchmark-guided search improves a mid-tier monitor by 49-64%; selective use of a stronger monitor improves budget-AUC by 10% at comparable modeled cost.
