JDhxa6pfl7.one_liner: Sparse-view 3DGS surface reconstruction that combines anchor depths from multi-view matching with local log-depth differences from VGGT.
JDhxa6pfl7.problem: Foundation-model depth supervision for sparse-view 3DGS lacks dense multi-view matching, and aligned VGGT depth has smoothly varying bias across surfaces while its local depth variations are more accurate.
JDhxa6pfl7.method: DGS combines point evidence (accurate absolute anchor depths from multi-view photometric matching) with edge evidence (local log-depth differences of VGGT), coupled by a global integration that extends anchors through local edge relations while constraining accumulated drift. It adds prior-based aggregation and anchor depth refinement to improve coverage (abstract truncated).
JDhxa6pfl7.key_idea: Integrate photometric-matching anchor depths with VGGT local log-depth differences globally, so edge relations extend anchors while constraining drift, instead of supervising directly with predicted depth.
JDhxa6pfl7.evidence: The visible abstract states the motivation and design; datasets, baselines, and results are in the truncated part and not visible.

r3OXShZBjo.one_liner: Benchmark of 789 questions comparing long-context LVLMs and memory-augmented agents on multimodal multi-session conversations at 32K-256K tokens.
r3OXShZBjo.problem: No existing benchmark systematically compares long-context LVLMs and memory-augmented agents on questions that genuinely require multimodal evidence.
r3OXShZBjo.method: MEMLENS has 789 questions across five memory abilities (information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge update, answer refusal) at four standard context lengths from 32K to 256K tokens under a cross-modal token-counting scheme.
r3OXShZBjo.key_idea: Score memory on questions that need image evidence, using controlled image ablation and cross-modal token counting to compare long-context LVLMs against memory-augmented agents at standard context lengths.
r3OXShZBjo.evidence: Evaluates 27 LVLMs and 7 memory-augmented agents; controlled image ablation on 634 image-essential and image-supportive questions drops two frontier LVLMs below 2% accuracy.
r3OXShZBjo.claimed_gains: Benchmark results: best 32K accuracy is 58.68% for LVLMs and 33.46% for memory agents, and multi-session reasoning caps most systems below 30%.

qYB9vc0xka.one_liner: Dialogue memory: sparse addressing finds the episode, binding-following completes evidence, and a budgeted set of original turns is selected.
qYB9vc0xka.problem: LLM conversational systems with long interaction histories must retrieve the most discriminative evidence for a response within a limited reader-context budget.
qYB9vc0xka.method: SEA-Mem encodes each turn into immutable traces, source atoms, and sparse bindings. At query time a planner groups information needs, then DG-Address pinpoints the episode via sparse addressing, CA3-Complete recovers evidence by following bindings, and CA1-Select picks a budgeted set of turns that jointly supports the query.
qYB9vc0xka.key_idea: Mimic hippocampal DG/CA3/CA1: address an episode by sparse cues, complete evidence through stored bindings, and pass only selected original turns, not the associations, to the answerer.
qYB9vc0xka.evidence: Experiments on LongMemEval and LoCoMo under a fixed source budget, a matched LongMemEval subset comparing Oracle evidence to full histories, and tests with semantically confusable distractors.
qYB9vc0xka.claimed_gains: Strong answer quality on LongMemEval and LoCoMo under a fixed source budget, accuracy largely preserved from Oracle evidence to full histories on a matched LongMemEval subset, and more resistance to confusable distractors; no numbers stated.

HeRiQIEY54.one_liner: Benchmark platform evaluating PDE reconstruction and forecasting under varying observation patterns, with 560,000 fields and trajectories from seven PDE families.
HeRiQIEY54.problem: Evaluating physical-field models under a single observation pattern does not show how performance changes when measurement density or spatial layout changes.
HeRiQIEY54.method: An integrated platform covering data generation, training, and evaluation, with configurable observation operators, seven adapted baselines for stationary reconstruction and short-horizon forecasting, and a protocol that compares models against references trained for each test pattern on identical test observations and targets.
HeRiQIEY54.key_idea: Separate observation construction from physical records so parameterized observation patterns and mixtures can vary while targets and splits stay fixed, scored against per-pattern reference models.
HeRiQIEY54.evidence: On a 14,000-record subset, 441 trained models were evaluated under nine test patterns, giving 3,969 evaluations across seven PDE families and seven baselines.
HeRiQIEY54.claimed_gains: Mean cross-pattern error exceeds mean matched-pattern error in all 49 PDE-method pairs, persisting in a configuration-matched subset of 117 models; denser test observations do not consistently reduce error for a fixed model.

DbfeqW6Pk9.one_liner: Benchmark of 336K multiple-choice questions testing whether foundation models ground UAV-image instances to vector-map entities and reason with map knowledge.
DbfeqW6Pk9.problem: Aerial perception benchmarks test class-level recognition in the image plane but not whether models can ground visual instances to their real-world entities in a vector map.
DbfeqW6Pk9.method: UAV-MapVQA has 336K multiple-choice QA pairs from 14,000 real UAV images across 3 countries and more than 1,000 km of flights, built with automatic registration, formally verified QA generation, and human validation. It spans eight tasks across four levels, and each question comes with both a rendered raster map and a structured entity table.
DbfeqW6Pk9.key_idea: Pair each UAV question with two representations of the same vector map, raster rendering and entity table, to isolate how map format affects cross-view grounding and geospatial reasoning.
DbfeqW6Pk9.evidence: Evaluation of 15 foundation models, spanning proprietary and open-weight, on the benchmark (results truncated in the abstract).

KpOgFQLOqG.one_liner: Unified static 3D and dynamic 4D spatial reasoning for VLMs using decoupled group-wise EMA and a spatial-dynamic fusion module.
KpOgFQLOqG.problem: 3D post-training can weaken dynamic understanding while 4D-specialized models lack strong static 3D reasoning, because spatial-dynamic interference is non-uniform across parameter groups and sensitive to late-layer MLPs.
KpOgFQLOqG.method: Decoupled EMA (D-EMA) applies configurable group-wise averaging to constrain drift in interference-sensitive pretrained parameters. Spatial-Dynamic Fusion (SDF) selectively integrates spatial and temporal priors from a dynamic geometry encoder into intermediate VLM representations under semantic guidance.
KpOgFQLOqG.key_idea: Constrain drift of interference-sensitive parameter groups with group-wise EMA while injecting a dynamic geometry encoder's priors into intermediate VLM features under semantic guidance.
KpOgFQLOqG.evidence: Ten metrics across nine static 3D and dynamic 4D benchmarks, including ReVSI, DSR-Bench, and DSI-Bench under sample-wise and group-wise protocols, plus a parameter-group interference analysis.
KpOgFQLOqG.claimed_gains: Highest average score across ten metrics on nine benchmarks; 56.0 on ReVSI, 67.2 on DSR-Bench, and 51.2 and 40.1 under DSI-Bench's sample-wise and group-wise protocols.

kR9nwx4zFa.one_liner: Shows masked diffusion LMs assemble a relation-conditioned entity state early, then uses it for Multi-View Edit knowledge editing and retrieval.
kR9nwx4zFa.problem: It is unclear how masked diffusion language models store the lookup key for a fact, which determines which queries can retrieve it, what an edit must cover, and what a retriever can read.
kR9nwx4zFa.method: Mechanistic analysis of the factual access state in DLMs, then two uses of it: Multi-View Edit fits one shared value per query direction across the state region and installs it in the early-MLP block from one declarative statement, and a retrieval use is also described (truncated in the abstract).
kR9nwx4zFa.key_idea: First-layer attention routes relation wording into the visible entity position and early FFNs look up the fact there, so edits must cover a region of states.
kR9nwx4zFa.evidence: Mechanistic comparison of autoregressive and masked diffusion LMs on factual recall; editing results on source-prompt reliability, paraphrase, and reverse queries are mentioned but cut off.
kR9nwx4zFa.claimed_gains: Multi-View Edit preserves source-prompt reliability while substantially improving paraphrase and reverse generalization (abstract truncated); no numbers stated.

NU6DWAXjWU.one_liner: Proves a single-noise-scale score field can identify a junction's center, local dimension, branch directions, and relative masses under stated conditions.
NU6DWAXjWU.problem: At a junction of intersecting branches the score blends several branches' contributions, and it is unclear whether one Gaussian noise scale suffices to locate the junction and recover branch directions and probability masses.
NU6DWAXjWU.method: Models the singularity as a d-homogeneous tangent cone and develops a derivative-free two-stage theory: a linear self-calibration system from a score identity gives the center and mass exponent, then the tangential score on one centered sphere determines the normalized angular measure. For at most K discrete rays, low-order spherical-harmonic deconvolution recovers branch count, directions, and weights.
NU6DWAXjWU.key_idea: Integrate the score identity against localized test functions to self-calibrate center and exponent, then deconvolve low-order spherical harmonics of the tangential score on one sphere to recover branches.
NU6DWAXjWU.evidence: Theory: identifiability and stability results, plus an example where symmetric three-way and four-way planar junctions share the same log-density Hessian at the vertex but have distinct score fields on a surrounding shell; no experiments are visible.

rn94dgkcFW.one_liner: Compresses the Bench2Drive closed-loop benchmark by cost-aware clustering of routes into representative low-cost anchors learned from model evaluation records.
rn94dgkcFW.problem: Closed-loop AD benchmarks such as Bench2Drive are costly, with statistical route redundancy and highly imbalanced per-route cost where a few long routes dominate total testing time.
rn94dgkcFW.method: Learns compact route representations directly from model evaluation records and selects representative low-cost anchor routes through cost-aware clustering, then estimates full-benchmark metrics from those anchors.
rn94dgkcFW.key_idea: Embed routes from existing models' evaluation records and pick low-cost anchor routes by cost-aware clustering, so a small route subset predicts full-benchmark results.
rn94dgkcFW.evidence: Held-out advanced AD model variants on Bench2Drive, compared with general-purpose benchmark compression methods and compact AD benchmarks, including out-of-distribution generalization.
rn94dgkcFW.claimed_gains: Cuts route count by 65% and total evaluation time by over 70%, estimates Success Rate with ~1.2% mean absolute error and 0.9+ Spearman correlation; versus existing compression methods, cuts evaluation time by 27.2% and estimation error by 64% on average.

OI3i0JpQuh.one_liner: Unified model with a physical reasoner, world generator, and action predictor, with actions as natural language and history-conditioned flow matching.
OI3i0JpQuh.problem: Vision-language-action models have limited grounding in world dynamics from action-only supervision, while world-action models are limited in semantic understanding and reasoning under distribution shifts.
OI3i0JpQuh.method: UniWAM integrates a physical reasoner, a world generator, and an action predictor, representing low-level robot actions in natural language and pre-training with complementary supervision from VQA data, human egocentric data, and robot demonstrations assigned to the appropriate components. Post-training uses future visual noise augmentation and history-conditioned flow matching, which initializes action generation from encoded action history.
OI3i0JpQuh.key_idea: Express robot actions in language to keep VLM abilities, route VQA, egocentric, and robot data to matching components, and initialize flow-matching action generation from encoded action history.
OI3i0JpQuh.evidence: Multiple evaluations including in-distribution performance; the rest of the list of evaluations is truncated in the abstract.
OI3i0JpQuh.claimed_gains: Claims best performance across multiple evaluations and significantly fewer denoising steps at maintained performance; no numbers stated.

y8pg5KaIK8.one_liner: Benchmark for vision-and-language navigation under language-specified forbidden regions, plus C2Nav, a constraint-conditioned navigator for graph-based agents.
y8pg5KaIK8.problem: VLN-CE is scored by goal reaching, so an agent can succeed while entering a restricted region or approaching a fragile object, an unsafe success that standard metrics hide.
y8pg5KaIK8.method: NS-VLN grounds negative spatial constraints as forbidden regions in continuous environments, with constraint-compliant reference trajectories, a three-level taxonomy (separated, linguistically integrated, semantically entangled), safety-specific metrics, and forbidden-allowed counterfactual pairs. C2Nav, a Constraint-Conditioned Navigator for graph-based VLN agents, learns linguistic-role-sensitive behavior (abstract truncated).
y8pg5KaIK8.key_idea: Distinguish goal success from safe success by grounding negative constraints as forbidden regions, and test understanding with forbidden-allowed counterfactual pairs.
y8pg5KaIK8.evidence: Evaluation of representative VLN-CE agents and of naive training on constraint-augmented data on the new NS-VLN benchmark.
y8pg5KaIK8.claimed_gains: Reports substantial unsafe success across representative VLN-CE agents and a substantial remaining gap after naive constraint-augmented training; no numbers stated.

fk9h8CvR0c.one_liner: Diagnostic benchmark separating State preparation, information Access, and Evidence use in long-context LLM memory systems, with 96 synthetic document collections.
fk9h8CvR0c.problem: When a memory-based LLM system answers incorrectly, the answer alone does not reveal whether the failure came from State preparation, information access, or evidence use.
fk9h8CvR0c.method: Specifies what knowledge a model should retain and generates 96 synthetic document collections across four task families, deriving questions and updates from the same facts and rules. Automated checks verify which combinations of retained knowledge and source records determine each answer, and independent function tests are compared with complete workflows.
fk9h8CvR0c.key_idea: Automated checks tie each answer to the retained knowledge and source records that determine it, so failures can be attributed to State, Access, or Evidence.
fk9h8CvR0c.evidence: 96 synthetic document collections over four task families, independent function tests versus complete workflows, and inspection of the memory and passages supplied in selected cases.
fk9h8CvR0c.claimed_gains: Finding: answering questions about State correctly does not guarantee retrieving the facts needed to use it; no numeric results stated.

KA5Msh8ETw.one_liner: Diffusion anomaly detection often works best with a single denoising step; ODD uses standard training but reconstructs in one step.
KA5Msh8ETw.problem: Diffusion-based anomaly detection assumes iterative denoising improves reconstruction and therefore detection, but it is unclear whether iterative refinement actually helps.
KA5Msh8ETw.method: ODD keeps standard diffusion training on normal samples but reconstructs with a single denoising step, motivated by an analysis of the optimal velocity field. It can also replace iterative denoising in existing methods as a plug-and-play component.
KA5Msh8ETw.key_idea: Iterative denoising increasingly reconstructs anomalous information (anomaly leakage), shrinking normal-anomaly score separation, so one denoising step minimizes leakage in the analyzed setting.
KA5Msh8ETw.evidence: A large-scale empirical study across diverse AD datasets and diffusion designs, a theoretical analysis of the optimal velocity field, and experiments across diverse datasets and modalities.
KA5Msh8ETw.claimed_gains: Reports strong detection performance with substantially improved inference efficiency across diverse datasets and modalities; no numbers stated.

Yrf4JrVpJa.one_liner: Native 3D Gaussian VAE that encodes scenes into fixed-layout triplane latents, with a latent flow-matching model for scene-level generation.
Yrf4JrVpJa.problem: Native 3D Gaussian scenes are hard to compress into generative representations because primitive counts vary widely, spatial density is nonuniform, and neighboring primitives differ in geometry and appearance.
Yrf4JrVpJa.method: The encoder uses cell-wise learned queries to aggregate projected Gaussians into multiple slots per cell; the decoder predicts occupancy to find active regions, then reconstructs local Gaussian sets with query-based set prediction and candidate selection. A latent flow-matching model on this representation supports point-cloud-conditioned synthesis and single-image-conditioned amodal generation.
Yrf4JrVpJa.key_idea: Impose a fixed triplane layout on the latent while keeping Gaussians spatially adaptive via multi-slot cell queries in the encoder and occupancy-gated set prediction in the decoder.
Yrf4JrVpJa.evidence: Experiments on reconstruction and on conditional scene-level generation from point clouds and single images (details truncated in the abstract).
Yrf4JrVpJa.claimed_gains: Claims high-fidelity reconstruction and generation from a single image; no numbers stated.

o8vtAxsted.one_liner: Weights on-policy distillation supervision per turn using final outcomes of paired student continuations, instead of relying on teacher-student token gaps.
o8vtAxsted.problem: On-policy distillation for multi-turn agents treats large teacher-student token-level gaps as places needing correction, but large gaps can be benign and small gaps can be outcome-critical.
o8vtAxsted.method: OG-OPD applies trajectory-relative weighting to teacher supervision and calibrates the weights using final task outcomes from paired student continuations, selectively strengthening supervision on the student's trajectories at turns where guidance helps (abstract truncated).
o8vtAxsted.key_idea: Calibrate trajectory-relative teacher-supervision weights with final task outcomes of paired student continuations, so guidance is strengthened where the student can turn it into better outcomes.
o8vtAxsted.evidence: An empirical analysis of the supervision-benefit mismatch in multi-turn agent distillation; benchmark results are truncated and not visible.

A77bt8Tjw1.one_liner: Selects sparse semantic memory edits that maximize counterfactual memory regret, the paired increase in downstream loss, instead of attack success.
A77bt8Tjw1.problem: Persistent-memory attacks on LLM agents are judged by whether they succeed, although successful attacks can leave persistent states with very different downstream consequences.
A77bt8Tjw1.method: Defines counterfactual memory regret (CMR), the paired increase in expected downstream loss relative to clean memory. MemHarm predeclares a finite class of sparse, grounded semantic edits, scores candidates through the normal agent memory interface with offline paired-loss feedback, and certifies resolved selections within that class.
A77bt8Tjw1.key_idea: Choose memory edits by paired downstream-loss increase over clean memory (CMR) from a predeclared finite class of sparse semantic edits, rather than by attack success.
A77bt8Tjw1.evidence: Two agent benchmarks and diverse memory designs, factor-removal interventions linking harm to the selected semantic factor, and native-agent deployments verifying the write-to-fresh-process attack path.
A77bt8Tjw1.claimed_gains: CMR-guided selection yields substantially larger downstream loss while retaining most of the success-rate gain, with the highest CMR point estimates among evaluated general attacks; no numbers stated.

XCj6DK0V7q.one_liner: Black-box multimodal jailbreak: calibrate once on a target using shared refusal coordinates, then reuse one carrier for unseen requests.
XCj6DK0V7q.problem: Universal multimodal jailbreaks rely on surrogate-side optimization without target adaptation, and query-based black-box methods need fresh target queries for every request.
XCj6DK0V7q.method: UniCal aligns refusal and compliance structures from heterogeneous surrogates into a shared coordinate space, and a coordinate-conditioned generator maps a fixed benign seed and a low-dimensional coordinate to a request-independent image and text carrier. For a new target the generator is frozen and only a sparse coordinate offset is chosen through an evaluator-mediated three-way decision-label interface.
XCj6DK0V7q.key_idea: Map surrogate refusal and compliance structure into shared coordinates, generate a request-independent carrier from a coordinate, and adapt to a new target by selecting only a sparse coordinate offset.
XCj6DK0V7q.evidence: Tested on five coordinate-pool models, with leave-one-model-out registration of the learned coordinates; results on unseen targets are truncated.
XCj6DK0V7q.claimed_gains: 89.6% mean strict success under one-time decision-label adaptation across the five coordinate-pool models.

yS1rjqg0nQ.one_liner: Behavior Turing Test: scores human-likeness of humanoid behavior under task and scene context, with the HuCo dataset and CoBE evaluator.
yS1rjqg0nQ.problem: Humanoid evaluation focuses on task success, tracking accuracy, or motion-level human-likeness, and does not ask whether a human would behave this way under the same task and scene.
yS1rjqg0nQ.method: Builds HuCo, 1,280 behavior clips from real humans, digital humans, real humanoids, and simulated humanoids, each paired with a Task Goal and Scene Description, and uses Context-SMPL to suppress embodiment-specific appearance while keeping motion and scene context. CoBE, a Context-conditioned Behavior Evaluator, retrieves context-relevant behavioral evidence to align with human judgments.
yS1rjqg0nQ.key_idea: Render all embodiments in Context-SMPL to remove appearance cues, collect contextual human-likeness judgments, and introduce an evaluator that retrieves context-relevant behavioral evidence.
yS1rjqg0nQ.evidence: HuCoBench with task and scene counterfactual subsets for context sensitivity, compared against human judgments on the HuCo dataset.
yS1rjqg0nQ.claimed_gains: Some humanoid behaviors reach the real-human reference under the Motion Turing Test but fall below it under BTT, and CoBE shows the strongest alignment with human judgments among evaluated methods (abstract truncated); no numbers stated.

5VBfF3tT8I.one_liner: Adaptive sampling for visual tool-use RL: accuracy buckets and a reward-feedback controller match batch difficulty to the model's current ability.
5VBfF3tT8I.problem: Training crop-and-zoom VLMs with GRPO on hard tool-essential data is inefficient because filtering all-zero-reward samples needs many extra multi-round rollouts.
5VBfF3tT8I.method: CalDS organizes examples into dynamically updated buckets by tool-augmented accuracy and uses a bounded reward-feedback controller with difficulty shaping to adjust sampling probabilities by bucket difficulty and reward history. It reuses recent rollouts to calibrate bucket difficulty estimates as the policy changes.
5VBfF3tT8I.key_idea: Sample from accuracy-based difficulty buckets with a bounded reward-feedback controller, and recalibrate stale bucket difficulty using recent rollouts, to emphasize challenging but currently learnable examples.
5VBfF3tT8I.evidence: The visible abstract describes the method for GRPO-based visual tool-use training; experiments and results are truncated and not visible.

IvVCyGOjj1.one_liner: FineHM multi-label harmful short-video dataset with frame and box evidence, plus ExplainHarm, a prompt-chained clue-mining detector.
IvVCyGOjj1.problem: Harm taxonomies are inconsistent across platforms and studies, public datasets are small and coarsely labeled, and multimodal fusion methods leave semantic gaps and temporal misalignment without frame-specific causal reasoning.
IvVCyGOjj1.method: FineHM spans 8 categories with harmful frames and bounding boxes and comes with fixed splits, metrics, and baselines. ExplainHarm surfaces dynamic evidence from category features and video content through a prompt-chained clue-mining process and aligns modalities with dual-scale temporal modeling.
IvVCyGOjj1.key_idea: Mine dynamic clues from category features and video content through a prompt chain, and align modalities across time with dual-scale temporal modeling.
IvVCyGOjj1.evidence: Experiments and statistical analyses on the FineHM benchmark with fixed splits, metrics, and baseline results; specific numbers are truncated.

4Ni9xL5Fpx.one_liner: Diagnostic framework that decomposes video-generation diversity into six dimensions: Semantic, Style, Subject, Scene, Motion, and Camera.
4Ni9xL5Fpx.problem: Video generation models often give highly similar outputs for repeated samples of one prompt, and global scalar diversity metrics hide where in the spatiotemporal space diversity collapses.
4Ni9xL5Fpx.method: Each of the six dimensions is measured with a reproducible computer-vision pipeline and analyzed alongside quality and instruction faithfulness. Controlled prompt interventions probe the causes of collapse.
4Ni9xL5Fpx.key_idea: Measure diversity per dimension with computer-vision pipelines, filter unfaithful generations, and use prompt interventions to separate default mode convergence from realization gaps.
4Ni9xL5Fpx.evidence: Systematic evaluation of representative video generation models, rankings checked after filtering unfaithful generations, and controlled prompt interventions.
4Ni9xL5Fpx.claimed_gains: Models with strong global diversity scores still collapse on specific dimensions, particularly Motion and Camera; no numbers stated.

o2KQHbRHhJ.one_liner: World action model that learns video and spatial representations via 3D Gaussian scene prediction and multi-view depth supervision for manipulation.
o2KQHbRHhJ.problem: World action models inherit spatio-temporal priors from video models, but visual plausibility does not ensure the geometric accuracy needed for fine-grained manipulation.
o2KQHbRHhJ.method: In video-spatial pre-training, a spatial expert extracts features from current and future video tokens using spatial and dynamics queries, and Spatio-Temporal Gaussian Modeling (STGM) fuses them to predict current and future 3D Gaussian scenes shared across views, with multi-view depth supervision. In post-training a randomly initialized action expert attends to the learned representations through joint attention while all three experts are updated, and STGM is omitted at inference.
o2KQHbRHhJ.key_idea: Supervise shared 3D Gaussian scene prediction with multi-view depth so video and spatial experts learn geometry, then let an action expert read those representations through joint attention.
o2KQHbRHhJ.evidence: Evaluated on RoboCasa, LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and three real-world tasks, with comparisons under identical pre-training data against video-only and 2D depth pre-training.
o2KQHbRHhJ.claimed_gains: 73.4% success on RoboCasa, 97.8% on LIBERO, 85.9% on LIBERO-Plus, and 72.0% average success across three real-world tasks.

XhpSPdQzxi.one_liner: Verifier-free diffusion inference that exchanges particles between neighboring chains at different sharpening strengths via an energy-based acceptance rate.
XhpSPdQzxi.problem: Achieving high sample quality under hard physical and dynamical constraints is difficult, and existing inference-time methods either need a costly or unavailable verifier or lose diversity without one.
XhpSPdQzxi.method: STEER (Score Tempering with Exchange between Exploratory Replicas) runs multiple diffusion chains at different sharpening strengths in place of single-chain sharpening, and neighboring chains exchange particles according to an energy-based acceptance rate, propagating exploration to output samples.
XhpSPdQzxi.key_idea: Replica exchange across diffusion chains tempered at different sharpening strengths provides population-based global search that keeps diversity without a verifier.
XhpSPdQzxi.evidence: Experiments from synthetic multimodal distributions to image generation, and continuous-control tasks in verifier-based and verifier-free settings.
XhpSPdQzxi.claimed_gains: Better fidelity-diversity trade-off across domains and improved success rates on continuous-control tasks in verifier-based and verifier-free settings; no numbers stated.

CXg1kNkheI.one_liner: Distills reusable LoRAs once per backbone for CFG, few-step sampling, and long-context error correction, deployed training-free on compatible video models.
CXg1kNkheI.problem: Specialized video diffusion models each repeat a distillation stage, for example for faster sampling or better long-video generation.
CXg1kNkheI.method: Learns reusable capabilities as LoRAs on a base model: single-pass classifier-free guidance, few-step sampling, and long-context error correction for autoregressive generation. A CFG LoRA offers guidance control through its inference weight, and combining it with a few-step LoRA keeps few-step generation and CFG controllability on downstream tasks.
CXg1kNkheI.key_idea: Train capability LoRAs on a base model once and plug them, without retraining, into downstream models from the same backbone family, even those with added conditioning branches.
CXg1kNkheI.evidence: Training-free deployment verified on 54 downstream models across three backbone families and eight task categories, including world modeling, robotics, editing, and multimodal generation.
CXg1kNkheI.claimed_gains: Verified on 54 downstream models across three backbone families and eight task categories without per-target retraining; no speedup numbers stated.

cJoMXWxAbm.one_liner: Agentic system that reconstructs a single image into an editable simulation-ready 3D scene, using edit-and-validate loops in a physics simulator.
cJoMXWxAbm.problem: Visual similarity is not enough for single-image scene reconstruction, since objects must be recovered, accurately placed, and physically grounded, and post-hoc simplistic physics settling often misplaces objects.
cJoMXWxAbm.method: SceneRig combines geometric, visual, and physical tools to reconstruct a 3D scene, and an agent then performs edit-and-validate loops inside a physics simulator to guarantee physical grounding.
cJoMXWxAbm.key_idea: An agent edits object placement and validates it inside a physics simulator, replacing post-hoc physics settling, so scenes are physically grounded.
cJoMXWxAbm.evidence: Evaluations on diverse scenes for instance segmentation, object-centric appearance, 3D placement, and physical stability, plus downstream real-robot policy outcome prediction and manipulation replay.
cJoMXWxAbm.claimed_gains: Improves instance segmentation, object-centric appearance, and 3D placement while keeping scenes physically stable, and predicts real-robot policy outcomes more accurately than baselines; no numbers stated.

4UBsk3YCDm.one_liner: Compresses only the endpoint interaction of Schrodinger bridges onto coarse states, giving a reusable solver that preserves fine marginals exactly.
4UBsk3YCDm.problem: When many endpoint pairs share the same dynamics, solving each Schrodinger bridge separately repeats a large optimization problem.
4UBsk3YCDm.method: They separate fine endpoint information from the interaction governing endpoint pairing, drop additive single-endpoint terms that leave the optimizer unchanged under fixed marginals, and approximate the remaining interaction on coarse states.
4UBsk3YCDm.key_idea: Because the marginals are fixed, additive single-endpoint terms do not change the optimizer, so only the log-interaction needs a coarse-state approximation.
4UBsk3YCDm.evidence: Theory bounding each KL direction by min{2*eta, eta^2/2} for a uniform log-interaction residual eta, a reference-only partition rule with an equal-budget guarantee, and experiments in molecular and stochastic-dynamics settings.

kNdGD5BTog.one_liner: Traces LLM output repetition to post-training choices via a loop-amplifying protocol, identifies three token-level factors and proposes two mitigations.
kNdGD5BTog.problem: Output repetition in LLMs degrades quality and wastes compute but is hard to reproduce reliably, leaving its mechanisms underexplored.
kNdGD5BTog.method: The Self-Reinforced Loop Approach (SRLA) amplifies repetition so it becomes reproducible, enabling comparisons across post-training recipes such as GRPO. Token-level analysis identifies selected-token lock-in, insufficient candidate token diversity and weak EOS activation, which motivate two mitigations.
kNdGD5BTog.key_idea: Amplify sporadic repetition with a self-reinforced loop, then attribute it to GRPO-style post-training through token-level lock-in, low candidate diversity and weak EOS activation.
kNdGD5BTog.evidence: Controlled cross-model comparisons using SRLA, including models trained with GRPO and on GRPO-distilled data, plus token-level distribution analysis.
kNdGD5BTog.claimed_gains: The two mitigations reduce repetition failure rates by an average of 86%.

FUoYzhoj4l.one_liner: Spiking neuron that fuses membrane prediction and input observation by Kalman-style weighting, with complex-valued spikes for robust temporal processing.
FUoYzhoj4l.problem: Disturbances disrupt spiking neural network membrane dynamics and spike generation, undermining computational reliability.
FUoYzhoj4l.method: The KF neuron forms a prediction from the preceding membrane state, treats the current input as an observation, and adaptively weights the two following the Kalman filtering principle to regulate membrane potential. The CS mechanism adds imaginary spikes that regulate real-valued firing through activity-dependent inhibition and provide an extra output stream, and a general convex-optimization framework describes input-state integration mechanisms.
FUoYzhoj4l.key_idea: Weight the membrane-state prediction against the current input observation with Kalman-style gains, and add imaginary spikes that inhibit real firing and carry temporal information.
FUoYzhoj4l.evidence: Experiments are not described in the visible abstract, which is truncated before the results.

Ih6YebKd6d.one_liner: DREAM keeps original memory records and adaptively activates retrieval entrances matching users' recent questions, rather than reorganizing memories in advance.
Ih6YebKd6d.problem: Memory-construction methods for AI assistants reorganize experiences without knowing future queries, and their advantage over directly retrieving original records (Dense) shrinks across diverse benchmarks and flips under question rephrasing.
Ih6YebKd6d.method: DREAM preserves original records and adapts the routes used to retrieve them: as users ask questions it activates retrieval entrances reflecting recent needs, so an initially retrieved record can lead to additional relevant evidence. A theoretical analysis shows no memory construction guarantees a universal advantage over Dense without query-distribution assumptions.
Ih6YebKd6d.key_idea: Keep raw records and add dynamically activated retrieval entrances that reflect recent user needs, linking an initially retrieved record to further evidence.
Ih6YebKd6d.evidence: Four benchmarks with Qwen3-VL-8B and Gemma4-12B, rephrasing counterexamples with evidence and answers held fixed, and a theoretical analysis.
Ih6YebKd6d.claimed_gains: Improves average Judge accuracy over Dense by 4.2 percentage points with Qwen3-VL-8B and 6.2 points with Gemma4-12B.

IXodoy1T6k.one_liner: Calibrates fine-tuned models by regularizing predictions and feature prototype structure toward the better-calibrated early-training model.
IXodoy1T6k.problem: Continued training or fine-tuning brings marginal accuracy gains but substantially increases calibration error, as models lose the uncertainty awareness of the early model.
IXodoy1T6k.method: EUA-Cal adds early prediction regularization to preserve early predictive uncertainty and prototype structure regularization that derives supervision from the early feature structure.
IXodoy1T6k.key_idea: Use the early-training model as an uncertainty anchor, regularizing both its output predictions and its prototype feature structure during later training.
IXodoy1T6k.evidence: Image classification and multiple-choice question answering across eight diverse models, compared with existing calibration methods.
IXodoy1T6k.claimed_gains: Outperforms existing calibration methods across eight models on image classification and multiple-choice question answering; no numbers stated.

rK38d8xJlc.one_liner: Interactive world model with factorized hybrid controls, compressed memory tokens shared by teacher and student, and Stable Forcing distillation.
rK38d8xJlc.problem: Interactive world models struggle with heterogeneous controls, while exploding contexts and unstable distillation block long-horizon consistency with real-time responsiveness.
rK38d8xJlc.method: WorldPlay2 pairs frame-aligned action control with structured semantic control that disentangles scene appearance, character identity, and dynamic events. It compresses history into memory tokens shared by the autoregressive student and bidirectional teacher, so the teacher scores short clips given history, and uses Stable Forcing (few-step initialization plus full-rollout replay).
rK38d8xJlc.key_idea: Compress history into shared memory tokens so the teacher distills short clips conditioned on history, and stabilize the student with few-step initialization and full-rollout replay.
rK38d8xJlc.evidence: not stated; the abstract is cut off before the experiments.

Ie6jjUf6MX.one_liner: A temporal benchmark that compares AI-generated research proposals from a frozen 2025 literature with 2026 human publications.
Ie6jjUf6MX.problem: Research taste, the judgment of what to read, pursue, and try, shapes AI scientists' work but is poorly understood compared with their ability to execute research.
Ie6jjUf6MX.method: ResearchMirror freezes the literature through 2025, has language models generate research proposals from it, and compares them with work published by the same communities in 2026. It adds blinded expert review of proposals against the 2026 papers.
Ie6jjUf6MX.key_idea: Freeze the literature at 2025 and score AI proposals against what human communities actually published in 2026 on citation and idea matching.
Ie6jjUf6MX.evidence: Six language models, four research areas, and more than 90,000 proposals, plus blinded expert review.
Ie6jjUf6MX.claimed_gains: AI scientists reach about 26% of the human level on citation matching and 18% on idea matching, across more than 90,000 proposals.

srWNrOWx2m.one_liner: A frozen LLM observer's representations, combined with target-specific examples and structured state, predict unfamiliar agents' next decisions.
srWNrOWx2m.problem: AI agents increasingly meet unfamiliar black-box counterparts, and it is unclear whether a counterpart's next decision can be predicted from a few observed interactions without access to its implementation.
srWNrOWx2m.method: They cast prediction as target-adaptive text-tabular inference, combining behavioral examples from the specific target with the current strategic state, the dialogue, and a representation from a frozen language-model Observer.
srWNrOWx2m.key_idea: Adapt prediction to each target using its few observed interactions and add a frozen LLM Observer's representation of the dialogue as extra features alongside structured state.
srWNrOWx2m.evidence: Bargaining and negotiation environments with a diverse population of independently built agents.

nj3z5EKYpn.one_liner: Trains one shared anonymous local policy for LLM agents so coordination emerges, via Swarm-Consistent Distillation.
nj3z5EKYpn.problem: Existing LLM multi-agent systems learn explicit roles, hierarchies, routing policies, or communication topologies that must be redefined when populations or conditions change.
nj3z5EKYpn.method: Waggle is a shared anonymous policy over bounded local views that jointly selects task actions, semantic communication, and local commitment updates. It is trained with Swarm-Consistent Distillation, which combines anonymous-orbit consistency with rollout-grounded prediction of the next local coordination field and adds no inference-time components.
nj3z5EKYpn.key_idea: Learn one reusable local law shared by interchangeable agents, so coordination forms and reorganizes from repeated local execution instead of explicit roles or global topology.
nj3z5EKYpn.evidence: Experiments across diverse coordination settings with changing populations and interaction budgets, including transfer without retraining and reorganization after counterevidence; specific benchmarks are not visible in the truncated abstract.
nj3z5EKYpn.claimed_gains: The learned law retains over 96% of substrate-specific oracle quality and transfers without retraining as populations and interaction budgets change.

Qn4HkwCuQH.one_liner: Hedge over constructed experts achieves sublinear regret for smoothed online regression with adversarial responses and bounded pseudo-dimension.
Qn4HkwCuQH.problem: The minimax optimal adaptive regret of smoothed online regression with bounded adversarial responses was an open problem posed in prior work (Blanchard et al., 2025).
Qn4HkwCuQH.method: Hedge-Cover aggregates a carefully constructed family of experts using Hedge, with a prior linking regret to the number of disagreements between a consistent selector and a target function, which is bounded using covariate smoothness. They also give a lower bound for linear predictors and revisit the well-specified setting with subGaussian response noise.
Qn4HkwCuQH.key_idea: Run Hedge over a constructed expert family with a prior tied to disagreements between a consistent selector and the target, bounded by covariate smoothness.
Qn4HkwCuQH.evidence: Theory only per the abstract: a regret upper bound for classes of bounded pseudo-dimension, a matching lower bound for linear predictors built on mutually orthogonal hyperplanes, and an extended lower bound for subGaussian noise.
Qn4HkwCuQH.claimed_gains: Regret of O~(sqrt(Pdim(F) C_cov T)) for classes with bounded pseudo-dimension, with a matching lower bound for linear predictors.

ui30anlEwI.one_liner: Constructs looped transformers that parse context-free languages exactly, bounding padding and loop counts, and studies learned parsing and scheduling.
ui30anlEwI.problem: Exact context-free parsing with looped transformers requires both organizing intermediate states in memory and scheduling updates that advance the computation.
ui30anlEwI.method: Gives theoretical constructions for strictly causal averaging-hard-attention transformers with storage and loop bounds, fixed parameters, constant width, logarithmic precision, and replayable parsing certificates, plus experiments on a separate learned parser with learned rankings under a fixed verifier and scheduling interventions.
ui30anlEwI.key_idea: Pair blank-padding memory layouts with looped updates to reach parsing, and treat reliable update scheduling (cyclic updates with bounded waiting) as a separate requirement from storage.
ui30anlEwI.evidence: Theoretical constructions for deterministic, unambiguous, and general context-free languages, and experiments on a learned parser including Palindrome inputs with learned rankings and scheduling interventions.
ui30anlEwI.claimed_gains: Fixed deterministic and unambiguous context-free languages admit O(n^2) and O(n^{log_2 7+eps}) blank padding respectively, with O(log^2 n) loops including initialization.

Bn02Ew9g82.one_liner: MedR2R compresses visual tokens in medical MLLMs via representative candidate selection followed by residual-based evidence refinement.
Bn02Ew9g82.problem: Existing acceleration methods for medical MLLMs preserve aggregate performance but can induce substantial instance-level prediction shifts, which is risky in safety-critical medical settings.
Bn02Ew9g82.method: A two-stage coarse-to-fine selection: after the vision encoder, build a representative candidate set under a relaxed token budget using pairwise cosine similarity that combines attention-derived global relevance with marginal representation gain, then refine the set after visual tokens are contextualized by an intermediate language-model layer.
Bn02Ew9g82.key_idea: Select visual tokens by both attention relevance and marginal representation gain to cover the whole visual space, then refine with residual-based evidence after contextualization.
Bn02Ew9g82.evidence: Medical MLLM tasks such as clinical visual question answering and medical image interpretation; specific datasets and models are not stated in the available text.
Bn02Ew9g82.claimed_gains: Improves the efficiency and reliability of medical MLLM inference while preserving strong task performance; no numbers stated.

wlcZJkBB6r.one_liner: KICS tests IV conditional exogeneity by comparing ordinary and IV-weighted kernel regression coefficients with a Wald-type test.
wlcZJkBB6r.problem: Existing tests of IV conditional exogeneity need structural restrictions such as linearity or discrete support, or auxiliary side information such as assignment mechanisms and negative controls.
wlcZJkBB6r.method: After removing the part of the candidate IV explained by observed covariates, it compares the coefficient systems of an ordinary kernel regression and a candidate-IV-induced weighted kernel regression. The estimated discrepancy is asymptotically normal, which enables a Wald-type test.
wlcZJkBB6r.key_idea: Under conditional exogeneity the ordinary and IV-weighted kernel regression coefficients coincide, so a significant discrepancy flags a violation.
wlcZJkBB6r.evidence: Population-level theory showing the coefficient systems coincide under the null and differ under detectable alternatives, plus synthetic and real-data-based experiments against specialized baselines.
wlcZJkBB6r.claimed_gains: Detects conditional exogeneity violations in flexible nonlinear settings, stays competitive where specialized baselines are favored, and gives real-data results consistent with prior IV assessments; no numbers stated.

UvUSTi1qjy.one_liner: Post-training quantization that refines an end-to-end-aligned loss surrogate with block-wise gradient descent after every 128-column block.
UvUSTi1qjy.problem: Closed-form second-order PTQ solvers approximate the global loss and freeze the Hessian across a layer, so it cannot refresh as the loss landscape shifts column by column, a problem the paper calls information misalignment.
UvUSTi1qjy.method: REAL-Q targets an end-to-end-aligned surrogate of the global loss and applies dynamic block-wise gradient descent after each block of 128 columns, with a sliding window for smooth cross-layer transitions to limit error propagation.
UvUSTi1qjy.key_idea: Gradient descent on an end-to-end-aligned surrogate after each column block refreshes the loss information that a frozen layer-wise Hessian keeps static.
UvUSTi1qjy.evidence: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B/8B/32B across twelve weight-only and weight-activation settings, measured by KL loss and downstream tasks.
UvUSTi1qjy.claimed_gains: Lowest KL loss and first rank on downstream tasks in most of twelve settings; the TL;DR states up to about 49% lower KL divergence than GuidedQuant.

wzHqe9ehvx.one_liner: Learns to select the constraint subset needing relaxation in infeasible MILPs, using a tripartite loss and constraint-centric representation.
wzHqe9ehvx.problem: Infeasibility relaxation of real-world MILPs at scale is an unresolved bottleneck, even though learning-based methods already accelerate solving of feasible ones.
wzHqe9ehvx.method: L-IR casts relaxation as constraint support set coverage and is trained with a quality-weighted binary classification loss, a complete-support ranking loss, and a coverage loss that truncates ranked subsets at inference, using a constraint-centric geometric representation of conflict topology.
wzHqe9ehvx.key_idea: Predict the constraint support set that needs relaxation, rank complete supports early, and truncate by learned coverage to give the solver a reduced problem.
wzHqe9ehvx.evidence: A new benchmark of 20,000 infeasible MILPs across 580 problem classes, evaluated against Gurobi, with generalization experiments (abstract truncated).
wzHqe9ehvx.claimed_gains: Accelerates Gurobi by up to 4.8x with matched or superior quality, with a mean primal gap of 2-3% across all instances.

hu5mtofNd4.one_liner: Localizes RLVR solution-space contraction to the initial computational entrance on Countdown, restoring diversity by layer interpolation.
hu5mtofNd4.problem: RLVR raises pass@1 but contracts the policy's solution space, and it is unclear whether breadth is lost in accessing a solution family or in executing it.
hu5mtofNd4.method: Countdown solutions are enumerated into entrance families defined by the first operand and operator, and PPO on Qwen2.5-3B and GRPO on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct are compared before and after training using per-token likelihood shifts, entrance-prefix supply, and layer interpolation.
hu5mtofNd4.key_idea: Separate access from execution by enumerating entrance families: contraction concentrates at the entrance, so alternative solutions stay executable but are no longer initiated.
hu5mtofNd4.evidence: Countdown task with PPO on Qwen2.5-3B and GRPO on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct.
hu5mtofNd4.claimed_gains: Solution coverage falls by up to 67%; per-token likelihood shifts are 11x-16x larger before the first arithmetic operation; an entrance prefix raises completion from 0.018 to 0.212 under PPO; layer interpolation raises coverage by 37% with pass@1 of 0.305 versus 0.278.

Bha1xKd91E.one_liner: Chain-of-exploration EQA agent that iteratively reasons, picks tools for geometric evidence, and decides where to explore next.
Bha1xKd91E.problem: Off-the-shelf VLMs have limited 3D reasoning in embodied question answering, causing inaccurate evidence retrieval, inefficient exploration, and incorrect answers.
Bha1xKd91E.method: The agent reasons over current observations and history, selects tools to acquire geometric evidence, and chooses where to explore; it is trained by supervised fine-tuning on EQA-RT-Train, built by an automatic pipeline that generates 3D reasoning trajectories, followed by an evidence-grounded stage (truncated).
Bha1xKd91E.key_idea: Interleave exploration, tool-based spatial evidence acquisition, and question answering in one iterative reasoning loop trained on generated 3D reasoning trajectories.
Bha1xKd91E.evidence: The EQA-RT dataset of 18K tasks, with EQA-RT-Seen and EQA-RT-Unseen test sets; results are cut off in the abstract.

9M6YO3p9H8.one_liner: Replaces sequential Top-1 adaptive tokenization with one global Top-K selection when importance scores are monotone along the hierarchy.
9M6YO3p9H8.problem: Sequential Top-1 refinement over a quadtree or octree takes 53-80% of each training step on the authors' 2D benchmarks, exceeding the model's own runtime.
9M6YO3p9H8.method: When ancestor scores are no lower than descendants', the hierarchy has heap order, so one global Top-K selection equals K sequential Top-1 refinements; non-monotone metrics are made monotone with bottom-up sum or max reductions.
9M6YO3p9H8.key_idea: Monotone scores give the hierarchy heap order, so a single global Top-K selection exactly reproduces K sequential Top-1 refinements.
9M6YO3p9H8.evidence: High-resolution 2D segmentation, large-scale 3D point clouds, and multichannel weather data.
9M6YO3p9H8.claimed_gains: Up to 3.73x training and 2.56x inference throughput over sequential refinement on 2D data, and 1.18x and 2.06x over a dense-voxel baseline (abstract truncated after this point).

bd13kcqzKr.one_liner: Traversing image tokens in Hilbert order enables power-of-four multiscale KV-cache summary compression for autoregressive image generation.
bd13kcqzKr.problem: Raster and diagonal zigzag token orderings in autoregressive image generation admit trivial worst-case spatial locality and incur high attention compute and KV-cache memory costs.
bd13kcqzKr.method: CHARM generates image tokens along a space-filling Hilbert curve achieving optimal beta=1/2 Holder spatial locality and partitions sequences into power-of-four intervals corresponding to multiscale 2D square regions. Replacing each completed square region with a single learned summary KV-cache entry lowers attention complexity to O(n^2 log n) and KV-cache space to O(log n).
bd13kcqzKr.key_idea: Order autoregressive image tokens along a Hilbert curve and recursively compress completed power-of-four spatial square regions into single learned KV-cache summary tokens.
bd13kcqzKr.evidence: Supported by beta-Holder locality proofs comparing Hilbert against raster and zigzag orders and class-conditional ImageNet generation experiments across model scales at 256 and 512 resolutions.
bd13kcqzKr.claimed_gains: CHARM reduces attention computation to O(n^2 log n) and KV-cache space to O(log n), while its recursively compressed 1.5B model achieves 1.64 FID at 256 resolution and 1.87 FID at 512 resolution on class-conditional ImageNet.

MF0pdf5MtY.one_liner: Measuring certificate interaction width and refutation witness size characterizes asymmetric verification requirements for optimal transport plans.
MF0pdf5MtY.problem: Computing a transport coupling does not establish how much evidence certifies its near-optimality or refutes it within a declared proof language.
MF0pdf5MtY.method: The paper defines candidate-specific verification profiles using positive-certificate width and replayable negative-witness size. VerifyOT combines certificate and refutation reasoning to return Certified, Refuted, or Unknown.
MF0pdf5MtY.key_idea: Measure positive certificate interaction width separately from negative witness size, using local Kantorovich duals and four-cycle improvements to verify transport candidates.
MF0pdf5MtY.evidence: Parity-family theory and theorem-aligned experiments establish width regimes, four-cycle bounds, and persistence of positive obstructions under Wasserstein perturbations.

DQRjN6cKk5.one_liner: Adversarial training across Gaussian-mixture tasks lets deep linear transformers transfer robustness through clean in-context demonstrations.
DQRjN6cKk5.problem: Adversarial training is costly to repeat per task, and robustness transfer to unseen tasks without further training lacks a theoretical foundation.
DQRjN6cKk5.method: The study adversarially trains sufficiently deep linear transformers across Gaussian-mixture classification tasks, then adapts to unseen tasks through clean demonstrations. It analyzes asymptotic robust Bayes error, gradient-flow convergence, the accuracy–robustness trade-off, and demonstration complexity.
DQRjN6cKk5.key_idea: Adversarially pretrain a linear transformer across tasks, then use clean in-context demonstrations to obtain robust classification on unseen Gaussian mixtures.
DQRjN6cKk5.evidence: Theory shows asymptotic attainment of robust Bayes error for a Gaussian-mixture task family, unlike standard training, and analyzes convergence and demonstration complexity.

cdEhL4sZlE.one_liner: Combining dense BEV states with persistent motion queries forecasts roadside occupancy through selective updates to moving regions.
cdEhL4sZlE.problem: Roadside occupancy forecasting must preserve global scene structure while modeling sparse local motion, which existing forecasting paradigms struggle to combine.
cdEhL4sZlE.method: InfraWorld initializes persistent queries from observed motion and updates a dense BEV state using short- and long-term temporal fusion. It refines the queries and injects confidence-weighted query information into corresponding BEV tokens.
cdEhL4sZlE.key_idea: Maintain global context in a dense BEV state while motion-initialized persistent queries inject confidence-weighted updates into corresponding dynamic regions.
cdEhL4sZlE.evidence: The abstract states experiments on InfraOcc and Occ3D--nus datasets but truncates before reporting their results.

WQYorHdT8x.one_liner: Diffusion bridge critics model inverse return distributions and analytically integrate them for distributional reinforcement learning.
WQYorHdT8x.problem: Diffusion-based reinforcement learning underexplores critics, while value-distribution collapse and discretization errors can impair value estimation.
WQYorHdT8x.method: DBC models the inverse cumulative distribution function of returns with a diffusion bridge to avoid Gaussian collapse. An analytic integral formula addresses discretization errors, and the critic can integrate into existing reinforcement-learning frameworks.
WQYorHdT8x.key_idea: Represent the return inverse cumulative distribution function with a diffusion bridge and use analytic integration to address discretization error.
WQYorHdT8x.evidence: The paper derives an analytic integral formula and states experimental results on MuJoCo, with the supplied abstract truncated before details.

ZHMZ4hBKDn.one_liner: Evaluating pipeline-native drama outputs with traceable human annotations and specialist agent judges links defects across production stages.
ZHMZ4hBKDn.problem: Isolated video benchmarks and manually constructed inputs obscure whether production defects originate locally or propagate from earlier stages.
ZHMZ4hBKDn.method: DramaChain Bench evaluates outputs from storyboard design through multi-episode delivery using a multidimensional schema, a generation agent, and a human-labeling system. Its automated judge combines a master–sub-agent architecture, specialist modules, and iterative tool use.
ZHMZ4hBKDn.key_idea: Evaluate native outputs throughout drama production with stage-spanning dimensions, localized human defect annotations, and tool-using specialist judges.
ZHMZ4hBKDn.evidence: Evaluation includes 5,569 reference items with three independent assessments each, 63 leaf dimensions, and 37 generation models.
ZHMZ4hBKDn.claimed_gains: DramaChain Agentic Judge achieves a mean model-level PLCC of 0.918 against human scores.

49ifMmUfPT.one_liner: Extracting modality-specific facts and applying explicit rubrics evaluates video prompt enhancers without rendering videos.
49ifMmUfPT.problem: Video-based prompt-enhancer evaluation is costly and confounds enhancer quality with downstream generator behavior.
49ifMmUfPT.method: WanPEBench directly evaluates text-to-video, image-to-video, and reference-to-video prompt enhancement using expert-verified cases and visual assets. Its evaluation framework combines modality-aware fact extraction with rubric-based assessment.
49ifMmUfPT.key_idea: Judge enhanced prompts directly against extracted multimodal facts and explicit criteria instead of using generated videos as a proxy.
49ifMmUfPT.evidence: The benchmark includes 1,100 expert-verified cases, 1,005 visual assets, 35 fine-grained tasks, and 24 criteria, with evaluations of representative prompt enhancers and human validation.

nnWeEWkYzp.one_liner: Value-order Decomposition suppresses category, defect, and domain information to align normal and anomalous representations across domains.
nnWeEWkYzp.problem: Residual feature spaces align normal samples but leave anomalies entangled with object categories, defect types, and domains.
nnWeEWkYzp.method: Value-order Decomposition disentangles and suppresses category-, defect-, and domain-specific feature information. It aligns samples within normal and abnormal groups while preserving separation between the groups.
nnWeEWkYzp.key_idea: Suppress category-, defect-, and domain-specific information while aligning normal and abnormal feature groups separately.

gNmU2oeP2a.one_liner: VA-Bench evaluates VLMs through metric robot actions, chosen viewpoints, and feedback-based correction in closed-loop manipulation.
gNmU2oeP2a.problem: Visual question answering and learned visuomotor-policy evaluations do not establish whether general-purpose VLMs can translate spatial understanding into physical actions.
gNmU2oeP2a.method: VA-Bench supplies task goals and visual demonstrations, requiring models to infer geometry and generate metric robot actions without task-specific policies or privileged spatial inputs. Models can choose viewpoints, update actions from feedback, and face geometry changes that preserve the task procedure.
gNmU2oeP2a.key_idea: Test spatial reasoning through closed-loop metric action generation with active perception and controlled geometric shifts.
gNmU2oeP2a.evidence: Across 14 manipulation tasks, VLMs show strong target identification but weaker spatial grounding and correction, with active-perception controls.
gNmU2oeP2a.claimed_gains: The highest overall task success rate is 53.9%, and active perception improves success by 7.86--23.93% over controls.

WBhnid2JvS.one_liner: Barycentric Procrustes alignment maps model representations into a shared space for comparing individual inputs.
WBhnid2JvS.problem: Representational symmetries obscure model equivalence, while dataset-level similarity metrics hide input-specific convergence and divergence.
WBhnid2JvS.method: The framework uses the Generalized Procrustes Algorithm to remove nuisance symmetries and construct shared embedding spaces across models. It measures instance-level agreement across vision, language, and brain representations and aligns unimodal models for cross-modal comparison.
WBhnid2JvS.key_idea: Align many representation spaces to a common barycenter while removing nuisance symmetries, then compare embeddings stimulus by stimulus.
WBhnid2JvS.evidence: Analyses cover vision and language model families, brain representations across individuals and cortical regions, and image-text similarity against human judgments.

IdjVqbg07c.one_liner: Functional scaling laws decompose checkpoint-averaged loss into signal learning and injection-time-dependent noise retention.
IdjVqbg07c.problem: The effects of model merging on learning dynamics and its dependence on learning-rate schedules are insufficiently characterized.
IdjVqbg07c.method: The paper derives a functional scaling law for fractional averaging in power-law kernel regression under general learning-rate schedules. Its signal-noise decomposition guides tail and power averaging and checkpoint density choices.
IdjVqbg07c.key_idea: Model averaging retains less-trained checkpoints while affecting noise according to when it enters the checkpoint sequence.
IdjVqbg07c.evidence: Controlled kernel-regression SGD experiments test scaling rates, averaging windows, and checkpoint counts, while LLM pretraining tests cross-schedule predictions without refitting.

7y7zmkpsqR.one_liner: LVOmniBench uses manually annotated long audio-video recordings to test omnimodal models' cross-modal comprehension.
7y7zmkpsqR.problem: Short-clip evaluations fail to reflect applications requiring understanding of audio-video recordings lasting tens of minutes.
7y7zmkpsqR.method: LVOmniBench selects and manually annotates long videos from open platforms. Its questions test long-term memory, temporal localization, fine-grained understanding, and multimodal perception.
7y7zmkpsqR.key_idea: Evaluate cross-modal comprehension using question-answer pairs over manually selected and annotated long-form audio-video recordings.
7y7zmkpsqR.evidence: The benchmark evaluates OmniLLMs on 275 videos lasting 10 to 90 minutes with 1,014 question-answer pairs.
7y7zmkpsqR.claimed_gains: Open-source models generally score below 40% accuracy, while Gemini 3.8-Flash reaches approximately 69%.

1qf1fepoTe.one_liner: Paired replay transitions impose relative Bellman constraints on critics to supervise value differences in residual reinforcement learning.
1qf1fepoTe.problem: Absolute-return targets only indirectly supervise the small value differences that determine useful corrections to frozen robot policies.
1qf1fepoTe.method: ReVRA adds relative Bellman constraints alongside standard temporal-difference learning. It pairs replay transitions to supervise value differences within the existing critic for residual policy adaptation.
1qf1fepoTe.key_idea: Relative Bellman constraints explicitly train critic value differences from paired replay transitions alongside ordinary temporal-difference targets.
1qf1fepoTe.evidence: Evaluation includes simulated locomotion, manipulation, VLA-based adaptation, and real-robot manipulation under a limited interaction budget.

7qB4ByzzX3.one_liner: Decentralized agents discover and exchange policy-controlled context assets through semantic discovery, safety gates, and ledger-backed evidence.
7qB4ByzzX3.problem: Private agents cannot safely collaborate through protocols that assume known partners, shared visibility, or trust across ownership boundaries.
7qB4ByzzX3.method: OPAC treats reusable context assets as the unit of cooperation under ownership-aware access control. AEP implements semantic discovery, demand-driven coordination, safety-gated asset exchange, and ledger-backed evidence derivation while distinguishing physical from local cognitive topology.
7qB4ByzzX3.key_idea: Agents discover task-relevant collaborators and exchange auditable context assets under ownership and integration policies despite partial network knowledge.

GwAaQFbo2m.one_liner: Noise-unconditioned scores turn generation into gradient ascent on one fixed density objective with conditional fidelity and diversity guarantees.
GwAaQFbo2m.problem: A fixed denoising objective needs guarantees that ascent reaches meaningful data while preserving diverse outcomes across initializations.
GwAaQFbo2m.method: The paper analyzes gradient ascent on empirical and population multi-scale Gaussian-mixture objectives. It derives manifold-proximity and regional-coverage results, identifies an affine non-memorization regime, and supports controllable generation through penalties on the same objective.
GwAaQFbo2m.key_idea: Noise unconditioning produces one fixed score field whose ascent dynamics and source-sink identity govern data proximity and regional coverage.
GwAaQFbo2m.evidence: Conditional theory covers manifold proximity, finite-resolution coverage, and affine non-memorization, while experiments examine large-step guidance and downstream generalization.

UpdcNE6HLZ.one_liner: A target-specific information scale supports regret bounds and adaptive exploration for counterfactually fair causal logistic bandits.
UpdcNE6HLZ.problem: Factual rewards may not identify counterfactual feasibility, and prior analyses lack appropriate coverage assumptions or matching lower bounds.
UpdcNE6HLZ.method: The paper establishes the necessity of coverage and defines a target-specific information scale under full-rank pooled factual covariance. It develops both a scale-tuned explore-then-exploit procedure and an adaptive algorithm that does not require the scale.
UpdcNE6HLZ.key_idea: Pooled factual covariance and a target-specific information scale characterize the exploration needed to learn rewards and counterfactual feasibility.
UpdcNE6HLZ.evidence: Theory gives a linear-loss impossibility without coverage and lower and upper bounds with a common T^(2/3) leading dependence under the stated full-rank condition.

ezxqO1qsZD.one_liner: Shared autoencoder latents and a flow transformer unify cloud removal across spectral, temporal, and optional SAR inputs.
ezxqO1qsZD.problem: Dataset-specific cloud removal models transfer poorly across sensors, spectral bands, and observation configurations.
ezxqO1qsZD.method: GeoCR adds compact input and output stems around frozen RGB autoencoder trunks to share latents across sensing domains. One flow transformer models clean RGB and non-RGB latents conditioned on cloudy observations and optional SAR tokens, supporting direct inference or LoRA adaptation.
ezxqO1qsZD.key_idea: Adaptable autoencoder stems map heterogeneous observations into shared latents that one conditional flow transformer uses for cloud removal.
ezxqO1qsZD.evidence: GeoCR pretrains on ten datasets with 883,331 cloud-free targets and evaluates held-out full-band and RGB-only splits, including SEN12MS-CR, Sen2_MTC_New, and CUHK-CR2.

EHUjd6KEst.one_liner: Role-labeled visual evidence tokens and adaptive attention routing guide a frozen segmenter from video reasoning.
EHUjd6KEst.problem: Existing MLLM-based reasoning video segmentation often requires costly alignment that couples language-model training to a downstream segmenter.
EHUjd6KEst.method: ReVEAL inserts target, background, and distractor evidence tokens into video reasoning and dynamically aggregates their video attention across layers. Training on ReVEAL-47K uses contrastive attention grounding, while inference fuses role-specific evidence to guide frozen SAM2 masks.
EHUjd6KEst.key_idea: Role-specific evidence tokens and learned layer routing convert MLLM attention into grounding signals for a frozen segmentation model.
EHUjd6KEst.evidence: Experiments on five benchmarks compare ReVEAL with alignment-free and alignment-based methods after training on ReVEAL-47K.

GOFjiCsATQ.one_liner: Curvature-selected forget updates projected away from retain gradients target retrained-model behavior during language-model unlearning.
GOFjiCsATQ.problem: Unlearning updates ignore joint forget-retain curvature, while suppression-based evaluation can reward overshooting the behavior of retrained models.
GOFjiCsATQ.method: CROP restricts forget ascent to directions with high forget curvature and low retain curvature, projects updates orthogonal to the retain gradient, and anchors on retain descent. It selects operating points by retrain-profile distance or a calibrated oracle-free rule.
GOFjiCsATQ.key_idea: Forget ascent stays within a curvature-selected subspace, removes the retain-gradient component, and combines with retain descent.
GOFjiCsATQ.evidence: TOFU uses validation-author checkpoint selection and held-out-author scoring, while MUSE compares retrain proximity for two 7B families; TOFU gains carry a utility cost.
GOFjiCsATQ.claimed_gains: On TOFU, CROP beats RMU on held-out forget quality on two of three seeds, while its oracle-best analysis checkpoints reach KS D 0.045–0.0725 from retraining over six seeds, with independent-retrain spread 0.0225–0.050.

x2fvQXFKey.one_liner: Teacher velocity anchoring and successor-state distribution matching jointly distill preference-aligned diffusion models along student trajectories.
x2fvQXFKey.problem: Few-step distillation can weaken preference alignment, while sequential alignment transfer and distillation can undo earlier capabilities.
x2fvQXFKey.method: OPDMD anchors student velocity to the teacher at selected student states and applies distribution-matching corrections at successor states. A single transition-aware mean-squared-error objective scales each correction by the transition span.
x2fvQXFKey.key_idea: A transition-aware objective couples teacher velocity anchors with distribution-matching corrections on successive states of student-generated trajectories.
x2fvQXFKey.evidence: Experiments use SD-3.5-Medium with GRPO-aligned expert teachers to assess preservation of aligned capabilities.

af6VzO3o3W.one_liner: A self-calibrated trajectory reward grants full credit only for correct answers that terminate within policy-derived length thresholds.
af6VzO3o3W.problem: Reasoning models can compute correct answers yet fail to express them before deployment token budgets expire.
af6VzO3o3W.method: R3 grants full reward only when a correct trajectory terminates within a threshold tracking the policy's recent correct-solution lengths. It requires no auxiliary judge, token-level labels, or curriculum and uses a matched correctness-only control to isolate termination effects.
af6VzO3o3W.key_idea: The reward conditions correctness credit on termination before a threshold adapted from recent correct-solution lengths.
af6VzO3o3W.evidence: Experiments compare R3 with six specialized efficiency methods across budget-dataset settings and include a correctness-only control and MATH token-use evaluation.
af6VzO3o3W.claimed_gains: R3 scores higher in 81 of 90 budget-dataset comparisons against six specialized efficiency methods while generating the fewest tokens on MATH.

3bUXNg2c4A.one_liner: Head-wise query steering uses context prototypes to adaptively balance visual, prefilled textual, and generated information during decoding.
3bUXNg2c4A.problem: Hallucination mitigation that primarily boosts visual evidence overlooks how models coordinate multiple context sources during generation.
3bUXNg2c4A.method: AIMS constructs compact prototypes for visual, prefilled textual, and generated contexts and estimates their affinity to the current query. These affinities determine head-wise steering weights that modify query representations without training or auxiliary forward passes.
3bUXNg2c4A.key_idea: Query affinities to context-domain prototypes determine head-wise steering directions for adaptive integration of visual and textual evidence.
3bUXNg2c4A.evidence: The abstract reports analyses of intrinsic vision-attending tendencies and textual-context contributions to hallucination mitigation, but provides no completed experimental details.

7hs0vjh7L4.one_liner: Small-model reinforcement-learning shifts guide a single large-model update through low-rank gradient probing and reward-based selection.
7hs0vjh7L4.problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards becomes computationally expensive as reasoning-model scale increases.
7hs0vjh7L4.method: OptScout extracts source-model policy shifts and converts them into target-specific updates using low-rank gradient probing and cross-split consistency filtering. Forward-only reward evaluation chooses the direction and magnitude, stops scouting when transfer stalls, and applies the selected target update once.
7hs0vjh7L4.key_idea: Early small-model policy shifts supply candidate large-model updates, filtered for consistency and selected by forward-only reward evaluation.
7hs0vjh7L4.evidence: Experiments span source-side reinforcement-learning algorithms, target-model settings, and multiple reasoning benchmarks, with direct target-side reinforcement learning as a comparator.
7hs0vjh7L4.claimed_gains: OptScout reports up to a 6.32× end-to-end speedup while achieving higher average performance than direct target-side reinforcement learning.

ii8v50vtyq.one_liner: Learned 3D anchor centers and radii ground Gaussian queries during image aggregation and local Gaussian decoding.
ii8v50vtyq.problem: Purely latent Gaussian queries can decode points scattered across distant scene regions instead of coherent local structures.
ii8v50vtyq.method: LocusGS attaches a progressively refined 3D center and support radius to each query. Anchor-to-ray bias directs multi-view feature aggregation, while anchor-centered decoding organizes each query's Gaussians within a local region.
ii8v50vtyq.key_idea: Explicit center-radius anchors guide query interactions, image-ray attention, and local Gaussian generation across decoder layers.
ii8v50vtyq.evidence: View-synthesis benchmarks compare rendering with query-based Gaussian token baselines under equal Gaussian budgets, and analyses inspect anchor layouts and Gaussian distributions.

O7YYoS6NqB.one_liner: Grounding paths from interpretable link predictors supervise query rewriting, subgraph retrieval, and language-model reasoning for knowledge graph completion.
O7YYoS6NqB.problem: Knowledge graph datasets lack retrieval and reasoning supervision needed for native language models to compete with traditional completion methods.
O7YYoS6NqB.method: PARR samples grounding paths from interpretable link predictors to augment subgraph retrieval, supervise a Rewriter LLM, and distill structural knowledge into a Reasoner LLM through chain-of-thought training. Reinforcement-learning fine-tuning uses soft verifiable rewards tailored to knowledge graph completion.
O7YYoS6NqB.key_idea: Link-predictor grounding paths provide shared supervision for retrieval, query rewriting, and chain-of-thought knowledge graph reasoning.
O7YYoS6NqB.evidence: Experiments compare PARR with discriminative and language-model completion methods across knowledge graph datasets in transductive and inductive settings.

GFLtNn4mKs.one_liner: Auxiliary reset variables and topological gluing embed stochastic hybrid systems into continuous latent stochastic differential equations.
GFLtNn4mKs.problem: Stochastic hybrid systems combine continuous dynamics with random resets that introduce explicit integral reset terms into probability evolution.
GFLtNn4mKs.method: The approach encodes reset-kernel branches with auxiliary variables, turning resets deterministic so topological gluing and Euclidean embedding can produce a continuous latent process. A distribution-matching loss trains one latent SDE without mode labels, segmentation, or event-based simulation.
GFLtNn4mKs.key_idea: Auxiliary variables make reset branches deterministic, enabling topological gluing and higher-dimensional embedding into a continuous latent stochastic process.
GFLtNn4mKs.evidence: An embedding theorem shows that the embedded probability evolution no longer requires explicit reset terms in the hybrid Fokker-Planck equation.

iKbk6CgL1y.one_liner: On-policy suffix branching and branch-weighted aggregation expand high-return trajectory coverage while analyzing policy-gradient bias.
iKbk6CgL1y.problem: Finite on-policy samples can miss rare high-return trajectories, but tree expansion changes state visitation and can bias gradient estimates.
iKbk6CgL1y.method: OPTS samples new policy suffixes at visited states and selects expansions using estimated performance differences. TTPO uses branch-weighted tree statistics, with unbiased chain-expectation recovery when choices and weights precede outgoing samples, plus bias analysis for adaptive expansion.
iKbk6CgL1y.key_idea: Policy-sampled suffix branches extend visited trajectories, while branch-weighted statistics control how their altered state visitation enters policy-gradient estimates.
iKbk6CgL1y.evidence: The Branch Aggregation Lemma, conditional monotonic-return analysis, adaptive-bias bounds, and fixed-position branching measurements support the approach.
iKbk6CgL1y.claimed_gains: With fixed-position branching, TTPG's measured relative bias decreases from 0.456 to 0.400.

J2V6tPOCod.one_liner: Entity-level semantic routing associates street-view evidence with satellite regions despite uncertain camera poses.
J2V6tPOCod.problem: Cross-view semantic segmentation commonly assumes precise registration that positioning and pose-estimation errors make unreliable.
J2V6tPOCod.method: CVRoute treats satellite regions and street-view observations as cross-view entities and learns their semantic relationships. It routes street-view evidence to relevant regions in the satellite spatial reference under uncertain geometry.
J2V6tPOCod.key_idea: Learned semantic relationships route street-view entity evidence to satellite regions without requiring exact pixel correspondence.
