TjInKkUYCl.one_liner: Spatial attention bias, shared decoder tokens, normal-consistent queries, and Poisson-inspired supervision align set-based 3D autoencoders with geometry.
TjInKkUYCl.problem: VecSet VAE latents suffer global attention sinks, periodic retrieval, inconsistent normal inputs, and missing distance-field-to-normal supervision.
TjInKkUYCl.method: Align-VAE adds shared decoder tokens and distance-biased cross-attention to predicted anchors, while removing normals from encoder queries but retaining them in keys and values. A screened Poisson-inspired regularizer supervises surface values and normal-direction derivatives without increasing the per-shape code.
TjInKkUYCl.key_idea: Global decoder tokens and anchor-biased retrieval separate global computation from local geometry, while normal-consistent queries and derivative supervision constrain field prediction.
TjInKkUYCl.evidence: Experiments compare Align-VAE with a standard VecSet VAE on the ABO dataset using Chamfer distance.
TjInKkUYCl.claimed_gains: On ABO, Align-VAE reduces Chamfer distance by 26.6% compared with the standard VecSet VAE.

ehBjrUQgya.one_liner: Counterfactual replay and Shapley credits train an evaluator to allocate terminal diffusion rewards across denoising transitions.
ehBjrUQgya.problem: Terminal preference rewards do not specify how to assign credit among interacting denoising decisions.
ehBjrUQgya.method: The method replaces selected stochastic transitions with deterministic updates and replays continuations using a fixed policy and indexed noise tape to derive Shapley credits. An evaluator initialized for noisy-latent preference perception learns offline credits and terminal gains, then weights terminal group advantages with bounded nonnegative step weights.
ehBjrUQgya.key_idea: Counterfactual transition replacement defines Shapley credit labels that train an evaluator to distribute terminal advantages across denoising steps.
ehBjrUQgya.evidence: Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium experiments evaluate GenEval, step-credit error, and permutation controls while retaining the same learned terminal evaluator.
ehBjrUQgya.claimed_gains: GenEval improves from 0.704 to 0.753, and latent initialization reduces step-credit mean absolute error from 0.028 to 0.019.

fMZDImfUwg.one_liner: Cognitively grounded video tasks probe multimodal memory retention, interference, source grounding, and long-sequence abstraction.
fMZDImfUwg.problem: Existing video benchmarks emphasize perception and reasoning without systematically testing memory fidelity or resistance to interference.
fMZDImfUwg.method: M3Eval provides tasks grounded in cognitive psychology for evaluating multiple dimensions of multimodal memory. It probes parallel video streams, source grounding, visual-to-symbolic abstraction, and indexed comparison over long sequences.
fMZDImfUwg.key_idea: Controlled video tasks isolate memory dimensions through parallel streams, source attribution, interference, and long-sequence comparisons.
fMZDImfUwg.evidence: Experiments across representative multimodal models reveal parallel-stream entanglement, nonhuman interference patterns, stronger spatial than temporal source grounding, and abstraction difficulties.

dWP5fKrb4O.one_liner: Reusable demonstration-derived skills combine separate execution and transition experts for embodied continual learning.
dWP5fKrb4O.problem: Feature drift compounds into behavioral errors under closed-loop control, while existing methods inadequately organize skills for reuse across evolving tasks.
dWP5fKrb4O.method: SCE uses Compositional Skill Grounding to decompose demonstrations into a reusable skill base. Dual Execution-and-Transition Experts compose these skills for new tasks, assigning one branch to execution and another to transitions.
dWP5fKrb4O.key_idea: Demonstration-derived skills form a reusable base, with separate experts controlling within-skill execution and between-skill transitions.
dWP5fKrb4O.evidence: LIBERO and real-world manipulation experiments measure retention and task performance, accompanied by feature-drift analyses and ablations.

n5X0esk5OQ.one_liner: Cumulative tactile motion and transient differences provide contact-stage guidance to coordinate slow and fast action experts.
n5X0esk5OQ.problem: Stage-agnostic tactile feedback cannot adapt action generation and local refinement to distinct stages of contact-rich tasks.
n5X0esk5OQ.method: GuidedVTLA combines proactive contact-stage guidance from optical tactile dynamics with reactive tactile refinement in a slow-fast architecture. Shared guidance coordinates both experts, while the slow expert routes a stage-aware mixture of experts.
n5X0esk5OQ.key_idea: Cumulative tactile motion and transient differences encode contact-stage guidance that coordinates slow generation and fast refinement.
n5X0esk5OQ.evidence: The abstract reports an analysis of optical tactile temporal dynamics linking cumulative motion and transient differences to contact-stage guidance.

g7rpNmtiER.one_liner: Watermark-key scores on original and recovered unwatermarked tokens predict signal retention through rendering and image processing.
g7rpNmtiER.problem: Watermark retention differs across autoregressive image models, but existing evaluations require generating watermarked images for every model-watermark combination.
g7rpNmtiER.method: RenderGap defines a retained-signal metric and approximates it from unwatermarked generations. It compares generated tokens with tokens recovered from rendered or processed images and scores both using the watermark key.
g7rpNmtiER.key_idea: Watermark-key score differences between generated and recovered tokens estimate signal retention without generating watermarked images.
g7rpNmtiER.evidence: A conditional detection-success theorem and independently calibrated experiments cover autoregressive image models with JPEG, blur, and tokenizer variants.
g7rpNmtiER.claimed_gains: Median absolute relative prediction errors are 0.009–0.073 across JPEG, blur, and tokenizer variants.

IEaivqYB87.one_liner: Preceding-decision accumulator growth recovers exact reach-weighted averages for outcome-sampling counterfactual regret minimization.
IEaivqYB87.problem: Outcome-sampling averaging rules can differ from the exact reach-weighted average covered by CFR's guarantee, increasing exploitability.
IEaivqYB87.method: The paper derives an information set's accumulated weight between visits from growth in the exact-average sum at the player's preceding decision for the action leading there. Reading that growth on each visit and at termination returns the exact average.
IEaivqYB87.key_idea: Accumulator growth at a preceding player decision supplies the missed reach weights needed for exact averaging between sampled visits.
IEaivqYB87.evidence: Experiments compare averaging rules on four games through ten million iterations, and a proof identifies exact between-visit weights from existing solver sums.
IEaivqYB87.claimed_gains: On three of four games, existing averages are ten to just over fifty percent more exploitable after a hundred thousand iterations and two to eight times as exploitable after ten million, while opponent-traversal updates leave OpenSpiel's rule at most two percent worse on average.

m0Q3j9Qhj6.one_liner: Labeled reference images calibrate frozen expert contributions and comparison geometry for open-domain fine-grained recognition.
m0Q3j9Qhj6.problem: Domain-specific fine-grained recognition requires repeated supervision and adaptation as domain coverage grows.
m0Q3j9Qhj6.method: A training-free framework uses labeled references to calibrate frozen experts for visual comparison and image-name matching, with within-class feature statistics defining visual geometry. Held-out reference predictions set the balance between visual and semantic evidence.
m0Q3j9Qhj6.key_idea: Use reference predictions and within-class statistics to calibrate expert weights, visual geometry, and visual-semantic evidence balance.
m0Q3j9Qhj6.evidence: Analysis of pretrained visual models finds uneven domain capabilities and complementary strengths; specific datasets and quantitative evaluations are not stated.

8K3gt4rfjA.one_liner: Architecture-aligned activation spikes and plateaus reveal how interleaved linear and full attention organize hybrid-model internal dynamics.
8K3gt4rfjA.problem: How hybrid linear and full attention reshape massive activations and their functional role remains poorly understood.
8K3gt4rfjA.method: The study characterizes pre-attention spikes and inter-spike plateaus through architectural comparisons, controlled pretraining, and output-gate changes. It also proposes reference-conditioned spike connection for retrieval without retraining.
8K3gt4rfjA.key_idea: Relate activation spikes before full attention and intervening plateaus to attention placement and output-gate effects in hybrid architectures.
8K3gt4rfjA.evidence: Evidence spans five linear-attention architectures, six hybridization configurations, five input domains, 12 public checkpoints of 1.2B–397B parameters, and controlled Gated DeltaNet pretraining up to 1.3B.

bcyzcxbGMI.one_liner: Objective tokens condition item generation, while specialist distillation and listwise policy optimization allocate recommendation positions across objectives.
bcyzcxbGMI.problem: Merging distinct engagement objectives into one generative recommendation signal creates conflicts where improving one objective degrades another.
bcyzcxbGMI.method: MOGR emits an objective token before each item's semantic IDs and distills objective-specific specialists into a shared decoder. Listwise policy optimization uses a concave reward to choose objectives across ranking positions, with an objective-aware codebook for industrial logs.
bcyzcxbGMI.key_idea: Generate an objective token before each item and optimize complete lists to allocate positions among separately distilled objectives.
bcyzcxbGMI.evidence: Experiments on Kwai26 compare Recall@512 across three objectives with MD-CBS and TIGER, alongside a reward-model proxy comparison for LGPO.
bcyzcxbGMI.claimed_gains: MOGR achieves a minimum relative gain of 4.3% over MD-CBS and 20.6% over TIGER across three objectives on Kwai26.

CDoist18Ex.one_liner: Spatial-cue-aware presentation and competing-hypothesis selection guide frozen VLMs toward relevant remote-sensing evidence.
CDoist18Ex.problem: Making small regions accessible in ultra-high-resolution images does not ensure that VLMs use their evidence correctly.
CDoist18Ex.method: GeoEPS uses explicit spatial cues to combine local context, textual alignment, unfilled marking, and query-conditioned presentation. Without cues, it searches local evidence candidates and compares them under competing answer hypotheses.
CDoist18Ex.key_idea: Use spatial cues to tailor evidence presentation, or compare candidate regions under competing answer hypotheses when cues are unavailable.
CDoist18Ex.evidence: Evaluation on XLRS-Bench and RSHR-Bench uses Qwen3-VL-8B and tests transfer to other frozen general-purpose and remote-sensing-specific VLMs.
CDoist18Ex.claimed_gains: GeoEPS raises Qwen3-VL-8B average task accuracy from 48.8% to 61.0% on XLRS-Bench and from 41.3% to 53.7% on RSHR-Bench.

jlKRX61rho.one_liner: Sparse attention and MLP features support attribution graphs tracing board inputs to a chess transformer's move logits.
jlKRX61rho.problem: Strong chess-playing transformers lack a mechanistic account of how internal computations produce move decisions.
jlKRX61rho.method: The method adapts Low-Rank Sparse Attention and Transcoders to decompose LC0's policy network and extends tracing to its bilinear output head. A chess taxonomy and agentic interpretation pipeline propose feature meanings and rule-based tests for end-to-end attribution graphs.
jlKRX61rho.key_idea: Decompose attention and MLP computations into sparse features and trace their contributions through the bilinear policy head to candidate-move logits.
jlKRX61rho.evidence: LC0 case studies examine tactical computations, while quantitative metrics assess separation across moves, within-move branching, and layerwise concentration on source and target squares.

k3wVCbBexR.one_liner: Soft competition between clean-data routes and reverse-flow amplification explain divergent diffusion outputs from nearly identical states.
k3wVCbBexR.problem: Deterministic diffusion trajectories can yield different terminal outputs from almost identical intermediate states, requiring an account of local and downstream sensitivity.
k3wVCbBexR.method: The paper models Gaussian denoising as soft-minimum competition between routes and probes terminal sensitivity with matrix-free Cauchy–Green Jacobian–vector products. Tropical Route Control combines finite-horizon probes, trajectory-level conformal event control, and exact prefix allocation under a continuation budget.
k3wVCbBexR.key_idea: Model denoising as soft route competition, then probe how remaining flow transports and amplifies route contrasts into terminal displacement.
k3wVCbBexR.evidence: Theory proves O(σ²) transition widths and O(σ⁻²) peak sensitivity at regular two-route boundaries; experiments verify local sensitivity and finite-horizon perturbation effects.

3TkUHSFp3e.one_liner: Direction-aware segment diagnosis rebalances policy gradients and repairs severe learner–sampler mismatch in native four-bit reinforcement learning.
3TkUHSFp3e.problem: Low-precision discrepancies between learner and sampler can amplify policy updates and destabilize reinforcement learning.
3TkUHSFp3e.method: TRIAGE diagnoses mismatch by update direction and response segment, selectively rebalances policy-gradient contributions, and bounds repairs to residual severe mismatch. It changes the objective while retaining native NVFP4 W4A4 forward execution for both learner and sampler.
3TkUHSFp3e.key_idea: Diagnose amplifying mismatch at segment level, rebalance affected policy-gradient updates, and apply bounded repair to remaining severe discrepancies.
3TkUHSFp3e.evidence: Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B experiments evaluate stability over the tested training horizon and performance on five mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
3TkUHSFp3e.claimed_gains: Native NVFP4 with TRIAGE delivers up to 2.3× higher rollout throughput than BF16 while achieving full precision level performance across five mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

CAAyqk9d58.one_liner: Base-modality smoothing and sparse ridge compensation repair channels with the largest cross-modal quantization discrepancies.
CAAyqk9d58.problem: Shared channel-wise smoothing can favor one modality's activations and degrade others in multimodal decoders.
CAAyqk9d58.method: SPARCQuant chooses a base modality per linear module, ranks other channels by activation-weighted range discrepancy, and selects a repair budget through regularized reconstruction. Selected-channel ridge compensation corrects residual errors while all modalities share quantized weights.
CAAyqk9d58.key_idea: Smooth shared weights using a base modality, select discrepant channels with a learned budget, and fit ridge compensation only on those channels.
CAAyqk9d58.evidence: Experiments cover vision-language and omni-modal models, including Qwen3-VL-2B/8B, MiniCPM-o-2.6, and InteractiveOmni-4B under low-bit quantization.
CAAyqk9d58.claimed_gains: At W4A6, SPARCQuant raises the Qwen3-VL-2B/8B five-task average by 4.13/5.42 points and reduces speech-recognition word error rate by up to 63.3% on MiniCPM-o-2.6 and 56.4% on InteractiveOmni-4B.

SqiTOxOtoj.one_liner: Linear probes read question-conditioned evidence readiness from frozen video-language models to decide when to answer.
SqiTOxOtoj.problem: Streaming video systems need to know whether question-relevant evidence has arrived, but typically learn a separate answer trigger.
SqiTOxOtoj.method: The study probes frozen model representations using readiness labels derived from timestamped evidence and tests question-conditioned readouts under identical video inputs. Readiness Gating converts the internal signal into an answer-timing policy.
SqiTOxOtoj.key_idea: Decode question-conditioned evidence readiness from frozen hidden representations and use the readout to gate answer timing.
SqiTOxOtoj.evidence: Experiments span seven models and 26 configurations, including identical-input controls, unseen-footage benchmark families, question swaps, and analysis restricted to wrong answers.
SqiTOxOtoj.claimed_gains: Readiness Gating improves accuracy by up to +9.75 pp at matched video duration, while readiness probes achieve AUROC 0.733–0.905 across seven models.

DMvUT7cHZ3.one_liner: Scene memory and consolidated reasoning experience guide a fixed vision-language backbone's spatial tool choices.
DMvUT7cHZ3.problem: Spatial reasoners must learn when to observe directly, reconstruct, measure, or change reference frames rather than merely access geometric tools.
DMvUT7cHZ3.method: SpatialBrain combines queryable 3DFusionMemory, reusable spatial tool procedures, and task-conditioned experience about when to use them. It abstracts completed trajectories into process records and consolidates them between task blocks without transferring scene coordinates or reference answers.
DMvUT7cHZ3.key_idea: Consolidate completed trajectories into reusable process records that guide memory and tool selection while keeping current-scene evidence separate.
DMvUT7cHZ3.evidence: Experiments span five spatial-reasoning benchmarks, with component comparisons, experience-coverage curves, and traced resource decisions.
DMvUT7cHZ3.claimed_gains: SpatialBrain improves over direct answers from the same backbone on four of five spatial-reasoning benchmarks and ties on the fifth.

qYcKeQWI92.one_liner: Foveated masks allocate mixed-resolution tokens densely near a selected region and sparsely in the periphery for diffusion generation.
qYcKeQWI92.problem: High-resolution image and video generation becomes costly as token counts grow, even when users need fine detail mainly near a specified region.
qYcKeQWI92.method: The method uses a foveated-resolution mask to allocate tokens non-uniformly and generates images or videos directly at mixed resolution. It constructs mixed-resolution tokens from high-resolution data for post-training a foveated diffusion model.
qYcKeQWI92.key_idea: Allocate high token density near the specified foveal region and lower density in the periphery, then generate directly with mixed-resolution tokens.

p55ibboglu.one_liner: Random benchmark subsets underpin BestRand, which reduces rare large score-estimation errors in compressed evaluation.
p55ibboglu.problem: Random benchmark sampling usually estimates full scores accurately but occasionally produces large errors that make evaluation unstable.
p55ibboglu.method: BestRand uses the paper's analysis of subset estimation errors to reduce the high-error tail while retaining random sampling's low construction cost; the supplied abstract does not specify its selection procedure.
p55ibboglu.key_idea: BestRand builds on random subset sampling and an analytical approximation of its error distribution; the precise subset-selection mechanism is not stated.
p55ibboglu.evidence: The paper derives an analytical error-distribution approximation and evaluates BestRand on 70+ text, multimodal, and agent benchmarks, with an extension to VLA evaluation.
p55ibboglu.claimed_gains: BestRand reduces high-error risk by more than 50% on average.

e6raRFGlbN.one_liner: A reinforcement-learned policy selects image patches to generate or remask using the partial image and frozen generator features.
e6raRFGlbN.problem: Random or locally confidence-based generation orders do not fully exploit evolving context or revise earlier image predictions.
e6raRFGlbN.method: PONDER uses group-relative policy gradients to learn which missing positions to fill and which completed positions to remask. Its rewards measure constraints, human preference, or distribution quality, including FIDgrad's image-level estimate of FID change.
e6raRFGlbN.key_idea: A policy conditioned on partial images and generator features chooses both the next positions to generate and earlier positions to remask.
e6raRFGlbN.evidence: Experiments with frozen generators evaluate MAR-B on ImageNet and generation of hard visual Sudokus against uncertainty-based greedy ordering.
e6raRFGlbN.claimed_gains: Learned ordering reduces MAR-B ImageNet FID from 4.09 to 2.78 and raises hard visual Sudoku accuracy from 3.9% to 56.6%.

SpgtpzmEuE.one_liner: Rollout interface states fine-tune local neural PDE solvers within optimized Schwarz domain decomposition.
SpgtpzmEuE.problem: Local neural PDE solvers trained on reference states encounter their own prediction-induced states during domain decomposition, compromising global accuracy.
SpgtpzmEuE.method: ONCE combines optimized Schwarz methods with Trajectory-aligned Tuning, which collects intermediate interface states from pretrained rollouts and pairs them with reference subdomain solutions. It retains reference-state supervision without additional numerical PDE solves or backpropagation through iterations.
SpgtpzmEuE.key_idea: Fine-tune local solvers on rollout-generated interface states paired with reference subdomain solutions while preserving reference-state supervision.
SpgtpzmEuE.evidence: The theoretical analysis characterizes neural domain-decomposition fixed-point convergence and establishes interface error bounds accounting for trajectory supervision.

StFWeSQ9uK.one_liner: Co-designs one-pass source-linked agent memory summaries, selective raw-evidence lookup, and server-side KV cache reuse for language agents.
StFWeSQ9uK.problem: Pre-query agent memory summaries omit details needed by future queries, while elaborate memory maintenance incurs high model-call, re-encoding, and KV-state storage costs.
StFWeSQ9uK.method: FlashMEM constructs compact, source-linked memory in one pass on the agent side and answers queries by combining retrieved summaries with a small amount of original evidence from linked sources. On the server side, it reuses recurring context across construction calls and retains KV states only for compact memory rather than full interaction history.
StFWeSQ9uK.key_idea: Pairs one-pass source-linked memory summaries and selective original-evidence retrieval on the agent side with cross-call KV cache reuse for compact memory on the server.
StFWeSQ9uK.evidence: Evaluated across three long-running language-agent datasets measuring F1 accuracy, construction and inference costs, time to first token, and KV storage overhead.
StFWeSQ9uK.claimed_gains: Achieves relative F1 gains of 16.1%, 33.1%, and 41.5% across three datasets while reducing construction costs by 97.0%, inference costs by 92.2%, TTFT by 66.8%, KV recomputation selection overhead by 99.3%, and long-term PIC KV storage costs by 84.9–93.8%.

jMMFk7aJOT.one_liner: Corrects noisy multilabel classifier predictions post-hoc via shared-decoder variational manifold alignment with Student-t and Gaussian latent shifts.
jMMFk7aJOT.problem: Label noise induces geometric displacement in a trained multilabel classifier's latent space, degrading predictions when retraining the base classifier is impractical.
jMMFk7aJOT.method: Latent-Shift Noisy Prediction Correction (LSNPC) trains a post-hoc variational autoencoder that aligns clean and noisy label distributions on a shared latent manifold by decoding both through the same decoder without retraining the classifier. It models noise-induced displacement with a heavy-tailed Student-t transition and applies a Gaussian shift toward clean representations to close residual displacement.
jMMFk7aJOT.key_idea: Aligns clean and noisy multilabel predictions on a shared VAE manifold through one decoder coupled with a Student-t displacement transition and Gaussian residual shift.
jMMFk7aJOT.evidence: Supported by theoretical bounds on posterior approximation, linear KL divergence under Student-t shifts, and label-covariance reconstruction error, plus experiments on four synthetic-noise benchmarks and real-world datasets.

wlghf4i49O.one_liner: Preserves natural-language generation during semantic-ID retriever training via drift-adaptive on-policy forward-KL distillation on student-generated prefixes.
wlghf4i49O.problem: Fine-tuning pretrained language models solely to predict document semantic IDs distorts their natural-language distribution, impairing interactive systems that must also converse.
wlghf4i49O.method: SpeakGR combines supervised semantic-ID learning with on-policy distillation that minimizes forward KL divergence over the original text vocabulary against a frozen copy of the pretrained model on student-generated prefixes. Adaptive SpeakGR dynamically adjusts this regularization strength according to observed language drift.
wlghf4i49O.key_idea: Combines supervised semantic-ID training with drift-adaptive on-policy forward-KL distillation against a frozen reference language model over student-generated prefixes.
wlghf4i49O.evidence: Evaluated across three LLMs on MS MARCO and Natural Questions retrieval benchmarks, measuring language drift via forward KL on WikiText-2 against SFT-only training.
wlghf4i49O.claimed_gains: Compared with SFT-only, SpeakGR reduces WikiText-2 forward KL by 81.3–93.8% on MS MARCO and 81.2–85.2% on Natural Questions while retaining effective retrieval.

Fr70riwkRa.one_liner: Improves unposed feed-forward Gaussian splatting via 3D-reprojected patch graph attention and rendering-feedback camera pose refinement.
Fr70riwkRa.problem: Feed-forward novel view synthesis from unposed images suffers from cross-view inconsistent Gaussian predictions and camera estimation errors that cause ghosting and blurred details.
Fr70riwkRa.method: Keeping a pretrained visual geometry backbone frozen, HiFiNVS constructs a patch graph by reprojecting 3D points across images and propagates features along geometric correspondence edges via Reprojection-Grounded Graph Attention. A feed-forward camera refiner then updates predicted camera poses using rendering feedback from the initial Gaussian scene before rerunning reconstruction once.
Fr70riwkRa.key_idea: Propagates features across views along 3D-reprojected patch correspondence edges and updates predicted cameras in a feed-forward pass using initial Gaussian rendering feedback.
Fr70riwkRa.evidence: Instantiated with frozen DA3, π³, and VGGT visual geometry backbones and evaluated on unposed-view novel view synthesis benchmarks for camera accuracy and rendering quality.

liUWwWlga1.one_liner: Selects per-layer pipeline delays and tunes thresholds and membrane potentials to balance latency and accuracy in spiking neural networks.
liUWwWlga1.problem: Overlapping timestep execution across spiking neural network layers triggers irreversible early spikes on incomplete inputs, yet increasing per-layer waiting can degrade both latency and accuracy.
liUWwWlga1.method: The authors introduce Falcon, which uses Pipeline Delay Search (PDS) to choose each layer's delay by balancing task-level accuracy gains against added network latency. Selected delay schedules are then adapted through spike-based quantization-aware training and bounded tuning of firing thresholds and initial membrane potentials.
liUWwWlga1.key_idea: Searches layer-wise pipeline delays across timestep-overlapped spiking layers and adapts selected schedules via spike-based quantization-aware training plus bounded threshold and membrane-potential tuning.
liUWwWlga1.evidence: Supported by theoretical proof that small increases in per-layer waiting in timestep-pipelined spiking neural networks can simultaneously worsen latency and accuracy.

Ctd34VGBhx.one_liner: Routes visual patches into compact task-conditioned world tokens and jointly predicts future tokens and robot actions via flow matching.
Ctd34VGBhx.problem: Dense future-image prediction in World-Action Models incurs heavy inference overhead and compounds prediction errors through recursive decoding and re-encoding.
Ctd34VGBhx.method: MuxWAM introduces a multiplexer-inspired world constructor (MUX) that maps dense visual patches to K task-conditioned world tokens per view via task-indexed routing over shared experts and normalized global fusion. It jointly predicts future world tokens and robot actions using flow matching without decoding future images at inference.
Ctd34VGBhx.key_idea: Maps visual patches to fixed-size task-conditioned world tokens via task-indexed expert routing and global fusion, predicting future tokens and actions jointly with flow matching.
Ctd34VGBhx.evidence: Evaluated with two world tokens per view on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, Meta-World, and physical ALOHA robot manipulation tasks.
Ctd34VGBhx.claimed_gains: With two world tokens per view, achieves 98.8% mean success on LIBERO, 83.76% averaged equally over Meta-World's four difficulty groups, and 78.3% across three physical tasks under normal conditions.

umcWjzqwF4.one_liner: Modulates geometric priors in novel-view-synthesis attention using an oracle-supervised multi-axis reliability field inside a product of experts.
umcWjzqwF4.problem: Uniformly injecting geometric priors into strong novel-view-synthesis backbones under-utilizes clean priors while indiscriminate integration of mixed-quality priors cancels beneficial and harmful cues.
umcWjzqwF4.method: Reliability-Calibrated Geometric Attention (RCGA) predicts a multi-axis geometric reliability field supervised during training by a comparative oracle that measures the incremental utility of geometry beyond the backbone. A partition-preserving product-of-experts uses this predicted field to calibrate geometric evidence in joint attention for selective correspondence refinement.
umcWjzqwF4.key_idea: Predicts an oracle-supervised multi-axis geometric reliability field that calibrates explicit geometric priors in joint cross-view attention via a partition-preserving product of experts.
umcWjzqwF4.evidence: Supported by controlled analyses examining uniform and mixed-quality geometric prior integration in novel view synthesis.

ojnmlXUtnV.one_liner: Combines execution diagnostics, cross-engine numerical alignment, and native W4A4 GEMM kernels to stabilize NVFP4 LLM reinforcement learning.
ojnmlXUtnV.problem: Matching weights and numerical formats alone fails to prevent policy-evaluation discrepancies between separate training and sampling engines in native NVFP4 LLM reinforcement learning.
ojnmlXUtnV.method: miniTE provides execution diagnostics, cross-engine numerical alignment, and native 4-bit weight-and-activation (W4A4) GEMM kernels without altering the RL objective.
ojnmlXUtnV.key_idea: Align cross-engine numerical execution between sampling and training engines alongside native 4-bit weight-and-activation GEMM kernels without altering the RL objective.
ojnmlXUtnV.evidence: Evaluated via long-horizon RL training on Qwen3-30B-A3B and learner throughput benchmarks on a single NVIDIA B300 GPU node against BF16 and Transformer Engine NVFP4.
ojnmlXUtnV.claimed_gains: On a single NVIDIA B300 GPU node, the learner reaches 33,540 tokens/s, achieving 1.39x and 1.47x the complete-update throughput of BF16 and Transformer Engine NVFP4, respectively.

59p9nWktvx.one_liner: Quantifies convergence gains of block-preconditioned gradient descent over scalar-step gradient descent under block-heterogeneous smoothness.
59p9nWktvx.problem: Using a single global scalar learning rate slows gradient descent when smoothness and curvature vary substantially across parameter blocks.
59p9nWktvx.method: The authors compare block-preconditioned gradient descent with constant-step gradient descent under a shared blockwise quadratic upper bound and establish lower-bound examples showing linear dependence on the block smoothness ratio. They evaluate block scaling on nonconvex interacting-block objectives, softmax regression, and GPT-2 curvature diagnostics.
59p9nWktvx.key_idea: Rescale parameter-block updates by blockwise smoothness constants to remove the largest-to-smallest block curvature ratio from stationarity bounds.
59p9nWktvx.evidence: Supported by convergence upper bounds, explicit quadratic lower-bound constructions, nonconvex synthetic tests with inaccurate scales, softmax regression experiments, and GPT-2 block curvature measurements.
59p9nWktvx.claimed_gains: At the largest tested coefficient ratio, the best scalar step in a four-rate grid needs 46.64-167 times as many updates to reach the ordinary-gradient target, and in softmax regression, measured curvature scales cut test loss by 3.99% over shuffled assignments.

Hv5cgCpQ6r.one_liner: Unifies user recommendation and multimodal content generation in a single mixture-of-transformers backbone trained via a multi-stage alignment curriculum.
Hv5cgCpQ6r.problem: Cascaded pipelines compress user behavior into a lossy intermediate representation before conditioning a frozen generator, hiding raw user context during multimodal content synthesis.
Hv5cgCpQ6r.method: RIGC uses a single mixture-of-transformers backbone where user behavior remains in the shared attention context across item retrieval, text generation, and image synthesis. It trains on a large-scale industrial multimodal dataset using a multi-stage alignment curriculum.
Hv5cgCpQ6r.key_idea: Share persistent user context across recommendation, text generation, and image synthesis inside one mixture-of-transformers model trained with multi-stage curriculum alignment.
Hv5cgCpQ6r.evidence: Constructs an industrial multimodal dataset pairing user behavior with item content, while downstream experimental details are truncated in the abstract.

cA6zJCAZVg.one_liner: Stabilizes low-precision LLM reinforcement learning by selectively applying importance-sampling corrections to reliable mismatch tokens while leaving noisy tokens unweighted.
cA6zJCAZVg.problem: Aligning low-precision rollout and actor policies directly conflates genuine policy divergence with quantization noise, failing to guarantee improvement on the latent full-precision objective.
cA6zJCAZVg.method: The paper casts low-precision RL as a three-policy alignment problem involving noisy rollout, noisy actor, and inaccessible full-precision policies. Excess-Risk-guided Importance Sampling (ERIS) corrects high-reliability mismatch tokens while keeping identity weights on noise-dominated tokens.
cA6zJCAZVg.key_idea: Formulate three-policy alignment with the latent full-precision policy to apply importance-weight corrections on reliable mismatch tokens and identity weights elsewhere.
cA6zJCAZVg.evidence: Evaluated on FP8 reinforcement learning across multiple Qwen model scales and architectures, including mathematical reasoning on Qwen3-8B against standard FP8 and BF16.
cA6zJCAZVg.claimed_gains: ERIS improves the average mathematical reasoning score over standard FP8 by 14.29% on Qwen3-8B while matching BF16-level performance.

KBVj7CAdyj.one_liner: Evidence-interval scoring evaluates whether audio-visual models ground correct answers in both modalities.
KBVj7CAdyj.problem: Multiple-choice audio-visual benchmarks score answers without checking supporting evidence and can permit textual or unimodal shortcuts.
KBVj7CAdyj.method: EvaOmni contains expert-annotated audio and visual evidence, video-grounded distractors, and questions filtered by text-only, audio-only, and visual-only checks. Models return answers and evidence intervals, scored by Coverage Grounded and Bottleneck Grounded metrics.
KBVj7CAdyj.key_idea: Score answer correctness together with temporal coverage and bottlenecks in annotated audio-visual evidence.
KBVj7CAdyj.evidence: The benchmark comprises 420 videos and 1,200 question-answer pairs across 15 capabilities and 3 levels, with expert evidence annotations and modality-specific shortcut checks.

Qyz7rBWpVK.one_liner: Local surface expansion generates order-agnostic high-resolution meshes with bounded context and geometric validation.
Qyz7rBWpVK.problem: Global mesh sequence prediction depends on serialization order and requires increasingly long contexts as resolution grows.
Qyz7rBWpVK.method: MeshExpand iteratively selects an open boundary edge and predicts the opposite vertex from nearby faces, point samples, and a global shape prior. It represents generated faces as an unordered set and applies online geometric validation and resampling.
Qyz7rBWpVK.key_idea: Grow meshes through bounded-neighborhood boundary expansion over an unordered face set rather than global ordered sequence prediction.
Qyz7rBWpVK.evidence: Experiments test high-resolution generation, out-of-distribution scanned and generated shapes, and generation using constant-size local context.
Qyz7rBWpVK.claimed_gains: MeshExpand scales to meshes with up to 136K faces using about 2 GB of GPU memory.

rp3Do316Ll.one_liner: Shared-state mutation between validation and action exploits check-use races in tool-augmented agents.
rp3Do316Ll.problem: Agents verify shared state before acting, but latency between check and use lets adversaries replace verified values with unverified ones.
rp3Do316Ll.method: TEMPO formalizes check-use race attacks in which an adversary mutates shared state during the race window. It evaluates multiple adversary types and race primitives across victim models, workflows, and a production-grade LangGraph+SQLite stack.
rp3Do316Ll.key_idea: Mutate shared external state after agent verification but before tool use so actions rely on stale premises.
rp3Do316Ll.evidence: Experiments cover eight victim models, two adversary types, three race primitives, a payment approval workflow, and an out-of-process adversary on LangGraph+SQLite.
rp3Do316Ll.claimed_gains: TEMPO achieves 100% attack success against reconnaissance-equipped attackers, while a prompt defense reducing injection success from 91.7% to 12.5% leaves TEMPO unchanged and a version check blocks 98.7% on one victim but only 7.1% on another.

mJeDCIjFGG.one_liner: Trains floating-point weights in low-dimensional seeded subspaces for data-free iterative test-time bit-flip recovery.
mJeDCIjFGG.problem: Floating-point weights on edge devices suffer from random and adversarial bit flips, while prior recovery methods are slow and mishandle rounding and nonfinite values.
mJeDCIjFGG.method: LoDiSS learns weights in low-dimensional seeded subspaces, regenerates recovery constraints at test time via shared pseudorandom transforms, and iteratively reconstructs only suspected weights while handling rounding and nonfinite values.
mJeDCIjFGG.key_idea: Parameterizes weights in low-dimensional seeded subspaces so pseudorandom recovery constraints can be regenerated on-device to repair suspected corrupted weights.
mJeDCIjFGG.evidence: Evaluations across 20 classification settings under repeated random faults, adversarial attacks, and recovery-aware adaptive attacks.
mJeDCIjFGG.claimed_gains: Retains approximately 100% clean accuracy under repeated random faults across 20 settings, with mean training and recovery speedups of 2.11x and 17.59x over the baseline.

gVF8zyAWmC.one_liner: Splits image anchors into disjoint DCT-band slots and routes only the lowest-frequency slot to global attention in pixel-space Transformers.
gVF8zyAWmC.problem: Pixel-space generative Transformers scale quadratically with token count when using one token per patch to capture fine image detail.
gVF8zyAWmC.method: SpecSlot expands each spatial anchor into multiple slots assigned disjoint DCT coefficient bands; only the lowest-frequency slot enters global attention while all slots interact locally, plus a spatial residual head.
gVF8zyAWmC.key_idea: Assigns spatial anchor slots disjoint DCT spectral bands and restricts global attention to the lowest-frequency carrier slot while keeping pixel-space loss.
gVF8zyAWmC.evidence: Evaluations on ImageNet-256, ImageNet-512, and text-to-image DPG-Bench against JiT baselines.
gVF8zyAWmC.claimed_gains: Improves ImageNet-512 FID by 2.84 over a compute-matched JiT control (TL;DR), comes within 1.47 FID of JiT-B/16 at 34.5% lower forward cost, and surpasses JiT-B/8 on DPG-Bench by 1.06 at 40.6% lower cost.

B8j0TbtlhK.one_liner: Trains a regressor on completed molecular assays to route four frozen predictors for new scarce-label assays.
B8j0TbtlhK.problem: Selecting a small subset of frozen molecular predictors for a new assay with 16-64 labels via target-side subset search is unreliable.
B8j0TbtlhK.method: AssayRouter labels candidate predictors on completed ChEMBL-MT assays by their post-fit reduction in held-out discovery loss and trains a shared regressor to predict this utility from support-set behavior without source identities. On a new assay, one ranking selects four sources for convex combination.
B8j0TbtlhK.key_idea: Learns a source-agnostic utility regressor from post-fit loss reductions on completed assays to select four frozen predictors in one pass.
B8j0TbtlhK.evidence: Training on completed ChEMBL-MT assays and evaluation on 24 external regression assays across six frozen interface families, including permutation and leave-one-interface-out checks.
B8j0TbtlhK.claimed_gains: AssayRouter-C lowers strict four-call negative log-likelihood (NLL) by 0.0409 relative to Support-CV@4.

F8ErR7pznP.one_liner: Anneals expert chain-of-thought prefixes with selective trace rollback and harmonized GRPO/trust-region SFT optimization.
F8ErR7pznP.problem: Mix-policy RL methods either use static full-trace expert guidance that suppresses exploration or unverified prefixes that risk training collapse.
F8ErR7pznP.method: MOER injects an annealing expert CoT prefix for model completion, rolls back failed completions to the full expert trace, and optimizes on-policy tokens with GRPO and expert/completion tokens with trust-region SFT.
F8ErR7pznP.key_idea: Combines decaying expert CoT prefixes, selective rollback of failed completions to full expert traces, and a joint GRPO plus trust-region SFT loss.
F8ErR7pznP.evidence: Experiments across mathematical and general domain reasoning tasks, multiple model scales, and diverse base model categories.

PuqTTXjeEn.one_liner: Generates five structured semantic evidence units and pools hidden states at their boundaries to form multimodal retrieval embeddings.
PuqTTXjeEn.problem: MLLMs can generate useful evidence for retrieval, but how evidence organization interacts with embedding readout positions is poorly understood.
PuqTTXjeEn.method: EviAlign jointly trains an MLLM with generation and contrastive retrieval losses, organizing generated evidence into five semantic units and aggregating contextualized hidden states read at each unit boundary.
PuqTTXjeEn.key_idea: Co-designs structured five-unit semantic evidence generation with boundary-aligned hidden-state pooling for multimodal retrieval embeddings.
PuqTTXjeEn.evidence: Controlled 2x3 study of evidence organization vs. readout positions and evaluation across 12 MMEB retrieval tasks with 500K training pairs.
PuqTTXjeEn.claimed_gains: Boundary readout increases the consistent-organization advantage from 0.65 to 2.39 points (a 1.74-point co-design interaction), and EviAlign achieves 76.9 average Recall@1 across 12 MMEB tasks.

pKp1yVjm8D.one_liner: Characterizes hidden-basis dependence of post-hoc OOD activation clipping and introduces orthogonal- and affine-invariant Radial-ReAct and Maha-Radial.
pKp1yVjm8D.problem: Coordinate-wise post-hoc OOD detectors like ReAct, ASH, and DICE depend on the network's hidden basis rather than the classifier function alone.
pKp1yVjm8D.method: The authors classify detectors by reparameterization symmetries, characterize orthogonal-equivariant shaping classes, and propose training-free Radial-ReAct and Maha-Radial detectors with orthogonal and affine invariance guarantees.
pKp1yVjm8D.key_idea: Replaces coordinate-wise penultimate activation clipping with radial and Mahalanobis-radial shaping invariant to orthogonal or affine basis transformations.
pKp1yVjm8D.evidence: Tested on an ImageNet ResNet-50 across six standard OOD suites and 20 random bases plus adversarial basis optimization.
pKp1yVjm8D.claimed_gains: Across random bases, ReAct's AUROC swings by up to 15.8 points (23 points at d <= 16), and an adversarially optimized basis inverts it from 0.97 to 0.003.

SxUE2HOIa0.one_liner: Schedules agentic LLM calls by normalizing projected completion against a critical-path horizon for joint prefill-decode placement.
SxUE2HOIa0.problem: Meeting workflow SLOs in agentic LLM serving is difficult when branches emerge dynamically and prefill-decode disaggregation places calls on heterogeneous workers.
SxUE2HOIa0.method: HexAGenT maintains a critical-path horizon over revealed LLM calls, normalizes projected call completion by that horizon to prioritize queue order and worker pairs, and refines prefill costs with local and global KV-prefix reuse asynchronously.
SxUE2HOIa0.key_idea: Normalizes projected call completion by a dynamic critical-path horizon to jointly prioritize queues and prefill-decode worker pairs.
SxUE2HOIa0.evidence: Evaluated with two LLMs, four agentic workloads, three homogeneous and heterogeneous cluster settings, and an ablation study.
SxUE2HOIa0.claimed_gains: Reduces the SLO scaling factor required for 95% and 99% workflow attainment by up to 46.5% and 53.7%, respectively.

droihIsWyK.one_liner: Repairs optical chemical structure predictions via coordinate-preserving rendering and index-anchored executable graph edits before selective rejection.
droihIsWyK.problem: Optical chemical structure recognition errors propagate into databases, and selection-only rejection cannot produce additional correct structures beyond the base recognizer.
droihIsWyK.method: ViCoR uses coordinate-preserving rendering to align source images with predicted structures, maps localized visual discrepancies via index anchoring to executable graph edits without full regeneration, and trains a shared VLM progressively from verification to revision.
droihIsWyK.key_idea: Pairs coordinate-preserving rendering with index-anchored visual discrepancy mapping to apply executable graph edits before selective rejection.
droihIsWyK.evidence: Evaluated on two real-world optical chemical structure recognition benchmarks.
droihIsWyK.claimed_gains: Improves overall accuracy from 73.53% to 88.26% and from 61.83% to 84.32%, while achieving over 97% accepted accuracy at 85-89% coverage.

qjrIQXooV3.one_liner: Expresses peak LR and decay ratio via critical-batch-size normalization to extrapolate LLM schedules to 10x larger token budgets.
qjrIQXooV3.problem: Optimal peak learning rate and decay ratio in LLM pretraining vary with token budget and batch size, requiring expensive grid-search retuning at scale.
qjrIQXooV3.method: Using a functional scaling law with an admissibility constraint on peak LR, K-scaling normalizes batch size by a shared critical batch size Bc(D) to collapse peak LR and decay ratio onto budget-independent profiles. A four-parameter model fitted on small budgets extrapolates schedules across subcritical (pure decay) and supercritical (WSD) regimes.
qjrIQXooV3.key_idea: Normalizes batch size by a shared critical batch size Bc(D) to reveal a budget-independent K-scaling collapse that jointly predicts optimal peak LR and decay ratio.
qjrIQXooV3.evidence: Evaluated on dense and MoE models spanning 0.1B–1B parameters trained with MuonH.
qjrIQXooV3.claimed_gains: Extrapolates to token budgets up to 10x the largest fitting budget, yielding schedules with final losses close to grid-search optima without retuning.

iVkaaUhwjo.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM embodied teams under matched upfront versus online task revisions to isolate expansion loss and negotiation benefits.
iVkaaUhwjo.problem: Existing embodied multi-agent benchmarks lack matched upfront and online task-revision conditions, confounding final-task complexity with online adaptation losses.
iVkaaUhwjo.method: The authors build a 50-task benchmark for heterogeneous LLM embodied teams that synchronizes task and evaluator revisions during continuous execution under matched final requirements. They also probe explicit allocation dialogue and test dynamic experience-based negotiation-mode selection.
iVkaaUhwjo.key_idea: Pairs upfront and online task-revision conditions with matched final requirements to separate task-expansion loss from online-adaptation loss and measure when negotiation helps.
iVkaaUhwjo.evidence: Evaluated 14 models on 50 embodied tasks under the Never protocol, plus four models with allocation dialogue and two Dynamic negotiation configurations.
iVkaaUhwjo.claimed_gains: Across 14 models, 75.1% of success-rate loss from original to online-revised tasks is already present upfront, while online introduction adds a 5.36 percentage-point loss.

NQZY4sq8Vz.one_liner: Branches student rollouts at high-uncertainty, high-disagreement tokens and applies protocol-boundary repair during on-policy distillation.
NQZY4sq8Vz.problem: Single-trajectory on-policy distillation realizes only one continuation per decision, limiting teacher supervision coverage under a finite sampling budget.
NQZY4sq8Vz.method: BranchOPD selects decision points using student uncertainty and teacher-student disagreement, resamples continuations from shared prefixes under the student policy, and applies token-level teacher supervision on main and branched paths. It also adds protocol-boundary repair (PBR) to curb repetition and wasted tokens.
NQZY4sq8Vz.key_idea: Branches rollouts from shared prefixes at uncertain, high-disagreement decision points and applies token-level teacher supervision plus protocol-boundary repair.
NQZY4sq8Vz.evidence: Evaluated against Vanilla OPD and Multi-Rollout OPD (n=7) on mathematics benchmarks (avg@16) and agent tasks (ALFWorld, WebShop).
NQZY4sq8Vz.claimed_gains: Outperforms Vanilla OPD by 18.55 percentage points in mean math accuracy (avg@16) and 13.8 points in mean ALFWorld ID/OOD success; prefix reuse cuts student tokens by ~19% on ALFWorld and ~31% on WebShop.

oRlJWAfK0U.one_liner: Couples masked hypergraph generation with continuous hypergraph structural entropy optimization for end-to-end attributed hypergraph clustering.
oRlJWAfK0U.problem: Attributed hypergraph clustering methods decouple representation learning from grouping or rely on contrastive augmentations without guaranteeing cluster-separable embeddings.
oRlJWAfK0U.method: HSENet formulates hypergraph structural entropy (HSE) with edge-dependent vertex weights and a differentiable relaxation via the Lovász extension. It jointly trains a masked generative self-supervised module and an HSE-guided clustering assigner that optimizes a soft partitioning tree.
oRlJWAfK0U.key_idea: Optimizes a Lovász-relaxed hypergraph structural entropy soft partitioning tree jointly with masked generative vertex-topology reconstruction.
oRlJWAfK0U.evidence: Experiments across 8 benchmark datasets comparing HSENet against 10 competing methods.

rH8y1c0DDx.one_liner: Models intermediate state recoverability in multi-hop knowledge graph retrieval using a prefix-state value function and beam search.
rH8y1c0DDx.problem: Existing knowledge graph retrieval methods for LLMs focus on local expansion or complete-path ranking, leading to cascading errors from early mistakes and path explosion.
rH8y1c0DDx.method: Act-on-Graph (AoG) converts answer-reaching paths into step-wise state-action and prefix-state supervision to jointly train a local relation-entity policy and a prefix-state recoverability value function. At inference, uncertainty-aware beam search keeps plausible alternatives while pruning low-recoverability branches.
rH8y1c0DDx.key_idea: Jointly learns a local relation-entity policy and a prefix-state recoverability value function to guide uncertainty-aware beam search on knowledge graphs.
rH8y1c0DDx.evidence: Experiments on WebQSP and CWQ knowledge-graph question answering benchmarks.

9BACcaCC5E.one_liner: A learned render-free selector distills genetic subset search using coverage, redundancy, and sharpness features.
9BACcaCC5E.problem: Redundant or poorly chosen input frames raise novel-view-synthesis cost and can degrade reconstruction quality.
9BACcaCC5E.method: The selector scores target-view coverage, redundancy with selected views, and image sharpness without rendering or per-scene optimization. It distills an offline genetic algorithm that optimizes reconstruction quality on training scenes.
9BACcaCC5E.key_idea: Train a lightweight geometric and image-level scorer to imitate reconstruction-optimized genetic frame-subset search.
9BACcaCC5E.evidence: Experiments span six datasets and multiple input budgets, comparing geometric and reconstruction-aware selectors and measuring selection cost.

mXgWi29erk.one_liner: Turn-dependency DAGs propagate success credit backward while attenuated dense penalties preserve feedback on failures.
mXgWi29erk.problem: Final-trace masking misses early prerequisite turns on successes, while fully masking failures removes corrective feedback and can reduce exploration.
mXgWi29erk.method: ECHO-Graph propagates outcome credit backward through a DAG of turn dependencies induced by context reconstruction. It applies attenuated dense penalties to unsuccessful trajectories without additional rollouts, critics, or model evaluations.
mXgWi29erk.key_idea: Propagate success credit through reconstruction-induced turn dependencies and use attenuated dense negative feedback when failure provenance is unreliable.
mXgWi29erk.evidence: Experiments on BrowseComp-Plus and SWE-Bench Pro compare ECHO-Graph with ECHO, including difficult instances and context-horizon scaling.

ZIfKzboCqr.one_liner: Models patch-level timestamp and missingness morphology via localized Gaussian bases to route experts for irregular time-series forecasting.
ZIfKzboCqr.problem: Existing irregular multivariate time-series models treat timestamps and missingness masks as point-level auxiliary inputs rather than modeling patch-level observation morphology.
ZIfKzboCqr.method: MorITS encodes patch timestamps and missingness masks independently of observed values using localized Gaussian basis functions. A Morphology-Guided Expert Mixture routes patch semantic extraction based on morphology, and a Semantic-Morphology Patch Interaction module combines semantic similarity with inter-patch morphology relations.
ZIfKzboCqr.key_idea: Extracts value-independent patch observation morphology with localized Gaussian bases to condition expert routing and cross-patch interactions.
ZIfKzboCqr.evidence: Evaluated on five real-world irregular multivariate time-series forecasting datasets.

KGft5lIHeq.one_liner: Reframes self-attention as a dynamically parameterized MLP and replaces explicit attention with linear-time dynamic parameter prediction.
KGft5lIHeq.problem: Explicit token-wise attention computation in Vision Transformers incurs quadratic complexity in sequence length.
KGft5lIHeq.method: The authors mathematically reframe attention as an MLP whose weights are dynamically predicted as a compressed representation of global context. They design dynamic parameter prediction strategies integrated into standard vision network layers to achieve linear-complexity global sequence modeling without explicit attention.
KGft5lIHeq.key_idea: Replaces quadratic token-wise attention with linear-time dynamic prediction of MLP layer parameters encoding global visual context.
KGft5lIHeq.evidence: Empirical studies across vision models comparing dynamic parameter prediction strategies against explicit attention.

Z31x7BaU8f.one_liner: Distills offline 3D geometry and next-frame semantics into MLLM hidden-state prediction heads to eliminate runtime 3D encoders.
Z31x7BaU8f.problem: Geometry-aware Multimodal LLMs depend on external 3D encoders at inference, adding substantial latency and compute overhead.
Z31x7BaU8f.method: GeoThinker-F uses two-stage training: first, lightweight Latent Frame Prediction heads on a frozen MLLM backbone learn from an offline 3D geometry expert and next-frame semantic targets; second, the external expert is dropped and the model jointly optimizes a Spatial-Grounded Temporal Fusion module to integrate self-predicted priors.
Z31x7BaU8f.key_idea: Internalizes 3D geometry and future semantics via offline-distilled hidden-state prediction heads fused at inference without external 3D encoders.
Z31x7BaU8f.evidence: Evaluated across diverse spatial intelligence benchmarks measuring accuracy and inference speedup.
Z31x7BaU8f.claimed_gains: Eliminates runtime dependence on external 3D encoders and achieves up to a 3.6x speedup.

0K0KzH6eJc.one_liner: Trains a CrossCoder routing proxy over dense LLM layers to monitor pretraining generalization via virtual pathway reuse.
0K0KzH6eJc.problem: Tracking dense LLM generalization during pretraining via periodic downstream benchmark evaluations is expensive and obscures the memorization-to-generalization transition.
0K0KzH6eJc.method: The authors construct a virtual Mixture-of-Experts view of dense LLM layers by training a CrossCoder as a routing proxy to extract per-sample computation pathways across layers. They track generalization without downstream benchmarks by measuring inter-sample pathway edit distance (reusability) and within-pathway latent state diversity.
0K0KzH6eJc.key_idea: Uses a CrossCoder routing proxy to define virtual MoE pathways in dense LLMs and tracks their edit-distance reuse and internal state diversity.
0K0KzH6eJc.evidence: Evaluated across pretraining checkpoints of Pythia (160M-1B), OLMo-1B, and OLMo2-1B.

GJEYbLxmLP.one_liner: Schedules disaggregated asynchronous LLM RL across heterogeneous GPU clusters using MILP search and graph partitioning.
GJEYbLxmLP.problem: Deploying LLM RL across heterogeneous GPU clusters is difficult because rollout generation, reward computation, and policy updates have distinct compute, memory, and communication profiles.
GJEYbLxmLP.method: The authors build AReaL-Hex, a heterogeneity-aware asynchronous RL training system that enforces data staleness bounds via a two-phase scheduler. Phase one solves a mixed-integer linear program to pick per-stage parallelization and workload assignments, and phase two applies graph partitioning to allocate heterogeneous GPUs and interconnects.
GJEYbLxmLP.key_idea: Use MILP-based per-stage parallelization search followed by graph-partitioned GPU and interconnect allocation under staleness bounds.

aNWYntEk06.one_liner: Attaches a dense latent confidence probe to an embodied world model for active selection and weighted retraining.
aNWYntEk06.problem: Action-conditioned world models suffer localized spatiotemporal errors under new tasks and scenes, making uniform post-training data selection inefficient.
aNWYntEk06.method: ConfAL-WM attaches a lightweight confidence probe to EVAC UNet decoder features to predict dense latent confidence maps aggregated into task-, frame-, and patch-level scores. After warming up EVAC and the probe on a small target subset, it prescreens tasks to allocate sampling budgets and retrains with optional frame- or patch-weighted enhancement.
aNWYntEk06.key_idea: Predict dense latent confidence maps from UNet decoder features and aggregate them into task-, frame-, and patch-level scores for budget allocation and weighted retraining.
aNWYntEk06.evidence: Evaluated on RoboTwin2.0 against scalar reward, progress, and judge-based scoring baselines.

TIVEp1yJ7c.one_liner: Combines disjoint filter-level random-projection and attention-noise weights with Lipschitz calibration for multimodal adversarial defense.
TIVEp1yJ7c.problem: Multimodal fusion defenses struggle to achieve both provable l2 certification and empirical l-infinity robustness without high computational overhead.
TIVEp1yJ7c.method: HyWeCS places Orthogonally Retracted Random-Projection Weights (ORaW) and Stochastic Hybrid-Space Attention-Noise Weights (SHANW) at disjoint locations inside each convolutional filter, reusing terminal stochastic weights for reciprocal intermediate cross fusion. Shared Lipschitz calibration yields a uniform 2-Lipschitz score bound for formal certification.
TIVEp1yJ7c.key_idea: Partition each filter into orthogonally retracted random-projection weights and attention-noise weights, reused across cross-modal fusion under shared 2-Lipschitz calibration.
TIVEp1yJ7c.evidence: Evaluated across eight natural and medical multimodal benchmarks against competing defenses, including adaptive attacks, alongside formal 2-Lipschitz certification.
TIVEp1yJ7c.claimed_gains: Reduces parameters by up to ≈ 60.5% and GFLOPs by up to ≈ 91.1%, while improving certified and empirical robustness by up to ≈ 12.4% and ≈ 12.8% over the strongest competing defenses.

b7Wrxm30Tc.one_liner: Introduces Workflow-GYM, a benchmark testing GUI agents on end-to-end long-horizon professional software workflows.
b7Wrxm30Tc.problem: Existing GUI agent benchmarks emphasize short-horizon tasks on general-purpose software, leaving long-horizon professional software execution unmeasured.
b7Wrxm30Tc.method: The authors construct Workflow-GYM to evaluate computer-use GUI agents on realistic, multi-stage workflows across diverse professional domains and specialized software environments, and analyze recurring failure modes.
b7Wrxm30Tc.key_idea: Evaluate GUI agents end to end on multi-stage workflows inside specialized professional software environments and categorize long-horizon failure modes.
b7Wrxm30Tc.evidence: Evaluates current GUI agent models across diverse domains in Workflow-GYM and performs failure-mode analysis covering stage omission, error propagation, and objective drift.
b7Wrxm30Tc.claimed_gains: Even the strongest evaluated models achieve only slightly above 30% success rates on Workflow-GYM.

VcMmindtUS.one_liner: Generates clean one-step robot action trajectories directly in action space, calibrated by predicted DCT frequency structure.
VcMmindtUS.problem: Multi-step diffusion and flow policies incur high iterative inference latency for robotic manipulation, whereas velocity-parameterized one-step policies recover clean actions indirectly without explicit temporal structure guidance.
VcMmindtUS.method: SOAR predicts an observation-conditioned discrete cosine transform (DCT) representation of future actions and directly generates clean action trajectories in action space, correcting them via spectral discrepancy without extra backbone evaluations. During training, it derives MeanFlow velocity from the calibrated clean action for consistency learning alongside an endpoint objective.
VcMmindtUS.key_idea: Predicts observation-conditioned DCT spectral structure to directly calibrate one-step action-space trajectories and derive MeanFlow consistency velocity during training.

tsKk1H1DvG.one_liner: Studies cost-bounded video diffusion training by pairing DINOv2-distilled autoencoders, image-to-video adaptation, and decoupled guidance schedules.
tsKk1H1DvG.problem: Scaling video diffusion models leaves unclear which latent-space, conditioning, and inference-guidance design choices yield the best return under a fixed compute budget.
tsKk1H1DvG.method: Open-Sora 2.0 trains a video generation model on a $200k budget and systematically evaluates three design axes: DINOv2 latent distillation for high-compression autoencoders, image-to-video fine-tuning to adapt to new autoencoders and transfer low-resolution motion to high resolution, and decoupled classifier-free guidance with a time- and frame-dependent image-guidance schedule.
tsKk1H1DvG.key_idea: Combines DINOv2-distilled high-compression video autoencoders, I2V low-to-high-resolution motion transfer, and time- and frame-dependent decoupled image-text CFG under a fixed compute budget.
tsKk1H1DvG.evidence: Empirical study built around training Open-Sora 2.0 for $200k and comparing cost against MovieGen and Step-Video-T2V.
tsKk1H1DvG.claimed_gains: Trained for $200k, 5 to 10 times lower cost than comparable systems such as MovieGen and Step-Video-T2V.

5fhbahuTJs.one_liner: Benchmarks general-purpose agents on end-to-end deliverable tasks derived from market-validated AI startup workflows with fine-grained rubrics.
5fhbahuTJs.problem: Existing agent benchmarks rely on researcher-selected tasks, leaving uncertain whether agent progress transfers to workflows with demonstrated real-world user demand.
5fhbahuTJs.method: StartupBench studies AI startup products with demonstrated adoption and translates their real-world professional workflows into end-to-end deliverable-oriented tasks evaluated with fine-grained rubrics under a unified agent harness.
5fhbahuTJs.key_idea: Constructs deliverable-oriented end-to-end agent tasks and fine-grained evaluation rubrics directly from market-validated AI startup product workflows.
5fhbahuTJs.evidence: Evaluates representative models under a unified agent harness on StartupBench and analyzes failure modes including complex instruction following and domain-specific expertise.
5fhbahuTJs.claimed_gains: Even the strongest evaluated model successfully completes only approximately 30% of StartupBench.

Wjf3f9Qlz7.one_liner: Trains a local SLM via reinforcement learning to rewrite queries into privacy-preserving, task-equivalent forms for cloud LLM collaboration.
Wjf3f9Qlz7.problem: Anonymizing local queries sent to cloud LLMs either leaves semantic cues vulnerable to attribute inference attacks or strips task-essential details, and lacks a joint benchmark.
Wjf3f9Qlz7.method: The authors build a 2,200-query benchmark from four QA datasets pairing four-option attribute-inference privacy probes with verifiable downstream answers. They then introduce ReAnon, a reinforced anonymization framework that trains a local small language model to rewrite queries into task-equivalent representations that resist cloud attribute inference.
Wjf3f9Qlz7.key_idea: Train a local SLM with reinforcement learning to rewrite queries so cloud LLMs can solve the task while failing attribute-inference probes.
Wjf3f9Qlz7.evidence: Constructed and evaluated on a benchmark of 2,200 privacy-bearing queries drawn from four QA datasets with attribute-inference probes and verifiable answers.

kb7kmVTe9M.one_liner: Pretrains a shared SAR-to-EO translation prior on 3M+ heterogeneous pairs using a speckle-robust encoder for fast LoRA adaptation.
kb7kmVTe9M.problem: Existing SAR-to-EO image translation models train on single small datasets, yielding sensor-specific models that do not transfer across sensing conditions.
kb7kmVTe9M.method: GeoSET curates over 3 million SAR-EO pairs from more than 10 million SAR observations across diverse sensors and resolutions, then pretrains a conditional image generator paired with a speckle-robust SAR encoder. The shared parent model adapts to downstream datasets via full fine-tuning or LoRA.
kb7kmVTe9M.key_idea: Pretrain a speckle-robust SAR encoder and conditional generator on 3M+ multi-sensor SAR-EO pairs to serve as a LoRA-adaptable translation prior.
kb7kmVTe9M.evidence: Pretrained on over 3 million curated SAR-EO pairs and evaluated on six downstream benchmarks (names not stated) using FID and DISTS.
kb7kmVTe9M.claimed_gains: LoRA adaptation updates 0.60% of generator parameters and takes approximately one hour per dataset across six benchmarks (numeric FID/DISTS scores not stated).

hc0Dx7ByKd.one_liner: Trains an RL arbiter with hybrid attention to decide whether speculative decoding retains draft tokens or falls back to target tokens.
hc0Dx7ByKd.problem: Standard speculative decoding rejects any draft token disagreeing with the target, discarding cases where the draft continuation yields a more accurate final answer.
hc0Dx7ByKd.method: Collaborative Speculative Decoding (CoSpec) introduces an arbitrator that observes context, draft blocks, and target verification tokens through a hybrid attention mask to choose between draft and target tokens at mismatches. It is trained with reinforcement learning combining final-answer correctness and accepted-length shaping while keeping parallel target verification.
hc0Dx7ByKd.key_idea: Use an RL-trained arbiter with a hybrid attention mask over draft and target tokens to optimize final-answer accuracy and speedup rather than exact target matching.
hc0Dx7ByKd.evidence: Evaluated across two model families (including LLaMA-3.3-70B as target) on reasoning, code, and knowledge benchmarks including GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP.
hc0Dx7ByKd.claimed_gains: With LLaMA-3.3-70B as target, achieves a 3.96x mean speedup over target-only decoding and raises mean GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP score from 90.05 to 91.72.

sZEsXr5Ywb.one_liner: Recovers lost capabilities in self-evolving agents by scoring frozen historical responses with cross-iteration agreement and margin-gated selection.
sZEsXr5Ywb.problem: Self-evolving agents suffer historical capability fragmentation, losing earlier skills in later iterations while parameter-level signals cannot reliably separate beneficial from harmful updates.
sZEsXr5Ywb.method: CapDyn-Match selects among frozen historical checkpoint responses without modifying weights. It scores candidates using query-response representations and cross-iteration agreement, then applies a conservative margin gate with a training-derived fallback to prevent harmful switches under weak evidence.
sZEsXr5Ywb.key_idea: Score frozen responses across self-evolution checkpoints via query-response representations and cross-iteration agreement, switching from the latest model only past a margin gate.
sZEsXr5Ywb.evidence: Evaluated across 14 math, general reasoning, and code benchmarks on three-iteration Qwen3-4B and six-iteration Qwen3-1.7B self-evolution trajectories.
sZEsXr5Ywb.claimed_gains: Improves question-micro accuracy over the latest iteration by 3.13 and 3.05 points on two three-iteration Qwen3-4B trajectories.

utPIU99k82.one_liner: Generates fashion videos by synthesizing low-frequency motion while propagating high-frequency reference garment details along learned spatial correspondences.
utPIU99k82.problem: Regenerating high-frequency logos and fabric textures frame by frame in fashion video diffusion causes progressive visual drift under pose changes and cloth deformation.
utPIU99k82.method: W-DiT disentangles low-frequency structure from high-frequency reference details via a VAE-bypassing pathway, aligns low-frequency reference and target features to compute soft spatial correspondences, and samples high-frequency details from a fixed reference bank into each frame. The authors also curate FashionVideo from authorized Xiaohongshu images.
utPIU99k82.key_idea: Bypass VAE compression for high-frequency reference garment details and warp them into target video frames using soft correspondences matched on low-frequency structure.
utPIU99k82.evidence: Curated the FashionVideo dataset (~10,000 synthesized fashion videos and 30,000 additional items from Xiaohongshu images); quantitative evaluation metrics not stated in abstract.

Ygjxq4MJfi.one_liner: Adapts frozen flow-matching policies to spatial shifts via warm-started denoising, velocity-density gating, and outcome-fitted action offsets.
Ygjxq4MJfi.problem: Pretrained flow-matching policies fail under fixed spatial layout shifts at deployment when neither demonstrations nor weight updates are available.
Ygjxq4MJfi.method: WDRS exploits a policy's own recorded successful rollout in the shifted layout through three sampler-level interventions: warm-started denoising from the stored success under current observations, a velocity-field density gate that returns control to the base policy when chunks diverge, and an action-space residual offset fitted from terminal outcomes.
Ygjxq4MJfi.key_idea: Inject a stored successful trajectory into a frozen flow-matching sampler via warm-started denoising, velocity-density gating, and terminal-outcome action residual search.
Ygjxq4MJfi.evidence: Empirically validated on LIBERO across three spatial jitter scales.
Ygjxq4MJfi.claimed_gains: Raises single-draw success on LIBERO from 0.247 to 0.720 at the smallest of three jitter scales.

Z1xFlHFJkS.one_liner: Improves on-policy agent distillation from frozen teachers by indexing teacher executions in a state graph and adding hindsight context.
Z1xFlHFJkS.problem: In multi-turn on-policy distillation, compounding student errors push trajectories outside an off-the-shelf teacher's effective supervision range.
Z1xFlHFJkS.method: Graph-Conditioned On-Policy Agent Distillation (GC-OPD) indexes repeated teacher rollouts (both successes and failures) in a graph by shared environment states. After each student episode, it retrieves current-state references or historical alternatives and combines them with student hindsight to enrich the frozen teacher's context when scoring student thought-action tokens.
Z1xFlHFJkS.key_idea: Enrich a frozen teacher's scoring context with state-graph-retrieved teacher execution traces and student hindsight without optimizing the teacher.
Z1xFlHFJkS.evidence: Evaluated on ScienceWorld (4B student), ALFWorld Unseen, and WebShop against vanilla OPD and GRPO-trained teacher OPD baselines.
Z1xFlHFJkS.claimed_gains: Improves mean success over vanilla OPD from 24.70% to 48.78% on ScienceWorld (4B student, vs. 46.66% strongest GRPO-teacher baseline), from 53.36% to 85.26% on ALFWorld Unseen, and from 29.10% to 37.65% on WebShop.

HMr4eJ5C6d.one_liner: Distills EEG foundation models into compact students via input-conditioned layer routing and magnitude-phase spectral alignment.
HMr4eJ5C6d.problem: EEG foundation models incur high inference cost, while distilling only a fixed final teacher layer misses intermediate-layer task information and introduces spectral distortion.
HMr4eJ5C6d.method: DLink uses a training-only input-conditioned router to aggregate representations across intermediate teacher layers and aligns magnitude and phase spectra between teacher and student. A project-then-compress student internalizes the routed knowledge so both teacher and router are discarded at inference.
HMr4eJ5C6d.key_idea: Aggregate intermediate EEG foundation-model layers via an input-conditioned training router and align magnitude and phase spectra into a project-then-compress student.
HMr4eJ5C6d.evidence: Evaluated across six EEG benchmarks (names not stated) with ablation analyses of layer aggregation and spectral distillation.

XAUmrZWTGW.one_liner: Predicts antimicrobial peptide MIC by fusing peptide-LM sequence features with orientation-similarity physics graphs under imbalanced multitask regression.
XAUmrZWTGW.problem: Single-modality antimicrobial peptide predictors fail to capture spatial membrane-disruption mechanisms and suffer from extreme label skewness in bioactivity data.
XAUmrZWTGW.method: GOA-PGN combines a peptide-tuned language model with partial convolutions in one branch and coordinate-free topological graphs built from side-chain orientation cosine similarities in a parallel branch, fused via attention. It trains with deep imbalanced regression using a dynamically weighted multitask loss over MIC and auxiliary physicochemical properties.
XAUmrZWTGW.key_idea: Fuse peptide-LM sequence motifs with coordinate-free side-chain orientation-similarity graphs via attention and train under dynamically weighted deep imbalanced multitask regression.

WmMI9xznOl.one_liner: Repairs video VLM spatial reasoning without training using a library of typed geometric operators and evidence-checking spatial skills.
WmMI9xznOl.problem: Aggregate spatial-reasoning scores hide underlying VLM failure modes in perception, missing context, measurement choice, and reference-frame or pose tracking.
WmMI9xznOl.method: After diagnosing four recurring error sources by comparing predicted and ground-truth spatial contexts under a shared coordinate contract, the authors build CROSS, a training-free library of typed geometric operators and evidence-checking spatial skills. CROSS provides verified context to non-coding VLMs or callable tools to a SpatialClaw agent.
WmMI9xznOl.key_idea: Supply VLMs and agents with training-free typed geometric operators and evidence-checking spatial skills enforcing explicit coordinate and reference-frame conventions.
WmMI9xznOl.evidence: Evaluated across five video spatial reasoning benchmarks including ReVSI and DSI-Bench for non-coding VLMs and the SpatialClaw agent.
WmMI9xznOl.claimed_gains: Raises average score from 55.9% to 60.2% on ReVSI and improves SpatialClaw from 62.8% to 66.3% on DSI-Bench.

sz9ToxrohZ.one_liner: Shares low-rank input bases across compatible Key heads in SVD-compressed transformers to allocate more rank to fragile Query/Value projections.
sz9ToxrohZ.problem: Independent SVD compression of Q, K, and V projections ignores cross-head subspace redundancy and the higher rank-reduction fragility of Value versus Key.
sz9ToxrohZ.method: ShareSVD adaptively groups geometrically compatible Key heads and shares a single low-dimensional input basis per group while keeping head-specific output factors. The parameter budget saved on Key factorization is reallocated to retain more low-rank directions in the more sensitive Query and Value projections.
sz9ToxrohZ.key_idea: Group compatible Key heads to share a low-rank input basis and reallocate saved SVD parameter budget to more fragile Query and Value projections.
sz9ToxrohZ.evidence: Evaluated across three VLMs on two benchmarks (names not stated) and on dense and MoE Qwen3 language models.
sz9ToxrohZ.claimed_gains: At a 0.3 retained QKV ratio, improves average accuracy by 8.57% over the competitive baseline across three VLMs and two benchmarks while reducing low-rank KV-cache memory by 14.7%.

Sl3CAwNqGQ.one_liner: Decouples multiobjective Bayesian optimization evaluations under uniform costs using a multitask GP and total-correlation subset selection.
Sl3CAwNqGQ.problem: Standard multiobjective Bayesian optimization uses independent GPs and evaluates all objectives and constraints together, ignoring cross-task correlations that allow cheaper decoupled evaluations.
Sl3CAwNqGQ.method: The authors model all objectives and constraints jointly with a multitask Gaussian process and introduce a total-correlation metric to select an optimal subset of objectives and constraints to evaluate at each round, even under uniform evaluation costs. They prove asymptotic consistency and expected posterior entropy reduction maximization under mild conditions.
Sl3CAwNqGQ.key_idea: Jointly model objectives and constraints with a multitask GP and select per-round evaluation subsets using a total-correlation criterion maximizing unevaluated-task entropy reduction.
Sl3CAwNqGQ.evidence: Theoretical consistency and entropy-reduction proofs plus empirical comparison against coupled and decoupled MOBO baselines (benchmark names not stated).

0Ue24iW30R.one_liner: Conditions security LLMs on entity interaction graphs via Topology-Injected Masked Fine-Tuning with continuous topological tokens.
0Ue24iW30R.problem: LLMs reasoning over temporal security event sequences cannot directly incorporate entity interaction topology, missing structural cues for anomaly detection.
0Ue24iW30R.method: SecBFF uses Topology-Injected Masked Fine-Tuning to condition an LLM's temporal reasoning on continuous topological tokens without modifying the vocabulary. This post-training strategy works even when topological information is available for only a small fraction of the data.
0Ue24iW30R.key_idea: Post-train security LLMs via masked fine-tuning conditioned on continuous topological tokens without altering the token vocabulary.
