0Ue24iW30R.evidence: Evaluated on three real-world security tasks spanning Cyber-Security, Blockchain, and Access Violation in real-time and full-sequence classification.

Ht1Ctcfs3s.one_liner: Evaluates KV-cache compression separately on utility, token coverage, and exact source reproduction using FACT-KV and unit-first retention.
Ht1Ctcfs3s.problem: Answer F1 scores hide severe failures of KV-cache compression policies to retain intact evidence units needed to reproduce source text on request.
Ht1Ctcfs3s.method: FACT-KV aligns declared source spans, original KV positions, and output tests under matched budgets and schedules, branching answering and reproduction from one base cache. Comparing Unit-first retention against ChunkKV20 and SnapKV shows that utility, retained token quantity, and exact unit residency rank KV policies differently.
Ht1Ctcfs3s.key_idea: Evaluate KV-cache policies on branched answer and source-reproduction continuations from one base cache and retain intact evidence units via unit-first selection.
Ht1Ctcfs3s.evidence: Evaluated on 600 held-out Mistral/HotpotQA examples and a preregistered test on 300 Llama-3.1-8B sources against ChunkKV20 and SnapKV at 64 MiB and 32 MiB budgets.
Ht1Ctcfs3s.claimed_gains: At 64 MiB on Mistral/HotpotQA, Unit-first raises supporting-sentence reproduction from 40.17% to 53.50% (+13.33 percentage points, 95% CI [9.83, 16.83]) over ChunkKV20 and +23.00 points over SnapKV (F1 +0.38 [-1.52, 2.26]), and gains 11.67 points [7.33, 16.00] on Llama-3.1-8B; at 32 MiB over SnapKV it loses 3.52 F1 points.

lHA3QJHvYQ.one_liner: Breaks the 3-approximation barrier for Euclidean fair k-center via generalized exact matching for fixed m and deterministic maximum matching for m=2.
lHA3QJHvYQ.problem: Known approximation algorithms for fair k-center clustering hit a factor-3 barrier in general metrics, leaving tighter Euclidean guarantees open.
lHA3QJHvYQ.method: The authors reduce Euclidean fair k-center with fixed demographic groups m to a generalized exact matching problem on an auxiliary graph, giving a randomized (1 + sqrt(3))-approximation. For m=2, they exploit Euclidean geometry to replace exact matching with maximum matching, yielding a faster deterministic algorithm with the same ratio.
lHA3QJHvYQ.key_idea: Reduce Euclidean fair k-center to generalized exact matching on a geometric auxiliary graph (and maximum matching for two groups) to break the factor-3 barrier.
lHA3QJHvYQ.evidence: Theoretical approximation proofs complemented by experiments on five real-world datasets and one synthetic dataset with known optimal solutions.
lHA3QJHvYQ.claimed_gains: Achieves a 1 + sqrt(3) ≈ 2.732 approximation ratio for Euclidean fair k-center (randomized for fixed m, deterministic for m=2), strictly below the factor-3 barrier for general metrics.

5LZx8KcgV2.one_liner: Reverse-engineers Internet videos with predefined priors into multi-turn clips to benchmark interactive omni-modal video assistants.
5LZx8KcgV2.problem: Static offline datasets cannot evaluate interactive omni-modal video assistants because unpredictable model responses dynamically alter subsequent user actions and diverge across valid interaction paths.
5LZx8KcgV2.method: The authors build OmniAssistBench by reverse-engineering Internet videos into deduced user goals and multi-turn clips, requiring over 1,000 expert person-hours. Models receive predefined priors derived from the source video so they must guide users along the exact same routes.
5LZx8KcgV2.key_idea: Constrains diverging interaction paths by supplying source-video priors to models evaluated on multi-turn clips segmented from reverse-engineered Internet videos.
5LZx8KcgV2.evidence: Evaluates proprietary Gemini-3-Pro and open-source Qwen3-Omni-Instruct on the constructed OmniAssistBench multi-turn interaction dataset.
5LZx8KcgV2.claimed_gains: Gemini-3-Pro scores 66.4 out of 100 and Qwen3-Omni-Instruct scores 51.2 out of 100.

gUzvHlL3HA.one_liner: Operationalizes Belief-Desire-Intention behavioral constraints across 360 scenarios to diagnose mental-state consistency in video generators.
gUzvHlL3HA.problem: Visually realistic video generators still produce character actions that contradict the information available to characters or the goals they pursue.
gUzvHlL3HA.method: Mind-VBench translates Theory of Mind evaluation into observable behavioral constraints structured around the Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) framework. The benchmark comprises 360 instances organized into three BDI components, six diagnostic dimensions, and twelve tasks.
gUzvHlL3HA.key_idea: Evaluates video generators against observable Belief-Desire-Intention behavioral constraints across 360 structured diagnostic instances.
gUzvHlL3HA.evidence: Evaluates representative video generation models under text-to-video and image-to-video settings on Mind-VBench.

6ROQ7XRKeV.one_liner: Alternates sensitivity-weighted mean aggregation and nearest-representative partitioning in key-projected space to reduce ViT tokens.
6ROQ7XRKeV.problem: Existing Vision Transformer token reduction methods rely on ad-hoc heuristics or task-specific auxiliary reducer modules rather than a unified optimization objective.
6ROQ7XRKeV.method: MUTE formulates token reduction as minimizing a sensitivity-weighted clustering distortion objective in key-projected space motivated by a first-order Taylor expansion of the next block. It alternates two analytic coordinate updates—weighted-mean aggregation and nearest-representative partitioning—that monotonically descend the objective and derive bipartite merging's size bias.
6ROQ7XRKeV.key_idea: Alternates analytic weighted-mean aggregation and nearest-representative partitioning to monotonically minimize sensitivity-weighted clustering distortion in key-projected space.
6ROQ7XRKeV.evidence: Evaluated under a unified training-free protocol across supervised and self-supervised backbones on classification, dense prediction, fine-grained classification, and zero-shot domain transfer.

dZbefFmJ4Q.one_liner: Expands predicted trajectories into candidates, self-verifies them on reconstructed scenes, and adapts planners via temporally consistent BEV entropy.
dZbefFmJ4Q.problem: Existing test-time adaptation methods for end-to-end driving planners only update a score decoder over fixed trajectories and execute corrupted trajectories without refinement or verification.
dZbefFmJ4Q.method: SimTTA applies Geometric Trajectory Refinement (GTR) to expand predicted trajectories in output space, then uses Simulation-based Self-Verification (SSV) on a scene reconstructed from the model's own perception outputs to pick the highest-scoring candidate without labels. It adapts the planner using Temporally-Verified Entropy (TVE) loss restricted to BEV regions whose predicted classes stay consistent across consecutive samples.
dZbefFmJ4Q.key_idea: Refines and selects trajectories via simulation on self-reconstructed scenes while minimizing entropy only on temporally consistent BEV regions.
dZbefFmJ4Q.evidence: Evaluated on end-to-end trajectory planning across eight corruption types.

KyLOpCobwc.one_liner: Coordinates a unified model's understanding and generation roles via role-specific supervision and reciprocal feedback gates for image editing.
KyLOpCobwc.problem: In complex image editing, a failed edit does not distinguish whether task interpretation or visual execution failed, and external prompt enhancers add separate modules.
KyLOpCobwc.method: DuplexBridge uses a unified model's own understanding branch to build a source-grounded bridge specifying targets, final-state changes, and preservation constraints for its generator. Understanding is supervised on request fidelity without seeing the output image, generation is supervised on executing the received condition, and reciprocal trust checks selectively admit global task feedback; the authors also introduce the 1,200-task CE-Bench.
KyLOpCobwc.key_idea: Separates understanding and generation supervision with a source-grounded prompt bridge and reciprocal trust gates inside a single unified model.
KyLOpCobwc.evidence: Evaluated across three model configurations and a Wan-image initialization on CE-Bench (1,200 tasks), KRIS-Bench, RISEBench, ImgEdit, and GEdit-Bench.
KyLOpCobwc.claimed_gains: Improves complete compliance over direct editors by 21.75–25.75 percentage points across three configurations, and reaches 77.08% compliance from Wan-image initialization versus 70.92% without gates and 75.00% with original-task generation supervision.

DGyripOkZb.one_liner: Pretrains a geometry-aware RGB-depth panoramic prior with equirectangular boundary handling and transfers it to unified RGB-only in-context tasks.
DGyripOkZb.problem: Horizontal wrap-around and latitude-dependent distortion in equirectangular projections make panoramic scene completion and editing difficult.
DGyripOkZb.method: Canvas360 is a two-stage framework that first learns a geometry-aware panoramic prior via parallel RGB-depth pretraining with pseudo-depth supervision, modality-specific representations, and panorama-aware boundary handling, then transfers it to an RGB-only generator for style transfer, inpainting, outpainting, and editing. The authors also construct Canvas360Dataset with annotated RGB-depth panoramas and context-target pairs.
DGyripOkZb.key_idea: Transfers a parallel RGB-depth panoramic prior trained with pseudo-depth supervision and boundary handling into a unified RGB-only in-context generator.
DGyripOkZb.evidence: Evaluated on text-to-panorama generation, completion, and editing tasks using Canvas360Dataset.
DGyripOkZb.claimed_gains: Reduces panorama-specific distributional distance by 49.4% relative to the strongest baseline on text-to-panorama generation.

T4P9MuyaCo.one_liner: Combines an adaptive shot-reference policy, persistent story memory, and evaluation-driven hierarchical repair for multi-shot story video generation.
T4P9MuyaCo.problem: Existing multi-shot story video workflows struggle to localize whether errors stem from story planning, reference construction, or video generation, causing costly fixed-stage retries that disrupt valid content.
T4P9MuyaCo.method: ReelOnce is an agentic framework that selects shot-specific reference formats, separates depicted reference states from target transitions, maintains persistent story memory, and uses evaluation findings to choose the smallest necessary repair scope. The authors also propose Reconstructed Story Semantic Alignment (RSSA) to measure story consistency by reconstructing observable events from generated videos.
T4P9MuyaCo.key_idea: Uses an adaptive per-shot reference policy, persistent story memory, and evaluation-guided minimal-scope hierarchical refinement.
T4P9MuyaCo.evidence: Evaluated on Pixar-style videos generated from 20 diverse stories using RSSA and VBench quality dimensions.

p57m5L0SaL.one_liner: Injects one unannounced methodology pitfall per medical AI workspace across nine harnesses to test proactive error detection by research agents.
p57m5L0SaL.problem: Autonomous research agents can introduce methodological flaws that inflate medical AI results, and it is unclear whether agents proactively detect such pitfalls during workflows.
p57m5L0SaL.method: MAP-Eval comprises 189 medical-AI workspaces, each containing one unannounced pitfall from a 33-type taxonomy. Each pitfall is held fixed across nine evaluation harnesses spanning single-turn static review, a tool-using ReAct loop, and review states captured from three autonomous-research frameworks.
p57m5L0SaL.key_idea: Tests unannounced methodological pitfalls held fixed across static review, tool-using ReAct loops, and autonomous-research framework checkpoints.
p57m5L0SaL.evidence: Evaluates ten frontier models across 189 medical-AI workspaces and nine harnesses.
p57m5L0SaL.claimed_gains: Across ten frontier models, static review reaches 66–70% mean identification rate, six framework states reach 41–50%, a post-data-preparation checkpoint holds every model to 21–34%, and tool access shifts performance from -37 to +26 points.

UcGYa2HG06.one_liner: Decouples event retention from per-pass compute via broad candidate pools, bounded complementary views, and confidence-based early stopping.
UcGYa2HG06.problem: One-shot fixed-size random sampling in event-based action recognition couples retention to per-pass compute, discarding evidence in dense recordings and padding or duplicating events in short ones.
UcGYa2HG06.method: EventVista retains a broader recording-wide authentic event candidate pool while keeping short recordings' natural cardinality, constructs bounded temporally complementary runtime views, and sequentially aggregates predictions from a shared network until confidence and stability trigger early stopping.
UcGYa2HG06.key_idea: Retains a broad authentic event pool, observes bounded temporally complementary views at native cardinality, and halts sequential aggregation upon prediction stability.
UcGYa2HG06.evidence: Evaluated on event-based action recognition benchmarks (specific dataset names not stated in the excerpt).
UcGYa2HG06.claimed_gains: Achieves Top-1 accuracy of 70.40% (additional numbers truncated in abstract).

a87iGur9hx.one_liner: Introduces collaborative evidence collection, consistency verification, and a reviewed vulnerability model into multi-agent vulnerability repair.
a87iGur9hx.problem: Repository-level automated vulnerability repair agents lack mechanisms to ensure that intermediate evidence gathered during repair is reliable enough for accurate understanding and patching.
a87iGur9hx.method: EviRepair is a multi-agent framework that adds an evidence-review stage where agents collaboratively collect vulnerability evidence, verify its consistency, and construct a reviewed vulnerability model to guide patch synthesis and validation.
a87iGur9hx.key_idea: Verifies consistency of collaboratively collected evidence to build a reviewed vulnerability model before patch synthesis and validation.
a87iGur9hx.evidence: Evaluated on PatchEval and SecBench across multiple agent frameworks and LLMs.
a87iGur9hx.claimed_gains: Achieves average resolved-rate improvements of 8.04% on PatchEval and 17.27% on SecBench over agent-based baselines.

gqbvspcc3R.one_liner: Aggregates 2D MRI slice features into a 3D latent representation via PSF-aware weighting and decodes anisotropic 3D Gaussians feed-forward.
gqbvspcc3R.problem: Existing learning-based slice-to-volume MRI reconstruction methods assemble an intermediate intensity volume before refinement, underutilizing multi-view slice features and hallucinating missing structures in sparse regions.
gqbvspcc3R.method: GaLA-SVR is a feed-forward 3D Gaussian framework that bypasses intermediate volume reconstruction by combining a dense patch-wise correspondence motion estimator with Point Spread Function (PSF)-aware feature aggregation from 2D slices into a 3D latent representation, decoded into anisotropic 3D Gaussians for volumetric rendering.
gqbvspcc3R.key_idea: Aggregates motion-aligned 2D slice features with Point Spread Function weighting into a 3D latent representation decoded directly into anisotropic 3D Gaussians.

oln5zvKDYO.one_liner: Recovers linear latent causal DAGs and sparse loadings from unknown-target instruments via IV total-effect clustering and reverse-topological peeling.
oln5zvKDYO.problem: Identifying latent causal variables and their DAG from high-dimensional observations is difficult when instrument targets are unknown and observed variables cross-load without pure measurements.
oln5zvKDYO.method: The authors prove necessary-and-sufficient conditions for population recovery of linear latent DAGs using exogenous instruments and introduce IV-CRL-Peel, which clusters proportional IV total effects to identify the latent subspace and recovers the DAG and sparse loading matrix via reverse-topological trimmed-regression residual peeling.
oln5zvKDYO.key_idea: Clusters proportional instrumental-variable total effects and peels descendant propagation in reverse topological order via trimmed regression.
oln5zvKDYO.evidence: Supported by population identifiability theory, synthetic graph recovery simulations against observational and IV baselines, and a masked OneK1K cis-eQTL illustration.
oln5zvKDYO.claimed_gains: Recovers every simulated graph under population IV total effects and exactly recovers cis-eQTL groups and the empirical latent DAG on masked OneK1K.

pFPDQOn7B8.one_liner: Maps data samples to learnable-boundary latent zones decoded in one step using only a reconstruction loss.
pFPDQOn7B8.problem: Existing generative paradigms trade off one-step sampling, training stability, flexible latent spaces, native inversion, likelihood estimation, and unconstrained architectures.
pFPDQOn7B8.method: Generative Latent Zoning Networks (G-LZNs) map each training sample to a latent zone with learnable boundaries and decode latents within that zone back to the sample using only a reconstruction loss. This enables one-step generation, native inversion, likelihood estimation, and training-free editing tasks such as attribute editing, super-resolution, and inpainting.
pFPDQOn7B8.key_idea: Assigns each sample a learnable-boundary latent zone and trains an unconstrained decoder to reconstruct samples from zone latents in one step.
pFPDQOn7B8.evidence: Evaluated on generative modeling and editing tasks (keywords note ImageNet and CIFAR-10; abstract truncated before quantitative results).
